# Fortis for agents

<!-- covers: LR 0 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [the Fortis guide](../guide/README.md). Source of truth: the
[Language Reference](../Fortis_Language_Reference.md) (LR).*

Fortis is a statically checked, compiled, library-first language built so that code written mostly by agents can
be reviewed and trusted by people: every ownership operation, mutation permission, failure disposition, effect
claim and observation point is written in the source (LR 1). This mode states the rules densely, by rule ID, with
the records the tools print and the corrections that fix them. It restates the LR; it never extends it.

## Precedence of sources

1. The Language Reference (`LANG-` rules) is normative for the core; where its prose and the grammar
   `reference/grammar/fortis.ebnf` disagree on syntax, the grammar wins; where a rule and an example disagree, the
   rule wins (LR 0).
2. The Platform Specification (`PLAT-` rules) defines the kits. A `PROG-` ID, in a record's `rule`, names a
   requirement on the toolchain itself: its tools, records and process.
3. This agent mode and the human guide are derived from them. A page that contradicts them is a defect in the page.

Decisions are logged as register rows `X-nnn`, and known toolchain defects as `D-nn`, in the maintainers'
planning records; pages cite them by ID. What v0.0.2 runs, and what it still refuses, is
[Known limitations](known-limitations.md); the release note is
[v0.0.2](../releases/v0.0.2.md).

## Tools

Run from the repository root after `cd compiler && cargo build --release`. `fortis` is `bin/fortis`.

| Command | Output (pipe, or `--format json`) | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `fortis view PATH` / `--decls` / `--symbol NAME` / `--query Q` / `--json` | JSON lines, `kind` one of `line`, `declaration`, `symbol`, `match`, `query` | read `.ft` source; never `cat`/`grep` |
| `fortis check FILE.ft\|DIR --format json` | one diagnostic record per line; none means clean | all static checks |
| `fortis run FILE.ft\|DIR [ARGS…]` | the program's standard output; runtime records on standard error | run `main` on the definitional interpreter with `ARGS` as its arguments; files from `FORTIS_DEV_ROOT` (relative to the working directory), else a fresh empty directory |
| `fortis test FILE.ft\|DIR --format json` | `test-result` records on standard error, then one `test-summary` on standard output | run tests and properties on the interpreter |
| `fortisc test FILE.ft\|DIR --format json` | the same records, on the same streams | run tests on the development VM |
| `fortisc vm FILE.ft\|DIR` | `observed: line\|line\|…` (the conformance form) | run `main` on the development VM |
| `fortis build FILE.ft\|DIR --out APP` | one `build` record (`binary`, `manifest`) | native executable through safe Rust |
| `fortis fmt --check PATH` / `--write PATH` | files not in canonical layout / rewritten | canonical layout, after rewriting older forms into the forms these pages teach where the module checks and the meaning is unchanged (`--no-migrate`: layout only) |

Every finding and runtime report is a record first; text is rendered from it, and the stream chooses the form
(JSON lines on a pipe) unless `--format` says otherwise. Schemas and record kinds are in
[records](records.md).

A diagnostic record (`reference/schemas/diagnostic.schema.json`), here for a use after a move
(LR 7.4):

```fortis
// reject: E-OWN-020
pure func size(items: owned List[Int]) Int {
  let kept = move items
  return items.count()                // reject: E-OWN-020
}

test "size" {
  expect size(List.of(1, 2)) == 2
}
```

```records
{"class": "Ownership", "code": "E-OWN-020", "column": 10, "fields": {"conflict": "use after move", "loan_region": "", "place": "items", "spans": "items"}, "file": "example.ft", "line": 4, "message": "`items` was moved and is used again (read)", "rule": "LANG-07-04", "severity": "error", "status": "violated"}
```

- `code`: stable; look it up in [codes](codes.md). `rule`: the `LANG-`/`PLAT-`/`PROG-` ID it enforces.
- `status`: `violated` (a proved violation), `unproved` (the checker could not prove a refinement or claim; not
  proof of a bug), `unknown` (a trust boundary).
- `fields`: the class's mandatory fields. `correction`, when present, is an applicable edit:
  `{"kind": …, "edits": [{"file", "line", "column", "end_line", "end_column", "replacement"}]}`.

A runtime failure is written to standard error once, by `report`, by a cleanup, by a scope abandoning a task's
result, or by a failing `try main` (LR 4.6, LR 10.6, LR 12.1, LR 12.5), as
a record with `kind: "runtime-failure"`, the failure's `code` and `payload`, its `origin` (`file`, `function`),
`cause` and `annotations` (the `annotate` trail), `reported_by` (`report`, `main`, `cleanup` or `abandoned`) and
`rule`. Tests write
`test-result` records (`test`, `case`, `status`, `evidence`) and one `test-summary` (`passed`, `failed`).

## The loop

1. Inspect: `fortis view --decls DIR`, `fortis view --symbol NAME DIR`, `fortis view --query Q DIR` (queries:
   `async`, `try`, `async-try`, `pure`, `noalloc`, `trusted`, `recovers`, `editable-params`, `owned-params`,
   `or-fail`, `or-recover`, `catch`, `fail`, `return`, `defer`, `scope`, `capture`, `expect`, `move`, `lambda`,
   `tests`, `errors`, `classes`, `aspect:NAME`).
2. Edit.
3. Check: `fortis check DIR --format json`. For each record: read `code`, `rule`, `fields`; apply `correction`
   when present; otherwise use the correction pattern of the code's page.
4. Test: `fortis test DIR --format json`; a failing test is evidence, not an obstacle.
5. Format: `fortis fmt --write DIR`, so inferred facts are printed back and old forms take their reading forms where
   they mean the same: unmarked `editable self` receivers and `fn mut` calls, `return local`, heads without `Void`,
   `main`'s capability parameters, implied `or fail` in tests, `Map.get` keys without `copy`, puns, or-pattern arms,
   checked operators, bare variants (LR 1.1, X-345).
6. Repeat until `check` prints nothing and every test passes.

## Prohibitions

- Do not read `.ft` files with `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed -n` or `less`, or search them with `grep` or `rg`; use
  `fortis view`.
- Do not weaken a contract, remove an `expect`, or change an expected output to make a check or test pass.
 
- Do not lower a threshold or delete an assertion without a visible, approved policy change.
- Do not hand-format Fortis code; run `fortis fmt --write`.
- Do not treat `unproved` as a bug or as safe: add the explicit proof or checked alternative the record names.

## Example notation on these pages

Every `fortis` block is checked by `python3 -I conformance/tools/docset_check.py` on the real toolchain.
First line: `// accept` (both checkers report nothing; it runs: `main` on the interpreter, the VM
and native code with exactly the `output` block shown, or its tests pass on all three; `(exit status N)` when
`main` fails on purpose), `// reject: CODE` (exactly that code on each line carrying the same marker, nothing
else), `// illustrative` (not a program). A `records` block is the exact JSON the checker prints for the block
above it, with the file named `example.ft` (LR 0).

# Known limitations of v0.0.2

<!-- covers: LR 0 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Known limitations of v0.0.2](../guide/known-limitations.md). Release note: [v0.0.2](../releases/v0.0.2.md).*

Open, non-blocking defects in v0.0.2's scope, plus loud refusals (X-343): a checked program, a non-zero exit, another backend correct. Do not treat a row as a licence to change the program's meaning. A soundness bug or a wrong result is absent here unless v0.0.1 already had it: those are carried under X-416 in their own section, and code must avoid their shapes, since the checkers do not. The last section is what v0.0.2 leaves for later by design (its release note).

Open, non-blocking defects in v0.0.2's scope, plus loud refusals (X-343): a checked program, a non-zero exit, another backend correct. Do not treat a row as a licence to change the program's meaning. A soundness bug or a wrong result on every backend is absent here on purpose. The last section is what v0.0.2 leaves for later (its release note): by design, or a recorded gap with its defect id.

Generated from the defect register and the release's own list, with the human-mode page; edit those, not the page.

## Valid programs the checkers reject, and library gaps

<!-- no-citation: each row is a toolchain limitation already recorded against v0.0.2 or before; the language rules are unchanged -->

| Defect | What you meet | Workaround |
|---|---|---|
| D-51.5 | An unused import is accepted with no warning. | Delete the import. Nothing else changes. |
| D-52.1 | An error constructor is typed as its own kind, so a use that the language accepts where a failure is expected is rejected. | Match the constructor's own type, or construct the failure where its own name is expected. |
| D-52.4 | Returning a call that passes a loan-holding closure is rejected even when the result is a plain integer. | None recorded. |
| D-52.6 | A class you declare with the same name as a prelude type, such as Task, is checked as the prelude's linear type. | Name the class something the prelude does not declare. |
| D-54.6 | For a parameter named with a keyword, fortisc vm reports a generic syntax error and fortisc check reports the keyword-specific one. | Rename the parameter. Both tools refuse the program. |
| D-58.1 | Map has no iterate operation. A for loop over a map yields key and value tuples, which the language reference does not state. | Write for over the map when a key and a value together are enough. |
| D-58.7 | Map has no remove and no contains. | None recorded. Build a new map without the key, or scan it. |
| D-58.9 | Every text accessor can fail, so a comparator written as a pure function of two texts must recover. | Recover inside the comparator, or do not mark it pure. |
| D-251 | A variant whose name is also a class's is rejected by both checkers, so the program does not reach the VM. List.of(Red) with the list's element type written out runs on the interpreter, the VM and native. | Write the variant with its enum prefix, or do not declare a class of the same name. The list form already runs when the expected type is written. |
| D-252 | Both checkers reject an optional-chained method call such as lights.get(0)?.code(). The call does not reach the VM. | Match the optional and call the method on the present value. |
| D-285 | A package whose manifest the loader refuses (conformance/packages/bad.policy) makes fortis check, run and test exit 2 with a message on standard error, and fortisc check exit 1 with a names record on project.yaml. | Both tools refuse the package. Read fortisc's record; it names the manifest. |
| D-343 | A property runs 25 generated cases with fortis test and 100 with fortisc test, from different generators, so a property that fails on few inputs can pass on one and fail on the other. | Run properties with fortisc test as well, and turn a failure it finds into an example test. |
| D-344 | The executor trace of a native build has no drop event for an owned optional local, for a temporary a ?? fallback made, or for the bindings of a match arm that owns its scrutinee; the interpreter and the VM trace each, and all three trace a fallback a ?? moved into its result. Cleanup runs once on all three, and the output and the log records agree. | Compare traces on the interpreter and the VM; the native trace leaves those drops out. |
| D-363 | A tuple that holds a loan, such as (xs.get(0), 1), cannot yet be reassigned to a let mut binding that holds one, or returned from a function declared to return one: both checkers reject it as a loan where an owned value is required, although the Language Reference allows both. The same with an optional, t = xs.get(1), is accepted. | Keep the loan in a binding of its own (let t = xs.get(0)) and the other values beside it, and reassign or return those separately. |
| D-365 | A defer that changes a list, such as defer { let v = xs.pop() }, is rejected while a binding of the same block holds a loan from that list inside an optional (let t = xs.get(0)), although a deferred block runs after its block's own loans have ended. | Put the loan in an inner block that ends before the defer's block does, or make the change after the block. |
| D-400 | A function that binds a loan of a type whose cleanup does I/O (let t = alias b.t, or a ?? whose fallback fails) is charged that cleanup's effects, so a function that destroys nothing may be refused as not pure or asked to declare io. | Declare the effect, or keep such loans out of functions declared pure. |
| D-401 | A let mut cursor cannot be reassigned (the checkers report a move of a lent owner), although a cursor is owned by its binding (LR 7.7). | Make a new cursor in a binding of its own. |
| D-402 | After match move o of a binding that holds a loan (let o = xs.get(0)), the loan o held is not released, so the owner stays frozen for the rest of the block (xs.push is refused as a change under a live loan). New with this release's loan holders. | Put the match and the binding in an inner block, so the loan ends with it. |

## One backend refuses the program

<!-- no-citation: each row is a loud refusal under X-343; another backend runs the same program -->

| Defect | What you meet | Workaround |
|---|---|---|
| D-54.10 | A catch that returns inside a for is refused: fortisc test and fortis build exit 1, reporting that the typed IR uses a moved binding. The interpreter's test passes. A move in a returning branch, the other half of this entry, builds and its VM test passes. | Run that test with fortis test. Keep the catch out of the loop, or bind the failure's value before the loop continues. |
| D-55.6 | A narrowed optional is not unwrapped in the native build. copy of a String? after != null, and a field read through a narrowed shared optional, each make fortis build exit 1 (rustc E0308, or no such field). The interpreter and the VM print the value. | Run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. |
| D-55.8 | A dynamic fn in a list or a field does not build natively (rustc E0308 for the list, E0277 for the field). The interpreter and the VM run the programs. | Run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. |
| D-55.16 | A local optional narrowed by != null and moved into a non-optional field is not unwrapped. fortis build exits 1 (rustc E0308). The interpreter and the VM print 7. | Run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. |
| D-156 | A function-type parameter that owns its argument, fn(owned T), is lowered as a borrowed parameter. fortis build exits 1 (rustc E0631 when a named function is passed, E0308 when a lambda is). The interpreter and the VM run the call. | Run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. |
| D-185 | A function whose result is an exclusive loan of its parameter, editable Cell from c, returning editable c (the Language Reference's own example in 7.6), does not build natively, nor does any returned exclusive loan: fortis build exits 1 (rustc E0308), because the returned loan is lowered as a read reference. The interpreter and the VM run it. | Run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. Or change the value through the parameter inside the function and return nothing. |
| D-157.1 | A closure stored in a class field does not build natively (rustc E0277, the field's display). The interpreter and the VM run the program. Assigning a second lambda to one closure binding is a separate item and is rejected by both checkers. | Run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. A dynamic fn is the heterogeneous form, and a field of that type is D-55.8, which also refuses natively. |
| D-244 | A type named like an item the generated Rust uses does not build natively: a class Vec, From or String, or a type alias String, in any program, Option beside an optional, and Box beside a recursive type (rustc E0107, E0404 and others). The interpreter and the VM run the program. Result, Rc, HashMap and the variant names Some, None, Ok and Err build. | Rename the type, or run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. |
| D-245 | Arithmetic on literals at a sized integer type, such as let x: Int32 = -2147483647 - 1 or let y: Int32 = 2 + 3, does not build natively: the literals are emitted as 64-bit integers (rustc E0308). The interpreter and the VM print the value. A single literal builds. | Write the folded literal (-2147483648, 5), or run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. |
| D-270 | A function declared to return one non-dynamic fn type may return two different lambdas. The interpreter and the VM run both (3 and 4). fortis build exits 1 (rustc E0308). | Run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. Return one lambda, or declare the result dynamic fn when the two bodies really differ. |
| D-342 | A test's expect that compares an optional with a literal, such as expect first(names) == "a", does not build natively (rustc E0614). fortis test and fortisc test pass the test. | Bind the present value first (let got = first(names) ?? "none", then expect got == "a"), or run the test with fortis test or fortisc test. |
| D-360 | A record literal that holds a loan, such as { item: xs.get(0), n: 1 }, does not build natively (rustc E0106), nor does a tuple with a loan passed to a read parameter of tuple type (E0308). The interpreter and the VM run them, and each cleanup runs once. A tuple holding a list's loan, such as (xs.get(0), 1), or an alias loan of a local, such as (alias own, make("p")), builds. A tuple bound first around a value of the function's own and returned as a from result (let t = (empty.get(0) ?? move d, 1), then return t from alias (Token, Int) from empty, which the Language Reference allows and the interpreter and the VM run correctly) does not build either (E0308), so a bearing aggregate from result has no spelling that builds natively yet. | Run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. Or keep the loan in its own binding and pass it on its own. |
| D-361 | A binding that holds a loan on one path and a value of its own on another does not build natively (rustc E0308): an if that gives xs.get(0) on one branch and move d on the other, or assigning a new class value, which the binding then owns, to a let mut binding that held a loan. The interpreter and the VM run it, and the binding destroys only a value it owns. | Run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. Or give the binding one kind of value: copy the loan, or keep the owned value in a binding of its own. |
| D-353 | A function whose result is an optional loan of text, such as (alias String from xs)? returning xs.get(0), does not build natively (rustc E0308). The interpreter and the VM run it. The same result of a class builds, except through a generic from function (D-387). | Return an owned copy (let t = xs.get(0), then return copy t from a function returning String?), or run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. |
| D-387 | A generic function whose result is an optional loan of its type parameter, such as func first[T](xs: List[T]) (alias T from xs)? => xs.get(0), does not build natively when it is instantiated at a class (rustc E0277). The interpreter and the VM run it. | Write the function for the class (func first(xs: List[Token]) (alias Token from xs)?), which builds, or run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. |
| D-390 | A byte string returned as the whole BytesView from xs result (=> b"abc"), or as a BytesView from static one, does not build natively (rustc E0515), nor does an if or match that gives a string literal on one branch and a view of a String through a loan on another (give "empty" beside give alias t.label, as StringView from t; rustc E0308), nor the outcome-expression spellings of that shape: or recover "missing" as a (alias StringView from xs)? result, or present("none") in an if branch of one (rustc E0308). The interpreter and the VM run them. A string literal as the whole StringView from xs result builds. | Return the literal from a function of its own, or run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. |
| D-415 | An anonymous record returned by return r past a deferred block that reads it (let r = { n: 5, m: 8 }, defer { console.print("bye ${r.n}") }, return r) does not build natively (rustc E0382), whatever its field types: the record is moved by the return, where a trivial class, a tuple or an enum is copied. Both checkers accept it and the interpreter and the VM run it. | Use a class or a tuple for the value, or run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. |
| D-382 | A marker written on a call of a module function, such as let t = alias first(alias xs), passes both checkers and runs on the VM and natively, but the interpreter stops with a dynamic failure (first is not declared). The marker belongs on the argument alone. | Write let t = first(alias xs): the call lends what its result declares, and no marker is needed on the call. |
| D-396 | first() on a list whose element is a class, such as xs.first() on List[Token], does not build natively (rustc E0277, the element is not Clone). The interpreter and the VM run it. | Use xs.get(0), which builds, or run it with fortis run or fortisc vm. |
| D-397 | I/O through a capability held in a local's field (let d = make(console, ...); d.console.print(...)) passes both checkers and runs on the interpreter, but the VM's IR validation refuses it (the receiver is not derived from a parameter through places) and native code reports that refusal as an internal compiler defect. | Print through the capability parameter itself, or a binding made from it directly. |
| D-399 | Array.filled with its size taken from the expected type, such as let arr: Array[Int, 3] = Array.filled(7), passes both checkers, and every backend then refuses it. | Write the size on the call: Array[Int, 3].filled(7). |
| D-354 | An owned optional local of a class with cleanup, written without a marker on the left of a ?? that moves its fallback (let p: Token? = none ?? move d), does not build natively (rustc E0382). The interpreter and the VM run it. | Write move none ?? move d, which builds and runs alike on every backend. |

## Defects carried from v0.0.1

<!-- no-citation: each row is a defect v0.0.1 already had, recorded for the next release under X-416 -->

The checkers accept each of these programs although the Language Reference rejects it, so a checked program can still go wrong. v0.0.1 had every one of them; v0.0.2 is no worse, and each is fixed in the release its record names. Avoid the shape, as the second column says.

| Defect | What you meet | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| D-352 | Inside a generic function, a loan can be returned or stored as if it were owned: func id[T](x: T) T { return x } and func first[T](xs: List[T]) T? { return xs.get(0) } are accepted, and the caller then holds a second reference to the argument or the list's element. | Write the function for the concrete type, where the checkers require copy or reject the loan. |
| D-355 | A loan given out of an if or match branch (give xs.get(0)), or lent by a match's scrutinee that is a temporary, such as match xs.get(0), ends with its statement, so the list can be changed while the loan is still in use. | Bind the loan with let first (let t = xs.get(0)) and branch or match on t: a let binding holds the loan to the end of its block. |
| D-356 | A field read through an optional loan with ?., such as xs.get(0)?.inner, is typed as owned, so a binding of it can change the list's own element on the interpreter and the VM. | Treat a value read with ?. through a loan as read-only: do not change it, or a binding made from it. To change a value of your own, build a new one. |
| D-357 | An owned optional binding written without a marker on the left of a ?? whose result is owned, as in let p: Token? = some ?? move d, is accepted, so p and some both own the value. | Write move some ?? move d, or copy some ?? move d. |
| D-362 | A loan held inside an optional by a let mut binding (let mut t = xs.get(0)) is treated as ended after a while or for loop whose body ends it (t = null), although a loop that runs no times, a break or a continue skips that, so the list can be changed while the loan lives. | End the loan before the loop (t = null), or keep the loan in a block that ends before the list changes. |
| D-364 | A defer that reads a binding of its block holding a loan inside an optional (let t = xs.get(0), then defer { ... t ... }) is accepted, although a deferred block may not use a binding of its block that holds a loan. | Read what the deferred block needs before it, into a value of its own (copy), and use that in the defer. |
| D-369 | A binding of a ?? whose fallback it owns, such as let t = empty.get(0) ?? move d, is typed as a loan of the list, so it can be stored in a binding of an outer block (keep = present(t)) and read there after the fallback's cleanup has run. | Keep such a binding in its own block, or move the fallback into a binding of its own first (let f = move d) and use that. |
| D-370 | On the interpreter, an unmarked copy of such a binding, or of a tuple element holding such a value (let a = t, let a = pair.0), becomes a second owner, so the fallback's cleanup runs when the copy ends, before the binding does. | Write copy t (or alias t) to say which you mean. |
| D-375 | A ?? whose fallback is the statement's own value, lent to a read parameter (show(console, empty.get(0) ?? move d)), is never destroyed on the interpreter or the VM, so its cleanup does not run; native code destroys it when the statement ends. | Bind the fallback first (let v = empty.get(0) ?? move d) and pass v, so the binding's end runs its cleanup. |
| D-376 | On the interpreter, assigning to a field of a record literal (rec.side = make(...), or a loan over a field that held a value of the record's own) does not run the old value's cleanup, and a loan assigned over such a field is cleaned up with the record while its owner still holds it. The VM runs each cleanup once, at its owner's end. | Use a class for a value whose fields are reassigned, or run the program on the VM. |
| D-379 | A fn once closure may return a loan from a move capture (fn once[move t]() Token from t { return move t }), which the consuming call destroys: both checkers accept it, the interpreter and the VM keep the value until the receiving binding ends or read it destroyed, and native code refuses the build. | Return the captured value itself from a closure returning the owned type, or let the caller keep the binding and lend it to the closure instead of moving it in. |
| D-388 | A tuple built around a value of the function's own (let t = (empty.get(0) ?? move d, 1)), bound first and returned inside present as a from result, passes both checkers; the interpreter destroys the value at the call and the caller then reads it destroyed, and the VM never runs its cleanup. | Return the owned value from a function returning the owned type, or keep the fallback in a binding of its own (let f = move d) that outlives the result. |
| D-389 | Inside a returned match arm, an if giving a loan on one branch and the function's own value on the other (let v = if flag { give x } else { give move d }; give v) passes both checkers, and both running backends destroy the moved value at the call, so later reads see it destroyed. | Give every branch a loan, or return the owned value from a function returning the owned type. |
| D-392 | A loan taken from a temporary receiver, such as let t = fresh().get(0) (also .first(), ?? make(...), or a cursor of a temporary), passes both checkers; the temporary is destroyed at the statement's end and t then reads the destroyed element on the interpreter and the VM; native refuses the build. | Bind the temporary first (let xs = fresh()) and take the loan from the binding. |
| D-393 | A pure function may print through a dropped value's cleanup: the io of a cleanup is not attributed to the function that drops the value, so both checkers accept it and every backend prints. | Do not drop a value whose cleanup does I/O inside a function declared pure; give the value to the caller. |
| D-394 | A lent match payload (match xs.get(0) { present(x) => ... }) is destroyed at the arm's end on the interpreter, and on the VM for a plain optional, rather than at its owner's end, so a read of the element after the match sees it destroyed; native is right. | Read what you need inside the arm, or bind the loan first (let t = xs.get(0)) and match on t. |
| D-395 | A result declared from one parameter (from xs) that lends another (ys) is rejected for a direct return but not through give, a match expression or an expression body, so the loan is recorded against the wrong owner and ys can change while the result lives. | Declare the result from the parameter it lends, and return it directly. |
| D-413 | On the VM, an owned value recovered by a catch expression whose result the statement discards (discard (g() catch e { report e; recover make(...) })) is never destroyed, so its cleanup does not run; the interpreter and native code run it. The or recover form, and a catch whose value a let binds, run it on the VM too. | Bind the catch's value (let x = g() catch e { ... }), so the binding's end runs the cleanup, or write or recover. |
| D-414 | An expect outside a test body, in an ordinary function or in a deferred block, is accepted by both checkers, and a failing one has no defined outcome: the interpreter stops with a Python traceback and writes no record, the VM reports a dynamic check failure, and native code does not build the program. | Write expect in test bodies only. In a function, test the condition with if, and fail or return. |

## What v0.0.2 leaves for later

<!-- no-citation: each row is a limit of this release that its release note lists; the Defect cell names the record of a gap left open on purpose, and is empty for a limit by design -->

| Defect | What you meet | What to do |
|---|---|---|
|  | The older forms are accepted alongside the new ones, so a reader may meet both until the code is migrated. | Run fortis fmt --write on the code. It rewrites each older form where the program means the same. |
| D-404 | fortis fmt never rewrites Int.shiftLeft(a, b) or fail to a << b or fail, although the two are the same operation; Int.add, sub, mul, div and rem are rewritten. | Write the operator form by hand, or leave the named call. The two mean the same. |
|  | fortis fmt does not rewrite a logging call, add @ignorable or derive Default, or rewrite a main that reads its Capabilities record other than field by field (a capability inside an interpolation, or the record moved whole). | Make those changes by hand. Each is the author's choice. |
| D-406 | fortis fmt keeps a pure or noalloc written on a lambda, although the function type the lambda is passed to already states it; it prints no inferred one. | Remove the modifier by hand if you want the shorter form. It changes nothing the checker decides. |
|  | Checked operators cover Int only. The sized integer types (Int32, UInt8 and the rest) have no checked, wrapping or saturating operations yet; they are planned for v0.4. | Give the operands a refined type, or test them first, so that the operation is proved. Or compute in Int. |
|  | fortis fmt prints a module's inferred facts back only when the module checks on its own, so a module of a package that needs the rest of its package to check is not given them. | Nothing changes in what the program means; the checker infers the facts either way. Write a fact by hand where you want it shown. |

# Records

<!-- covers: LR 0 -->
*Agent mode. Source of truth: the schema `reference/schemas/diagnostic.schema.json`, and LR 10.6, LR 10.8, LR 13
and LR 14 for the runtime records.*

Every finding, runtime failure report, test result and observation the toolchain produces is a record first: a
JSON object of a known kind, from which the text a person sees is rendered. Read the
record, not the text.

## Streams

| Situation | What is written |
|---|---|
| standard output is a pipe | one JSON object per line |
| standard output is a terminal | text rendered from the same record |
| `--format json` / `--format text` | forces that rendering |
| a running program's records (failure reports, defects, logs, observation frames and events) | standard error, same rule; the program's own output is standard output (LR 4.6) |

Where each command writes, as the toolchain does today:

| Command | Standard output | Standard error |
|---|---|---|
| `fortis check`, `fortisc check` | diagnostic records | — |
| `fortis run`, a native executable | the program's output | runtime records |
| `fortis test` (interpreter) | the `test-summary` record | `test-result` and other runtime records |
| `fortisc test` (VM) | the `test-summary` record | `test-result` and other runtime records, as `fortis test` writes them |
| `fortis build`, `fortisc build` | the `build` record | diagnostic records if the check fails |
| `fortisc vm` | the conformance format: `=== FILE`, `observed: …` (output lines joined by `\|`), `trace: …`, `record: …` | — |

A finding has one identity: `fortis check`, the daemon and the agent protocol produce byte-equal records for the
same snapshot. `fortis check` (the reference checker) and `fortisc check` (the
production checker) print records of this one schema, with the same codes at the same lines.

## Diagnostic records

Schema: `reference/schemas/diagnostic.schema.json`.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | stable diagnostic code, `E-XXX-NNN` |
| `class` | string | the diagnostic class (table below) |
| `rule` | string | the normative rule the record enforces (`LANG-`, `PROG-` or `PLAT-` ID) |
| `file`, `line`, `column` | string, integer, integer | primary location, the user's nearest responsible operation (1-based) |
| `severity` | `error` or `warning` | a warning does not fail the check |
| `status` | `violated`, `unproved` or `unknown` | a proved violation, an inability to prove, an unknown trust boundary |
| `message` | string | one-line explanation |
| `fields` | object | the class's mandatory fields |
| `correction` | object, optional | `{kind, edits: [{file, line, column, end_line, end_column, replacement}]}`, an applicable edit |

`unproved` means the checker could not prove a bound, not that the program is wrong: supply the proof or use the
checked alternative the message names (LR 6.3). A `correction`'s `kind` is a short
description of the edit (for example `add the marker`). A fix preserves behaviour, changes it or weakens a
contract, but today's records do not carry that class, so judge it from the edit itself; the compiler never
removes `noalloc` or a security requirement to make code compile, and an agent never applies an edit that weakens
a claim.

### Classes and mandatory fields

| Class | Code prefix | Mandatory `fields` | Correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Type | `E-TYP`, `E-MIX-001` (LR 6.10) | `expected_type`, `actual_type`, `primary_span` | behaviour-preserving or behaviour-changing fix |
| Ownership | `E-OWN` | `place`, `conflict`, `spans`, `loan_region` | marker, block restructuring, `copy` |
| Obligation | `E-OBL`, `E-ERR-001` (LR 5.4) | `obligation_origin`, `unconsumed_path` | `or fail`, `or recover`, `report`, `match` |
| Effect | `E-EFF` | `required_contract`, `violating_effect`, `witness_path` | contract-weakening or behaviour-changing fix |
| Refinement unproved | `E-REF` | `required_range`, `proved_interval`, `widening_point` | a checked operator (`a + b or fail`), `validate` |
| Unsupported shape | `E-OWN-090` (LR 7.10) | `lowering_row` | none (restructure) |
| Resource limit | `E-LIM` | `budget`, `operation` | none |
| Internal defect | `E-INT` | `reproduction` | none |
| Syntax | `E-SYN` | `expected_tokens`, `found_token` | where the grammar allows one |
| Names and modules | `E-NAM` | `name`, `candidates` | import, rename |
| Patterns | `E-MAT` | `missing_variants`, `arm_set` | add arms |
| Closures | `E-FUN` | `violation`, `capture_span`, `use_span` | capture entry, stronger kind |
| Defer and async | `E-DEF`, `E-ASY` | `offending_statement`, `rule_reference` | move the statement out of `defer`, add an `await` site |
| Observation | `E-OBS` | `frame_field`, `exit_path` | add or remove `capture` |
| Dependency injection (kit, Platform 3) | `E-DI` | `consumer`, `slot`, `candidates` | target, `replaces`, `lifetime:` |
| Telemetry (kit, Platform 6.4) | `E-TEL` | `plan_line`, `projection`, `field` | `bind_at`, a new metric name, a new schema version |

Every code, its class, its rule and its correction pattern: [codes.md](codes.md).

### Example: a violation

The record for an assignment to an immutable binding (LR 5.1):

```fortis
// reject: E-NAM-002
pure func next(n: Int<0..9>) Int {
  let x = n
  x = 1                     // reject: E-NAM-002
  return x
}

test "next" {
  expect next(1) == 1
}
```

```records
{"class": "Names and modules", "code": "E-NAM-002", "column": 3, "fields": {"candidates": ["let mut"], "name": "x"}, "file": "example.ft", "line": 4, "message": "`x` is immutable", "rule": "LANG-05-01", "severity": "error", "status": "violated"}
```

### Example: an unproved bound

An integer `+` the checker cannot prove in range is `E-REF-002` with status `unproved`; `proved_interval` is what
the checker established and `required_range` what the type needs (LR 6.4):

```fortis
// reject: E-REF-002
pure func sum(a: Int, b: Int) Int {
  return a + b              // reject: E-REF-002
}

test "sum" {
  expect sum(1, 2) == 3
}
```

```records
{"class": "Refinement unproved", "code": "E-REF-002", "column": 12, "fields": {"proved_interval": "[-18446744073709551616, 18446744073709551614]", "required_range": "[-9223372036854775808, 9223372036854775807]", "widening_point": ""}, "file": "example.ft", "line": 3, "message": "`+` may overflow Int: operands [-9223372036854775808, 9223372036854775807] and [-9223372036854775808, 9223372036854775807] give [-18446744073709551616, 18446744073709551614]; use Int.add, or write the operator as the checked operation: `a + b or fail` (or `or recover`, `catch`)", "rule": "LANG-06-02", "severity": "error", "status": "unproved"}
```

### Example: a record with a correction

The text rendering lists the fields, then the correction's `kind` and each edit as
`file:line:column-end_line:end_column -> "replacement"`. A missing ownership marker (LR 7.5):

```fortis
// reject: E-OWN-001
class Note {
  export text: String
}

test "note" {
  let a = Note(text: "x")
  let b = a                 // reject: E-OWN-001
  expect b.text == "x"
}
```

```output
example.ft:8:11: error E-OWN-001 [LANG-07-01] (Ownership, violated): `a` is an existing ownership-bearing place: write `copy a`, `alias a` or `move a`
    conflict: "marker required"
    loan_region: ""
    place: "a"
    spans: "a"
    correction: add the marker
      example.ft:8:11-8:11 -> "copy "
```

The edit inserts `copy ` (a behaviour-preserving choice); `move a` or `alias a` are the other repairs the message
names, chosen by what the code does with `a` afterwards (LR 7.5).

## Runtime records

Written while a program or its tests run (see Streams above for where each command writes them). The schemas are
`interpreter/records.py`; field values below are real records of the reference toolchain.

| `kind` | Written when | Fields | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runtime-failure` | `report f`, a failure reported during cleanup, a failure in a task result the scope abandoned, or a failing `try main` (exactly one report, exit status 1) | `code`, `message`, `payload`, `origin` (`file`, `function`), `cause`, `annotations`, `reported_by` (`report`, `main`, `cleanup`, `abandoned`), `rule` | LR 4.6, LR 10.6, LR 12.1, LR 12.5 |
| `defect` | a defect terminates a task | `class` (`stack_exhaustion`, …), `task`, `rule` | LR 10.8 |
| `observation-frame` | an observed activation completes | `schema`, `function`, `outcome`, `fields`, `truncated`, `rule` | LR 13 |
| `observation-event` | a `record` statement runs | `schema`, `fields`, `rule` | LR 13 |
| `log` | a `log.info`, `log.warn` or `log.error` statement runs; text `warn: a fallback was taken` | `level` (`info`, `warn`, `error`), `message`, `function`, `rule` (`LANG-13-04`) | LR 13 |
| `test-result` | each test, table row or property case | `test`, `case`, `status` (`pass`, `fail`, `error`), `evidence` (typed actual and expected), `rule` | LR 14 |
| `property-failure` | a property or fuzz target fails | `test`, `mode`, `seed`, `case`, `original`, `minimal` (the shrunk input), `shrinks`, `evidence`, `replay` (the command that replays it), `rule` | LR 14 |
| `test-summary` | end of a test run | `passed`, `failed`, `rule` | LR 14 |
| `task-lifecycle` | a never-polled future is discarded, or a task is cancelled before it starts (`state` `not_started`) | `function`, `state`, `rule` | LR 12.3, LR 13 |
| `task-completion` | a detached task completes, as its supervisor observes it | `task`, `outcome`, `rule` | LR 12.6 |
| `buffer-overflow` | the task reporter's buffer overflowed: one record, its `dropped` count growing | `bound`, `dropped`, `rule` | LR 15 |
| `executor-trace` | a native program run with `FORTIS_TRACE=1` | `events` (`launch`, `start`, `suspend`, `resume`, `complete`, `join`, `loans-end`) | LR 12.5 |
| `build` | `fortis build` / `fortisc build` finishes | `binary`, `manifest` | LR 1 |

The backends do not yet agree on every field (D-57): the interpreter counts each property case as a test, native
code writes `evidence` as a string, and a failure's `origin` has no line on any backend; `fortis test` and
`fortisc test` write the same `evidence`, its `line` included. Match on `kind`, `code`, `test` and `status`.

Captured field values leave the process only through the Telemetry kit's pipeline; with no telemetry plan the
task reporter writes a frame's schema, outcome class and duration but never a captured value (`fields` is empty),
and `FORTIS_TELEMETRY=permit-all` is the explicit development plan that writes them unchanged (LR 15).

A failure's `origin.file` is never an absolute path, on any backend, so an executable does not depend on where it
was built: a module of a package is named relative to the package's directory (`src/pricing.ft`), and a standalone
module relative to the current directory when it lies below it, else by its file name.

A `report` of a declared error, as written by the interpreter and the native executable (LR 10.6):

```json
{"annotations": [], "cause": [], "code": "demo.not_even", "kind": "runtime-failure", "message": "", "origin": {"file": "examples/02_outcomes.ft", "function": "half"}, "payload": {"value": "9"}, "reported_by": "report", "rule": "LANG-10-06"}
```

A frame and an event under `FORTIS_TELEMETRY=permit-all` (LR 13, LR 15):

```json
{"fields": {"value": "5"}, "kind": "observation-event", "rule": "LANG-13-01", "schema": "Line"}
{"fields": {"items": "3", "total": "23"}, "function": "process", "kind": "observation-frame", "outcome": "success", "rule": "LANG-13-02", "schema": "OrderProcessing", "truncated": []}
```

A failed `expect` (LR 14):

```json
{"case": "", "evidence": {"actual": "4", "expected": "== 5", "line": 4}, "kind": "test-result", "rule": "LANG-14-02", "status": "fail", "test": "deliberately wrong"}
```

## `fortis view --json` records

<!-- no-citation: the toolchain's source viewer, not a language rule -->

`fortis view` reads Fortis source as the compiler does and never writes; `--json` is its primary form.
One object per line, `kind` one of:

| `kind` | From | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `line` | `fortis view FILE` | `path`, `line`, `text`, `spans` (`[column, length, class]`, class `keyword`, `name`, `type`, `punctuation`, `comment`, …) |
| `declaration` | `--decls` | `path`, `line`, `column`, `name`, `declaration`, `head`, `modifiers`, `contracts`, `aspects`, `doc`, `exported`, `member_of` |
| `symbol` | `--symbol NAME` | `path`, `name`, `line`, `end_line`, `text` |
| `match` | `--query Q` | `path`, `line`, `column`, `query`, `text` |
| `query` | `--queries` | `name`, `description` |

```json
{"aspects": [], "column": 10, "contracts": [], "declaration": "func", "doc": "", "exported": false, "head": "try func half(n: Int) Int", "kind": "declaration", "line": 11, "member_of": null, "modifiers": ["try"], "name": "half", "path": "examples/02_outcomes.ft"}
{"column": 21, "kind": "match", "line": 45, "path": "examples/02_outcomes.ft", "query": "or-fail", "text": "or"}
```

---
source: docs/agent/codes.md

# Diagnostic codes

<!-- covers: LR 0 -->
*Agent mode. Source of truth: the LR section cited in each row; classes and mandatory fields:
[records.md](records.md).*

Every diagnostic code the Language Reference names, grouped by class. **Rule** is the rule ID the toolchain's
record carries for the code (most often; where several rules share one code, the record names the one the
finding breaks; where the record carries a rule that is not the one the LR states for the code, the row says so,
D-57). **Pairs** is the agent page holding a reject/accept correction pair for the code, or the rules
for it. Look a record up by its `code`, read the cited section, apply the correction, re-check.

## Syntax (E-SYN)

| Code | Rule | LR | Trigger | Correction | Pairs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E-SYN-000 | LANG-03-02 | LR 3.2, LR 5.6, LR C.2 | not a sentence of the grammar (also `f() or fail ?? 0`; a loan type naming two origins) | fix the syntax; split the expression; `let v = f() or fail` on its own line | [03](03-lexical.md), [05](05-statements.md) |
| E-SYN-001 | LANG-03-01 | LR 3.2 | a `;` outside strings, comments, raw template regions | delete it (the record carries the edit) | [03](03-lexical.md), [B](appendix-b-decisions.md) |
| E-SYN-002 | LANG-03-04 | LR 3.4 | a keyword in a declaration or binding position | rename; a method may keep a keyword name | [A](appendix-a-keywords.md) |
| E-SYN-004 | LANG-05-06 | LR 5.6 | outcome operators, `??` and `&&`/`\|\|` mixed without parentheses | parenthesise | [05](05-statements.md) |

## Names and modules (E-NAM)

| Code | Rule | LR | Trigger | Correction | Pairs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E-NAM-001 | LANG-04-05 (as recorded; for an assignment the rule is LANG-05-01, D-57) | LR 4.5, LR 5.1, LR 10.3, LR 13 | an undeclared name (assignment to it, a use of it; `log` other than as a log statement, where nothing named `log` is declared; a `${name}` in an error's `message` that is not a payload field); also used for other unresolved names and module errors | declare it, import it, or fix the name; a log is `log.info(m)`, `log.warn(m)` or `log.error(m)` as a statement; a message names only payload fields | [05](05-statements.md), [04](04-modules.md) |
| E-NAM-002 | LANG-05-01 | LR 5.1 | assignment to an immutable binding or a parameter | `let mut`; copy a parameter into a `let mut` local | [05](05-statements.md) |
| E-NAM-003 | LANG-04-05 | LR 4.5 | a `let` shadows a visible binding | a new name | [05](05-statements.md), [04](04-modules.md) |
| E-NAM-004 | none stated (records carry the shadowing rule in error, D-57) | LR 4.4 | a declaration or member not visible here (not exported, or a constructor with a non-visible field) | `export` it, or use an associated function | [04](04-modules.md) |
| E-NAM-005 | LANG-04-06 | LR 4.6 | a parameter of the entry `main` the runtime cannot supply: a type other than `List[String]` or a capability imported from `fortis.host`, or a mode, default or `...` | give `main` only `name: List[String]` and `name: Console` (and the other capability types), and take anything else from them | [04](04-modules.md) |
| E-NAM-006 | LANG-04-06 | LR 4.6 | two parameters of the entry `main` with the same type | keep one parameter per type; lend it to the functions that need it | [04](04-modules.md) |
| E-NAM-010 | LANG-04-03 | LR 4.3 | dependency names that make the package/module split ambiguous | rename a package or module | [04](04-modules.md) |
| E-NAM-020 | PROG-ARC-04 | LR 4.1 | lockfile does not pin a dependency, pins one no manifest reaches, or is unreadable | `fortis lock` | [04](04-modules.md) |
| E-NAM-021 | PROG-ARC-04 | LR 4.1 | a package, compiler, standard library or Rust toolchain digest differs from the lockfile | restore the pinned input, or re-lock deliberately | [04](04-modules.md) |
| E-NAM-030 | PLAT-01-03 | LR 4.1 | an import of a standard module the build target's feature set lacks (`check --target`, `build --target`) | remove the import, or choose a target with the feature set | [04](04-modules.md) |
| E-NAM-031 | PLAT-01-01 | LR 4.1 | a standard-package dependency outside the published compatibility set | depend on the set's version | [04](04-modules.md) |
| E-NAM-032 | PROG-CMP-06 | LR 4.1 | a native build of a package that ships a Cargo build script | remove the build script | [04](04-modules.md) |
| E-NAM-034 | PROG-DEL-04 | LR 16 | a declaration head a kit defines (`export model Customer { … }`, `policy`, `page`) whose kit this toolchain does not install; `fields.candidates` names the kit | install the kit and import it, or remove the declaration (a plain `class` where no kit is wanted) | [16](16-kits.md) |

## Type (E-TYP, E-MIX-001; LR 6.10)

| Code | Rule | LR | Trigger | Correction | Pairs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E-TYP-010 | LANG-05-03 | LR 5.2, LR 6.8 | a non-`Bool` condition (`if n`, `if maybe`) | compare explicitly (`!= 0`, `!= null`) | [05](05-statements.md) |
| E-TYP-020 | LANG-06-05 | LR 6.3 | a float refinement | refine an integer, or validate by hand | [06](06-types.md) |
| E-TYP-030 | none stated (records carry the shadowing rule in error, D-57) | LR 4.4, LR 6.9 | an exported signature names a non-exported type, or a tuple, record or variant map (aspect parameters and the `fortis` package's own signatures excepted) | export the type; use a nominal class in exported signatures | [04](04-modules.md), [06](06-types.md) |
| E-TYP-040 | LANG-06-01 | LR 3.5, LR 6.1, LR 9.4, LR 9.7, LR 10.1 | a type mismatch (an `Outcome[T]` where `T` is expected; an interpolated `String` bound to `StringView`; a non-`Displayable` interpolation; a direct `cleanup` call; a bare variant whose name is also a class, error or type in scope, or that nothing expects the enum of) | consume the outcome first; fix the type; never call `cleanup`; qualify the variant (`Severity.Error`) or annotate the binding | [10](10-outcomes.md), [06](06-types.md), [09](09-classes.md) |
| E-TYP-050 | LANG-05-09 | LR 5.8, LR 9.2 | a parameter without a default, or a constructor field, left unbound | pass it | [05](05-statements.md), [09](09-classes.md) |
| E-TYP-060 | LANG-09-03 | LR 9.5 | an interface requirement cycle | break the cycle | [09](09-classes.md) |
| E-TYP-070 | LANG-09-01 | LR 9.1 | a name declared twice in a class (fields, methods, constants share one namespace) | rename one | [09](09-classes.md) |
| E-TYP-080 | LANG-09-03 | LR 9.5, LR 9.6 | incomplete implementation: missing member or required interface, incompatible signature, unmet mixin requirement | add the member, implementation or method | [09](09-classes.md) |
| E-TYP-090 | none stated (records carry the trivial-set rule in error, D-57) | LR 6.10, LR 13 | a derivation whose rule is not met (a field without the interface; `Encodable` with a private field; a canonical codec call on a non-codec type; a non-`Encodable` schema field) | implement the interface on the field type, export the fields, or write `encode`/`decode` by hand | [06](06-types.md), [13](13-observation.md) |
| E-TYP-100 | LANG-06-10 | LR 6.10, LR 9.5 | coherence: an implementation outside the packages defining the interface or the type, or an overlap | implement in the defining package; remove the overlap | [09](09-classes.md) |
| E-TYP-110 | LANG-05-05 | LR 5.4 | a path reaches the end of a non-`Void` function; a block arm or `if`-expression branch without `give` (reported at the function) | `return`/`fail` on that path; `give` in the branch | [05](05-statements.md) |
| E-TYP-120 | LANG-05-05 | LR 5.4 | `give` outside a match arm or `if` expression, `recover` outside `catch`, `break`/`continue` outside a loop | move it into the construct it ends | [05](05-statements.md) |
| E-TYP-130 | LANG-05-09 | LR 5.8 | positional after named, unknown parameter name, parameter bound twice, too many arguments | fix the argument list | [05](05-statements.md) |
| E-TYP-140 | LANG-05-08 | LR 5.5 | an unused non-`Void` expression statement (a call of an `@ignorable` function excepted) | `discard e`, or use the value; or declare the function `@ignorable` when most callers drop its result | [05](05-statements.md) |
| E-TYP-150 | LANG-11-09 | LR 11.8, LR 5.5 | an aspect application that does not match: unknown aspect, wrong arguments, unmet or ambiguous `needs`, `...rest` outside a parameter list; `@ignorable` on a function whose result is linear (`try`, `async`, a linear type) | fix the application or the target's parameters; drop `@ignorable` from a function whose result must be consumed | [11](11-effects.md) |
| E-TYP-160 | LANG-06-11 | LR 6.10 | a type argument fixed neither by the arguments nor by the expected type (`let names = List.default()`) | annotate the receiving binding | [06](06-types.md) |
| E-MIX-001 | LANG-09-04 | LR 6.10, LR 9.5, LR 9.6 | two mixins provide one method; a class derives an interface it also implements by hand | declare the method in the class; drop the `derive` or the hand-written method | [09](09-classes.md) |

## Ownership (E-OWN)

| Code | Rule | LR | Trigger | Correction | Pairs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E-OWN-001 | LANG-07-01 | LR 7.5, LR 7.6 | an existing ownership-bearing place assigned, returned (other than a local, which `return` moves), initialised into a field or passed `owned` without a marker; a loan of a copyable, non-trivial value (`xs.get(0)`, a binding holding one) where an owned value is expected (D-341); an `editable self` receiver or `fn mut` call, marked or not, on a root that cannot change (a `let`, a read parameter or loan, a read `self`), whatever its type | `copy p`, `alias p` or `move p` (the record carries an edit); for a loan, `let v = xs.get(0)` then `copy v`, or `match … { present(w) => copy w … }`; for a receiver, declare it `let mut` or take it `editable` (X-345: then it needs no marker) | [07](07-ownership.md), [records](records.md) |
| E-OWN-002 | LANG-07-08 | LR 7.5, LR 7.6, LR 7.8  | `copy` of a non-copyable place (`Shared`, `Weak`, a resource); a loan of a value that is not Copyable where an owned value is expected, which has no owned copy (D-341) | `retain()` for `Shared`/`Weak`; keep the loan (a read parameter, a `from` result) or take the value out of its owner (`pop`, `move`) | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| E-OWN-010 | LANG-07-05 | LR 7.3, LR 8.3 | a conflicting loan: an exclusive loan while other loans are active; two `editable` captures of one owner | end the earlier loan by closing a block | [07](07-ownership.md), [08](08-functions.md) |
| E-OWN-011 | LANG-07-05 | LR 7.3, LR 8.3 | the owner used while loaned (suspended by an exclusive child, frozen by a read child) | use it after the loan's block ends | [07](07-ownership.md), [08](08-functions.md) |
| E-OWN-012 | LANG-07-04 | LR 5.7, LR 7.3 | a later argument moves, assigns or exclusively loans a place an earlier argument reserved | evaluate the conflicting argument into a binding first | [05](05-statements.md) |
| E-OWN-020 | LANG-07-04 | LR 7.4, LR 7.5 | use after move | `copy` before the move, or re-initialise a `let mut` | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| E-OWN-030 | LANG-06-07 | LR 6.11 | a `trivial class` with a non-trivial field | drop `trivial`, or make the field trivial | [06](06-types.md) |
| E-OWN-040 | LANG-07-01 | LR 7.2, LR C.2, LR 7.5  | a partial move | move the whole value; destructure it with `let Name(…) = move p` | [07](07-ownership.md), [C](appendix-c-lowering.md) |
| E-OWN-050 | LANG-07-06 | LR 7.6 | a result borrowing from two parameters | return an owned value, or split the function | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| E-OWN-051 | LANG-07-06 | LR 7.6 | returning a loan of a local or a temporary; a value of the function's own returned where the result is declared `from` a parameter, which must lend: `move d`, a copy, a fresh value, a tuple or record literal, a constructor, a lambda, a call whose result is owned, or a `??`, `if` or `match` any of whose results is one of these, at any depth (D-373, D-377, D-381) | return an owned value (`move`); for a `from` result, bind the loan and return an owned value from a function whose result is owned (`let v = xs.get(0)` then `return copy v ?? move d`), or lend on every path | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| E-OWN-052 | LANG-07-04 | LR 7.3, LR 12.1 | a `defer` body using a binding of its block that holds a loan | use the owner, or move the deferred work | [12](12-async.md) |
| E-OWN-053 | LANG-07-06 | LR 7.7, LR C.2 | a lifetime parameter, or a field of a loan or loan-carrying type (not `from static`) | own the value, copy it, hold a `Shared`, or pass it per call | [07](07-ownership.md), [C](appendix-c-lowering.md) |

## Unsupported shape (E-OWN-090; LR 7.10)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Obligation (E-OBL, E-ERR-001; LR 5.4)

| Code | Rule | LR | Trigger | Correction | Pairs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E-OBL-001 | LANG-10-01 | LR 5.5, LR 6.12, LR 10.1, LR 11.8, LR 12.3, LR 12.4 | a linear value dropped, overwritten or discarded (an `Outcome`, `Failure`, `Future`, `Task`, `Must`; a never-polled future holding nothing linear and no exclusive loan may be discarded, LR 12.3); an unconsumed linear `owned` parameter on a failing `before` path | `or fail`, `or recover v`, `catch`, `match`, `report`, `await`, launch, or pass it on | [10](10-outcomes.md), [05](05-statements.md) |
| E-OBL-002 | LANG-10-01 | LR 10.4, LR 10.1  | a `catch` block path that does not end in `recover`, `return`, `fail` or a `Never` call | end every path | [10](10-outcomes.md) |
| E-OBL-005 | LANG-06-09 | LR 6.12, LR 12.4 | a linear value live across a cancellation point (`await`), or at an `or fail`, that does not implement `Abandonable` | consume it before the `await`, or pass it into the awaited call | [12](12-async.md) |
| E-OBL-006 | LANG-10-02 | LR 8.3, LR 10.7 | a `fn` or `fn mut` closure capturing a linear value by `move` | declare it `fn once` | [08](08-functions.md) |
| E-OBL-007 | LANG-10-02 | LR 9.2, LR 10.7 | `...move p` drops a linear field the target lacks | give the target the field, or consume it first | [09](09-classes.md) |
| E-OBL-008 | LANG-11-09 | LR 11.8 | an `after` hook that may fail when `R` is linear | do not fail in `after`, or return a non-linear type | [11](11-effects.md) |
| E-ERR-001 | LANG-10-01 | LR 5.4, LR 10.2 | `fail` outside a `try` function | declare the function `try` | [05](05-statements.md), [10](10-outcomes.md) |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E-EFF-001 | LANG-11-01 | LR 11.1, LR 11.2 | the summary exceeds the claims: an effect in `pure`, an allocation in `noalloc`, `suspend` without `async`, `fail` without `try`, `recovers` without `recovers` (the record names the claim's rule) | remove the effect, or write the modifier the summary needs | [11](11-effects.md), [C](appendix-c-lowering.md) |
| E-EFF-010 | LANG-11-07 | LR 11.6, LR 4.6 | `io` through a capability with no `Authority` parameter; `Host.capabilities()` outside `main`, twice, or in a `main` that takes capability parameters | take the capability as a parameter; give `main` the capabilities as parameters (`func main(console: Console)`) instead of calling `Host.capabilities()` | [11](11-effects.md) |

| E-EFF-040 | LANG-11-05 | LR 11.3 | warning from `fortis check --api-baseline OLD`: an exported function lost a written `pure`/`noalloc` or gained `async`/`try`/`recovers` | restore the claim, or make the API change deliberately | [11](11-effects.md) |

# Overview: design invariants and notation (LR 1, LR 2)

<!-- covers: LR 1, LR 2 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [A tour of Fortis](../guide/tour.md). Source of truth: LR 1 and LR 2.*

LR 1 and LR 2 state no numbered rules; they fix the invariants every later rule serves. Write code so that each of
these is visible on the line.

## Invariants

| Invariant | Consequence when writing code | LR |
|---|---|---|
| Every local decision is visible: ownership operations, mutation permission, failure disposition, effect claims, observation points. | Never rely on inference for these; write the marker, modifier or handler. A marker the declaration already shows is left out: an `editable self` call on a `let mut` binding, `return local` (LR 7.5). | LR 1 |
| Imported signatures can never be weaker than their bodies. | Read the callee's signature (`fortis view --symbol`) instead of its body. | LR 1 |
| Library-first: program = packages, package = modules, module = one file; HTTP, data, web UI, telemetry, jobs are kits (libraries). | The core imports nothing from kits. | LR 1 |
| Explicit ownership: assigning or passing an existing owned value states `copy`, `alias` or `move`; mutable access is `editable`. No hidden clones or reference counts. | See [ownership](07-ownership.md). | LR 1 |
| Three distinct answers: `T?`, `Bool`, `Outcome[T]` with `??`, `\|\|`, `or`. Nothing is truthy. | Compare explicitly (`x != null`, `n != 0`). | LR 1 |
| Linear failures: an outcome is consumed exactly once (`or fail`, `or recover`, `catch`, `match`, `report`); dropping one is a compile error. | Every call to a `try` function is followed by a disposition; in a `test` or `property` body `or fail` is implied (LR 14). | LR 1 |
| Closed effect set: `pure`, `noalloc`, `async`, `try` are checked claims over eight effects; contracts are conjunctions of them. | See [effects](11-effects.md). | LR 1 |
| Lexical loans; synchronous `defer`; one cancellation point (`await`); structured `scope`. | End a loan early by closing a block. | LR 1 |
| Two backends, one semantics: development VM and safe-Rust native code run the same checked IR. | Never depend on backend behaviour. | LR 1 |
| Absent by design: scripting semantics, runtime reflection, inheritance, macros, exceptions, implicit conversions. | Do not emulate them. | LR 1 |

## Notation

Every non-alphabetic symbol and what it answers (LR 1.1):

| Notation | Meaning | Never |
|---|---|---|
| `{ }` | block, record literal, record type | |
| `( )` | call, parameter list, tuple, grouping | |
| `Name[ ]` | generic arguments after an uppercase name | |
| `place[ ]` | index after a lowercase place | slices |
| `fn[ ]` | a lambda's capture list, only when non-empty | `fn[]` |
| `+ - * / %` `<< >>` `& \| ^` | arithmetic and bitwise; proof-required on integers | overloading |
| `== !=` `< <= > >=` | `Equatable`, `Comparable`; IEEE comparison on floats | chained comparisons |
| `&& \|\|` `!` | Boolean logic | truthiness |
| `+=` and friends | `x = x op e` | |
| `< >` after a type | refinement (type position only) | |
| `:` | has type, named argument, record field, label | ternary, slicing |
| `=` | assignment, `let` initialiser | equality |
| `=>` | expression body of a function, lambda or match arm | map literals |
| `.` | member access, module paths | ranges |
| `..` `..<` | integer ranges in `for` headers and refinements | |
| `?` `?.` | optional type suffix, optional chaining | error propagation |
| `??` | absent-value fallback | |
| `@name(args)` | apply an aspect, on the lines above a function head | contracts |
| `${ }` | string interpolation | |
| `//` | comment; documentation directly above a declaration | `///`, `/* */` |
| `,` | list separator | |
| `...` | spread a place into a constructor; forward remaining aspect arguments | |

Keywords that carry a decision (LR 1.1): `let` (new name), `mut` (changes), `copy`/`alias`/`move`/`editable`
(how a place is used), `owned`/`editable` on a parameter, `try`/`pure`/`noalloc`/`async`/`recovers` and named
contracts in the modifier position, `or fail`/`or recover`/`catch`, `give`, `export`.

Silence (LR 1.1): an unmarked argument, or the receiver of a `self` method, is a read loan ending when the call
returns (or with the future of an `async` call); an unmarked `for` source is a read loan for the loop; an unmarked
assignment is a fresh or trivial value. The unmarked receiver of an `editable self` method, or a `fn mut` being
called, is the exclusive loan its root's declaration shows (`let mut`, `editable`), and `return local` moves the
local (LR 7.5).

Removed, never write (LR 1.1): semicolons; `///`, `/* */`; `yield`; `or die`; `nostate`; `self: editable Self`
(write `editable self`); `alias editable` (write `editable`); `alias type` (a `type` is always nominal); `within`;
`give` in a single-expression arm; `fn[]`; `::`; operator overloading; implicit `it`; postfix `?` for errors; `new`
(name constructors `create`, `of`, `from`); `return` in an expression-bodied function.

Two deliberate costs (LR 1.1): `(f() or fail).amount` needs parentheses, so write `let v = f() or fail` on its own
line; an `async` call builds a `Future`, and `await` or `launch` is the visible point where it runs.

Formatted source shows every inferred fact (closure kind, loan modes, a contract's modifiers), except a lambda's
inferred `pure`/`noalloc`, which the function type it is passed to states (LR 1.1, LR 8.2). `fortis fmt --write`
also rewrites older forms into the forms these pages teach where the meaning is unchanged; run it before review.

## Correction patterns: notation from other languages

All of these are `E-SYN-000` (LR 3.2), a sentence outside the grammar of LR 1.1's notation.

### Postfix `?` for errors (LR 1.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-000
try func parse(n: Int) Int => n

try func twice(n: Int) Int {
  let v = parse(n)?                   // reject: E-SYN-000
  return v
}

test "twice" {
  expect twice(2) == 2
}
```

```fortis
// accept
try func parse(n: Int) Int => n

try func twice(n: Int) Int {
  let v = parse(n) or fail
  return v
}

test "twice" {
  expect twice(2) == 2
}
```

### Empty capture list (LR 1.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-000
pure func countPositive(items: List[Int]) Int {
  let positive = fn[](n: Int) Bool => n > 0    // reject: E-SYN-000
  return items.countWhere(positive)
}

test "countPositive" {
  expect countPositive(List.of(1, -2, 3)) == 2
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func countPositive(items: List[Int]) Int {
  let positive = pure noalloc fn(n: Int) Bool => n > 0
  return items.countWhere(positive)
}

test "countPositive" {
  expect countPositive(List.of(1, -2, 3)) == 2
}
```

### `return` in an expression body (LR 1.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-000
pure func double(n: Int<0..100>) Int => return n * 2    // reject: E-SYN-000

test "double" {
  expect double(2) == 4
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func double(n: Int<0..100>) Int => n * 2

test "double" {
  expect double(2) == 4
}
```

### `::` paths and `new` (LR 1.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-000
class Point {
  export x: Int
}

pure func origin() Point => Point::new(0)     // reject: E-SYN-000

test "origin" {
  expect origin().x == 0
}
```

```fortis
// accept
class Point {
  export x: Int
  export pure func of(x: Int) Point => Point(x)
}

pure func origin() Point => Point.of(0)

test "origin" {
  expect origin().x == 0
}
```

## The worked module (LR 2)

LR 2 is one module that uses every construct; [the tour](../guide/tour.md) has a self-contained counterpart that
runs. Its constructs, by section:

| Construct in LR 2 | Example | LR |
|---|---|---|
| imports: aliased module, braced members | `import fortis.text`, `import fortis.money { Money, Currency }` | LR 4.3 |
| nominal refined newtype | `export type CustomerId = Int<1..>` | LR 6.9, LR 6.3 |
| class with exported and private fields, generated constructor | `export class Line derive Equatable { … }` | LR 9.1, LR 9.2 |
| refined field type | `quantity: Int<1..10000>` | LR 6.3 |
| method modes | `total(self)`, `issue(editable self, …)` | LR 9.3, LR 7.6 |
| enum with payloads | `Issued(at: Timestamp)` | LR 9.7 |
| declared failure with payload and template | `export error CurrencyMismatch { … }` | LR 10.3 |
| interface, mixin with `requires` | `Renderable`, `Summarised` | LR 9.5, LR 9.6 |
| fallible associated constructor | `pure try func create(…) Invoice` with `fail` | LR 9.2, LR 10.1 |
| `or fail` propagation, return of a local (a move) | `let lineTotal = line.total() or fail`, `return sum` | LR 10.2, LR 7.5 |
| `editable self` call on a `let mut` binding, unmarked | `out.appendLine(…)` | LR 7.5 |
| exhaustive `match` with payload bindings | `Paid(at: paidAt, reference: ref) => …` | LR 9.8 |
| closure with explicit kind and capture | `pure fn[alias threshold](line: Line) Bool { … }` | LR 8.2, LR 8.3 |
| `defer`, `catch` with `report` and `recover`, `recovers` | `withAudit` | LR 12.1, LR 10.4 |
| tests, table test with `as row` | `test "quantity boundary" cases { … } as row { … }` | LR 14 |
| entry point in another package, capabilities as parameters | `try func main(console: Console)` | LR 4.6 |

---
source: docs/agent/03-lexical.md
---

# Lexical structure (LR 3)

<!-- covers: LR 3 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Lexical structure](../guide/03-lexical.md). Source of truth: LR 3.*

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-03-01 | A `;` outside strings, comments and raw template regions is a parse error (`E-SYN-001`). There is no semicolon token and no automatic insertion. | LR 3.2 |
| LANG-03-02 | A newline ends a statement unless (a) it is inside `(…)`, `[…]` or `{…}` of the same expression or argument list, (b) the line ends with a trailing continuation token, or (c) the next line starts with a leading continuation token. Refinement `<` `>` are not continuation tokens. | LR 3.2 |
| LANG-03-03 | Uppercase first letter: type, interface, mixin, enum, variant, contract, error kind, observation schema. Lowercase or `_`: value, function, method, field, parameter, module alias, label. Decided lexically, no symbol table. | LR 3.3 |
| LANG-03-04 | Every keyword of LR Appendix A is reserved in every declaration and binding position (`E-SYN-002`), including the kit heads; a keyword is a valid name after `.` and as a method or associated-function name. | LR 3.4 |
| LANG-03-05 | Literal typing follows the LR 3.5 table; an out-of-range literal is rejected at compile time (`E-REF-001`). | LR 3.5 |
| LANG-03-06 | Each interpolated expression is evaluated once, left to right, must be `Displayable`, and must not be fallible or suspending. | LR 3.6 |

## Token facts

| Fact | LR |
|---|---|
| Source: UTF-8, extension `.ft`; identifiers ASCII `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`; Unicode only in strings, comments and data; a byte-order mark is rejected. | LR 3.1 |
| Quotas: a file over 16 MiB or 2,000,000 tokens, or nesting of brackets, blocks, prefix operators or interpolations deeper than 256, is `E-LIM-002` and is not parsed. | LR 3.1 |
| Trailing continuation tokens: `,` `(` `[` `=` `=>` `+` `-` `*` `/` `%` `<<` `>>` `&` `\|` `^` `&&` `\|\|` `??` `==` `!=` `<` `<=` `>` `>=` `..` `..<` `.` | LR 3.2 |
| Leading continuation tokens: `.` `or` `catch` `??` `else` `)` `]` `with` `where` `implements` `derive` `from` | LR 3.2 |
| Body brace (statement block or declaration body) vs expression brace (record literal or type): decided by the token before `{`; expression brace after `=`, `(`, `,`, `:`, `[`, `??`, `==`, `!=`, a compound assignment, `return`, `give`, `fail`, `recover`. A body may be one line: `{ statement }`. | LR 3.2 |
| `return`, `fail`, `give` take their operand on the same line; a bare `return` on its own line returns `Void`. | LR 3.2 |
| Parsing decisions P1 (one `NL` per run of blank/comment lines), P2 (longest chains), P3 (alternatives in grammar order) are normative for any parser. | LR 3.2 |
| Integer literal: decimal, `0x`, `0b`, `0o`, `_` separators; type from context, default `Int`. Float: needs `.` or exponent; `f32` suffix gives `Float32`. Decimal: `d` suffix. Duration: `ms` `s` `min` `h`. | LR 3.5 |
| `"text"` is `StringView from static`; `"a ${x}"` is a fresh `String` that a binding annotated `StringView` cannot hold (`E-TYP-040`); `"""raw"""` is `StringView from static`, no escapes, no interpolation; `b"abc"` is `BytesView from static`; `null` is the absent case of `T?`. | LR 3.5 |
| Interpolation takes a read loan of the places it names; it never escapes for HTML or any other context. | LR 3.6 |
| Comments: only `//`. Documentation is the `//` run directly above a declaration with no blank line between. A fenced `fortis` block in documentation needs a first-line marker (`// accept`, `// reject: CODE`, `// execute: R`, `// illustrative`). | LR 3.7 |

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-SYN-001 | `;` in code | delete it (the record carries the edit) | LR 3.2 |
| E-SYN-000 | not a sentence of the grammar: a line starting with a binary operator, `/* */`, a byte-order mark, a top-level statement | move the operator to the end of the previous line; use `//`; remove the mark | LR 3.2 |
| E-SYN-002 | keyword used as a declaration, binding or parameter name (`match`, `state`, `view`, `model`, …) | rename; keywords are valid only after `.` and as method or associated-function names | LR 3.4 |
| E-REF-001 | literal outside its target type or refinement | change the literal or widen the declared type | LR 3.5 |
| E-TYP-040 | interpolated expression not `Displayable` (including an `Outcome` from a fallible call); interpolated literal bound to a `StringView` | bind the result first (`let v = f() or fail`, then `${v}`); annotate `String` | LR 3.5 |
| E-LIM-002 | source over the size, token or nesting quota | split the file or reduce nesting | LR 3.1 |

## Correction patterns

### E-SYN-001: semicolon (LR 3.2)

The record carries a correction, an edit that deletes the semicolon; apply it as given.

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-001
pure func pair() Int {
  let a = 1; let b = 2           // reject: E-SYN-001
  return a + b
}

test "pair" {
  expect pair() == 3
}
```

```output
example.ft:3:12: error E-SYN-001 [LANG-03-01] (Syntax, violated): ';' is not a token
    expected_tokens: []
    found_token: ";"
    correction: delete the semicolon
      example.ft:3:12-3:13 -> ""
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func pair() Int {
  let a = 1
  let b = 2
  return a + b
}

test "pair" {
  expect pair() == 3
}
```

### E-SYN-000: binary operator at the start of a line (LR 3.2)

Binary operators continue a line only when they are last on it.

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-000
pure func total(a: Int<0..100>, b: Int<0..100>) Int {
  let sum = a
    + b                          // reject: E-SYN-000
  return sum
}

test "total" {
  expect total(1, 2) == 3
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func total(a: Int<0..100>, b: Int<0..100>) Int {
  let sum = a +
    b
  return sum
}

test "total" {
  expect total(1, 2) == 3
}
```

Leading `.`, `or`, `catch`, `??` and `else` do continue a line:

```fortis
// accept
pure try func half(n: Int) Int {
  if n % 2 != 0 { return 0 }
  return Int.div(n, 2) or fail
}

pure recovers func pipeline(fallback: Int?) Int {
  let n = fallback
    ?? 7
  let h = half(n)
    or recover -1
  return h
}

test "pipeline" {
  expect pipeline(null) == 0
  expect pipeline(10) == 5
}
```

### E-SYN-002: keyword as a name (LR 3.4)

Kit head words (`state`, `view`, `model`, `component`, `context`, `action`, `resource`, `inject`, `provide`, …)
are reserved like every other keyword.

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-002
pure func size(state: Int) Int => state     // reject: E-SYN-002

test "size" {
  expect size(1) == 1
}
```

```records
{"class": "Syntax", "code": "E-SYN-002", "column": 16, "fields": {"expected_tokens": ["lowerIdent"], "found_token": "state"}, "file": "example.ft", "line": 2, "message": "keyword 'state' used as an identifier", "rule": "LANG-03-04", "severity": "error", "status": "violated"}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func size(current: Int) Int => current

test "size" {
  expect size(1) == 1
}
```

A keyword is allowed as a method or associated-function name and after `.`:

```fortis
// accept
class Celsius {
  export degrees: Int
  export pure func from(degrees: Int) Celsius => Celsius(degrees)
}

test "from" {
  expect Celsius.from(21).degrees == 21
}
```

### E-REF-001: literal out of range (LR 3.5)

```fortis
// reject: E-REF-001
pure func percent() Int<0..100> {
  let p: Int<0..100> = 101       // reject: E-REF-001
  return 100
}

test "percent" {
  expect percent() == 101
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func percent() Int<0..100> {
  let p: Int<0..100> = 100
  return p
}

test "percent" {
  expect percent() == 100
}
```

### E-TYP-040: interpolation (LR 3.5, LR 3.6)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-040
try func risky(n: Int) Int => n

try func label(n: Int) String {
  return "value ${risky(n)}"     // reject: E-TYP-040
}

test "label" {
  expect label(2) == "value 2"
}
```

```fortis
// accept
try func risky(n: Int) Int => n

try func label(n: Int) String {
  let v = risky(n) or fail
  return "value ${v}"
}

test "label" {
  expect label(2) == "value 2"
}
```

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-040
pure func greeting(name: StringView) Int {
  let text: StringView = "hello, ${name}"     // reject: E-TYP-040
  return text.byteCount()
}

test "greeting" {
  expect greeting("ada") == 10
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func greeting(name: StringView) Int {
  let text: String = "hello, ${name}"
  return text.byteCount()
}

test "greeting" {
  expect greeting("ada") == 10
}
```

## Facts used when writing code

- Order: interpolated expressions run once each, left to right with the string (LR 3.6).
- A string literal is free (`StringView from static`); converting it to `String` where a `String` is expected
  allocates and is the one implicit conversion (LR 6.6).
- A byte string literal `b"…"` is a `BytesView from static`; read bytes with `get(index) Byte?` and
  `byteCount()` (LR 3.5, LR 6.6).
- Documentation comments are `//` runs directly above a declaration; `fortis view --decls` lists them (LR 3.7).

---
source: docs/agent/04-modules.md
---

# Modules and packages (LR 4)

<!-- covers: LR 4 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Modules and packages](../guide/04-modules.md). Source of truth: LR 4.*

> Preview: dependencies and lock files (LR 4.1) arrive in v0.2. An async entry point (LR 4.6, LR 12.3) arrives in v0.3. One package, its modules, imports, visibility and the ordinary entry point (LR 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5 and 4.6) are in v0.0.1.

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-04-01 | A module is one file under `src/`; its path is its identity (`src/a/b.ft` is `a.b`, imported from another package as `PKG.a.b`). A module holds only declarations and `const` bindings with compile-time constant initialisers. | LR 4.2 |
| LANG-04-02 | Importing a module executes no code (there is no module initialisation). | LR 4.2 |
| LANG-04-03 | Across packages, only modules listed in the exporting package's `exports:` may be imported. | LR 4.3 |
| LANG-04-04 | Two versions of one package are two packages; a type's identity is its name, package, version and declaring module, so same-named types of two modules or versions never interchange. | LR 4.1 |
| LANG-04-05 | A `let` may not shadow a visible binding (`E-NAM-003`). | LR 4.5 |
| LANG-04-06 | The entry point is the `main` of the manifest's `entry` module, exported or not, with one of the four heads of LR 4.6, each optionally `recovers` (X-155; refused in packages today, D-52); each parameter is `List[String]` or a capability type, each type once (`E-NAM-005`, `E-NAM-006`), supplied by the runtime by its type (X-345). | LR 4.6 |

## Package and import facts

| Fact | LR |
|---|---|
| Package = directory with `project.yaml`, lockfile `fortis.lock`, `src/`. Manifest keys: `schema: fortis.project/v1`, `name`, `version`, `exports: [modules]`, `dependencies: {name: "version"}`, optional `entry: module` (application), optional `root: module`. | LR 4.1 |
