# Functions and closures (LR 8)

<!-- covers: LR 8 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Functions and closures](../guide/08-functions.md). Source of truth: LR 8.*

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-08-01 | Every parameter has a type and the success type is written, except that a function or method head leaves out `Void` and a lambda's are inferred as LR 8.2 allows; modifiers in the order `[export] [Contract …] [pure] [noalloc] [async] [try] [recovers] func`; aspects on the lines above. | LR 8.1 |
| LANG-08-02 | A lambda writes its kind (`fn`, `fn mut`, `fn once`) and its capture list (brackets only when non-empty); a body needing a stronger kind than declared is rejected. | LR 8.2 |
| LANG-08-03 | A name not in the capture list is inaccessible in the lambda body. | LR 8.3 |
| LANG-08-04 | Callable assignability: kind `fn` ≤ `fn mut` ≤ `fn once`; parameter modes match exactly; modifiers at least as strong; an owned closure's region at least as long. The backend boxes a closure only where `dynamic fn` is written. | LR 8.4 |

## Facts

- Expression body: `func f(x: T) R => expr`, exactly one expression (LR 8.1).
- A `Void` result is left out of every function and method head, expression bodies and `cleanup` included:
  `func reset(c: editable Counter) { … }`. A function type keeps it (`fn(Int) Void`), and so does a block-bodied
  lambda. Older code writes `) Void {`; `fortis fmt` drops it (LR 8.1).
- A named function is not a value; its name where a callable is expected becomes a non-capturing `fn` of the
  matching type (LR 8.1).
- `try`, `async`, `recovers` must be written when the summary has them (functions and lambdas); `pure` and
  `noalloc` are optional claims, inferred for lambdas; the formatter prints no inferred one back on a lambda and
  keeps one the author wrote (the callee's function type states them and the checker enforces it there) (LR 8.1,
  LR 8.2, X-345).
- Lambda shape below; `=> expr` for an expression body; a block body writes its return type, an expression body
  may leave it out: it is the callee's (or annotation's) result type when that names one, else the body's type
  widened as an unannotated `let` (LR 8.2, X-345); parameter types may be omitted only when passed directly to a
  parameter of known function type; lambdas are not generic (LR 8.2).

```fortis
// illustrative
[pure] [noalloc] [async] [try] [recovers] fn[captures](params) ReturnType { body }
fn(params) ReturnType => expression
fn(params) => expression
```

- Kinds (LR 8.2):

  | Kind | Captures may be | Call | Binding | Lowers to |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `fn` | `copy`, `alias`, `move` (read-only use) | `f(x)` | `let` | `Fn` |
  | `fn mut` | plus `editable`, and mutated `move` captures | `f(x)`, an exclusive loan of `f` | `let mut` | `FnMut` |
  | `fn once` | plus `move` captures moved out | `move f(x)`, once | `let` | `FnOnce` |

- A `fn mut` call needs no `editable` where the binding shows it may change (`let mut`, an `editable` parameter or
  capture), and is checked as the marked call; through a `let` it is `E-OWN-001`, marked or not. Older code writes
  `editable f(x)` (LR 8.2, LR 7.5).
- A `move` capture alone does not require `fn once`; moving the captured value out does (LR 8.2).
- Capture entries: `copy x`, `alias x`, `editable x`, `move x`; a trivial value may be bare (`[n]` = copy).
  Evaluated left to right when the lambda is evaluated. Module `const`s, functions and types are not captures
  (LR 8.3).
- Capturing a field path (`alias self.lines`) captures that path and loans the root owner for the closure's
  lifetime; two `editable` captures of one owner, or `editable` plus any other capture of it, conflict (LR 8.3).
- A loan-holding closure passed to a plain `fn` parameter is a read loan for the call: no region in the type.
  Owned positions (`owned fn` parameter, return) must name its region: `fn(Int) Bool from limit`; a field never
  holds one (LR 8.3, LR 7.7).
- A closure capturing a linear value by `move` is linear: it must be `fn once` and be called exactly once on every
  path, or passed to an `owned fn once` parameter (LR 8.3).
- `fn() (StringView from s) from s`: when the result is loan-carrying, `from` after it belongs to the result; the
  closure's own region goes on a parenthesised result (LR 8.4).
- `dynamic fn(…) R`: boxed, owned, allocates on creation; the only way to hold closures of different concrete
  types in one collection (LR 8.4).

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-FUN-010 | the body needs a stronger kind than declared (a `fn` mutates a capture, a `fn mut` moves one out); reported at the use, with a `correction` edit to the kind | strengthen the kind (`fn` → `fn mut` → `fn once`) | LR 8.2 |
| E-FUN-011 | a name used in the body is not in the capture list | add the capture with the right marker | LR 8.3 |
| E-OWN-010 | two captures of one owner where one is `editable` | capture once, or narrow to disjoint field paths read-only | LR 8.3 |
| E-OBL-006 | a `fn` or `fn mut` captures a linear value by `move` | declare `fn once` and call it once with `move f()` | LR 8.3 |
| E-OWN-001 | a `fn mut` called through a binding that cannot change (a `let`), marked or not; a `fn once` call without `move` | hold the `fn mut` in a `let mut` and call `f(…)`; write `move f(…)` | LR 7.5 |
| E-OWN-020 | a `fn once` called a second time (the first call moved it) | call it once; restructure | LR 7.4 |
| E-OWN-011 | a captured place used while the closure holds an exclusive loan of it | end the closure's block before using the place | LR 8.3 |

Modifiers appear in exactly the order of LR 8.1; any other order is a canonicalisation error that the formatter
fixes (LR 8.1). Today's tools disagree with that rule: both checkers report an out-of-order head as `E-SYN-000`
(LR 3.2) and `fortis fmt` refuses the file, a disagreement recorded in X-153 and D-59. Write modifiers in order.

## Correction patterns

### E-FUN-010: kind too weak (LR 8.2)

```fortis
// reject: E-FUN-010
func countCalls() Int {
  let mut calls = 0
  {
    let bump = fn[editable calls]() Void {
      calls = Int.saturatingAdd(calls, 1)        // reject: E-FUN-010
    }
  }
  return calls
}

test "calls" {
  expect countCalls() == 0
}
```

```fortis
// accept
func countCalls() Int {
  let mut calls = 0
  {
    let mut bump = fn mut[editable calls]() Void {
      calls = Int.saturatingAdd(calls, 1)
    }
    bump()
    bump()
  }
  return calls
}

test "calls" {
  expect countCalls() == 2
}
```

### E-FUN-011: missing capture (LR 8.3)

```fortis
// reject: E-FUN-011
pure func countAbove(items: List[Int], limit: Int) Int {
  return items.countWhere(fn(n: Int) Bool => n > limit)    // reject: E-FUN-011
}

test "above" {
  expect countAbove(List.of(1, 5, 9), 4) == 2
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func countAbove(items: List[Int], limit: Int) Int {
  return items.countWhere(fn[limit](n: Int) Bool => n > limit)
}

test "above" {
  expect countAbove(List.of(1, 5, 9), 4) == 2
}
```

### E-OWN-001: `fn mut` called through a binding that cannot change (LR 7.5, LR 8.2)

A `fn mut` held by a `let mut` binding is called as `add(item)`; held by a `let`, it cannot be called at all.

```fortis
// reject: E-OWN-001
func sum(items: List[Int]) Int {
  let mut total = 0
  {
    let add = fn mut[editable total](n: Int) Void {
      total = Int.saturatingAdd(total, n)
    }
    for item in items {
      add(item)                                   // reject: E-OWN-001
    }
  }
  return total
}

test "sum" {
  expect sum(List.of(1, 2, 3)) == 6
}
```

```fortis
// accept
func sum(items: List[Int]) Int {
  let mut total = 0
  {
    let mut add = fn mut[editable total](n: Int) Void {
      total = Int.saturatingAdd(total, n)
    }
    for item in items {
      add(item)
    }
  }
  return total
}

test "sum" {
  expect sum(List.of(1, 2, 3)) == 6
}
```

### E-OWN-010: conflicting captures (LR 8.3)

```fortis
// reject: E-OWN-010
func reset() Int {
  let mut count = 5
  {
    let mut both = fn mut[editable count, alias count]() Void {   // reject: E-OWN-010
      count = 0
    }
    both()
  }
  return count
}

test "reset" {
  expect reset() == 0
}
```

```fortis
// accept
func reset() Int {
  let mut count = 5
  {
    let mut clear = fn mut[editable count]() Void {
      count = 0
    }
    clear()
  }
  return count
}

test "reset" {
  expect reset() == 0
}
```

### E-OBL-006: a linear capture in a repeatable closure (LR 8.3)

The `fn mut` below also never consumes what it owns, so its binding is dropped with an obligation: `E-OBL-001`
on the same line (LR 6.12).

```fortis
// reject: E-OBL-006, E-OBL-001
export error Oops {
  code: "demo.oops"
}

pure try func risky(n: Int) Int {
  if n > 9 {
    fail Oops()
  }
  return n
}

pure recovers func later(n: Int) Int {
  let pending = risky(n)
  let mut run = fn mut[move pending]() Int {        // reject: E-OBL-006, E-OBL-001
    return 0
  }
  return run()
}

test "later" {
  expect later(3) == 3
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export error Oops {
  code: "demo.oops"
}

pure try func risky(n: Int) Int {
  if n > 9 {
    fail Oops()
  }
  return n
}

pure recovers func later(n: Int) Int {
  let pending = risky(n)
  let run = fn once[move pending]() Int {
    return move pending or recover 0
  }
  return move run()
}

test "later" {
  expect later(3) == 3
  expect later(12) == 0
}
```

### A loan-holding closure in an owned position needs its region (LR 8.3, LR 8.4)

A returned closure that holds a loan names its region in the return type (`fn(Int) Bool from limit`); without it
the function is rejected (LR 8.3). Which code reports that is not yet settled (X-152): the record names the place
and asks for `… from limit`.

```fortis
// accept
class Limit {
  export value: Int
}

func above(limit: Limit) fn(Int) Bool from limit {
  return fn[alias limit](n: Int) Bool => n > limit.value
}

test "above" {
  let limit = Limit(value: 3)
  let check = above(alias limit)
  expect check(5)
  expect !check(2)
}
```

### Callback purity (LR 8.4)

A non-`pure` callable where `pure fn` is required is a type mismatch (`expected_type` `pure fn(…)`).

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-040
import fortis.host { Console }

pure func applyPure(f: pure fn(Int) Int, x: Int) Int => f(x)

func logged(console: Console, n: Int) Int {
  console.print("called")
  return n
}

func run(console: Console) {
  discard applyPure(fn[alias console](n: Int) Int => logged(console, n), 1)   // reject: E-TYP-040
}

test "run" {
  expect true
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func applyPure(f: pure fn(Int) Int, x: Int) Int => f(x)

pure func double(n: Int) Int => Int.saturatingMul(n, 2)

test "run" {
  expect applyPure(double, 4) == 8
  expect applyPure(fn(n: Int) Int => Int.saturatingAdd(n, 1), 4) == 5
}
```

---
source: docs/agent/09-classes.md
---

# Classes, interfaces, mixins and enums (LR 9)

<!-- covers: LR 9 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Classes, interfaces, mixins and enums](../guide/09-classes.md). Source of truth: LR 9.*

> Preview: interfaces and mixins (LR 9.5, 9.6) arrive in v0.1. Classes, cleanup, enums and match (LR 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 9.7 and 9.8) are in v0.0.1.

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-09-01 | No inheritance, no runtime member lookup, no reflection-based construction. | LR 9.1 |
| LANG-09-02 | The generated constructor `Name(field: v, …)` is callable only where every field is visible; private fields are settable only inside the module. | LR 9.2 |
| LANG-09-03 | An implementation may not strengthen a precondition (narrower parameter refinement) or weaken a guarantee (drop `pure`, add `try`/`async`, widen a return refinement); coherence: implement only in the package defining the interface or the type, at most one implementation per (interface, type). | LR 9.5 |
| LANG-09-04 | Mixins require methods only, add no fields, constructors or `cleanup`; a method name provided by two applied mixins and not declared by the class is rejected. | LR 9.6 |
| LANG-09-05 | `match` over a closed type (enum, optional) is exhaustive without `otherwise`; each missing variant is named. | LR 9.8 |
| LANG-09-06 | Pattern ownership: `match p` takes a read loan and binds read loans; `match move p` consumes and binds owned values; a match of a fresh value owns it; a linear payload needs the owning form and must be consumed. | LR 9.8 |

## Facts

- Class shape: `[export] [trivial] class Name[T] [derive …] [implements …] [with …] { fields, methods,
  associated functions, const, cleanup }`; fields and members private unless `export`; field defaults are constant
  expressions; one namespace for fields, methods, associated functions and constants (LR 9.1).
- Constructor arguments are owned positions: an existing ownership-bearing place needs `copy`/`move`; fields with
  defaults may be omitted. A field may be given by a pun, `Item(sku, wanted)` for `Item(sku: sku, wanted: wanted)`;
  a pun passes the place unmarked, so an owned ownership-bearing local is written `name: move name` (LR 9.2,
  LR 5.8).
- Spread: `Name(...copy p, f: v)` copies same-named fields of matching type (or with `From`), leaves `p`;
  `...move p` consumes `p`, drops untaken fields (never a linear one), and `p` may not have `cleanup`. Order: spread,
  explicit fields left to right, then defaults (LR 9.2).
- Associated function: no `self`, called `Name.f(…)`; the only path to values with private fields; constructors
  are named `create`, `of` or `from` (LR 9.2, LR 1.1).
- `derive Default` on a class gives `Name.default()`, no arguments: each field at its initialiser, a field without
  one at its type's default (`false`, `0`, empty, `null`, a class's own derived default, the `default()` of a type
  that implements `Default`, a newtype's representation's); a field with neither is `E-TYP-090` (a class without
  `Default`, a capability, `Int<1..10>`, an `Array`, `FixedList`, `FixedMap` or `OrderedMap`, also behind a
  newtype, a type parameter `T`). On an enum it is `E-TYP-090`: the enum `implements Default` and its `default()`
  returns the variant. Use it instead of a hand-written `create()` that sets every field empty (LR 6.10, LR 9.2,
  X-345).
- Receivers: `self` (read; call `v.m()`), `editable self` (exclusive; call `p.m()` on a `let mut` binding, an
  `editable` parameter or the method's own `editable self`, as `self.items.push(x)`; elsewhere `E-OWN-001`, LR 7.5), `owned self` (call
  `move p.m()`); fields as `self.field`; associated constants `const c = …` read as `Name.c` (LR 9.3). Older code
  writes `editable p.m()`, which stays accepted.
- A `pure` method may write through `editable self` (its footprint), nothing else (LR 9.3).
- `cleanup(editable self)` runs at destruction before fields drop; not `try`, not `async`, not callable; its
  effects join every function that may drop the type (LR 9.4).
- Interfaces: signatures with modifiers and receiver modes, associated functions, associated constants; no
  bodies, no associated types; `where` on type parameters; `requires` other interfaces (LR 9.5).
- Implementing: `implements I` with every member, `derive I`, or `implement I for T { … }` at module level
  (the form for generic implementations); same names alone never implement (LR 9.5).
- Bundle = requirements, no members: satisfied automatically (`Codec`). Marker = no members, no requirements:
  explicit only (`Authority`). `Copyable`, `Shareable` are structural (LR 9.5).
- `dynamic I`: owned and boxed (allocates on creation); `alias dynamic I` (loan); `Shared[dynamic I]`.
  Dynamic-eligible: no associated types, no generic methods, no `Self` by value. An `async` method through
  `dynamic` allocates its future (LR 9.5).
- Mixin: `requires` method signatures; body checked at each application against the class's exported members
  only; a class method beats a mixin method of the same name (LR 9.6).
- Enum variants UpperCamel, optional named payloads; `E.V`, `E.V(f: x)`; prefix optional in match patterns and
  wherever the expected type is that enum (return, argument, field initialiser, annotated `let`, the right operand
  of `==`/`!=`/`<`… whose left operand is that enum); a variant name where a function type is expected is its
  constructor (LR 9.7). A bare name that is also a class, error or type in scope, or one nothing expects the enum of
  (`let x = Error`, an unannotated `List.of(Error)`), is `E-TYP-040`: write `E.V`, or annotate the binding
  (LR 9.7, X-345).
- Patterns: `name`, `_`, literal, `Variant(…)`, `present(x)`/`null`, `success(x)`/`failure(f)`,
  `is Error(…) [as n]`, `Name(field: p, …)` (consuming only, every field named or `_` for non-linear, no
  `cleanup`), `(p1, p2)`, `{ f: p }`, `otherwise` (open types only: integers, strings, `Failure`). Guards
  `when b`; guarded arms do not count for exhaustiveness. No range patterns, no `x @ p` (LR 9.8).
- Or-patterns: `A | B | C => v` matches when any alternative does, left to right. Alternatives bind nothing
  (`Circle(radius: _)`, literals, `null`, `present(0)`), are never `otherwise`, and the arm takes no `when`
  guard (`E-MAT-003`); each alternative counts for exhaustiveness (`E-MAT-001` for a variant none names), and a
  `_` alternative is a catch-all (`E-MAT-002` over a closed enum). Use them for tables of equal results
  (LR 9.8, X-345).

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-TYP-070 | a name declared twice in one class (fields, methods, associated functions and constants share one namespace) | rename one | LR 9.1 |
| E-NAM-004 | generated constructor called where a field is not visible | call an exported associated function (`create`) | LR 4.4, LR 9.2 |
| E-TYP-050 | constructor call missing a field with no default and no spread source | pass the field | LR 9.2 |
| E-OBL-007 | `...move p` would drop a linear field the target lacks | consume the field first (destructure), or give the target a field for it | LR 9.2 |
| E-TYP-040 | `cleanup` called directly | let destruction run it; expose an explicit method for fallible finalisation | LR 9.4 |
| E-TYP-080 | missing member, incompatible signature (a dropped `pure`, an added `try`), unmet `requires`, unmet mixin requirement | provide the member with the interface's exact contract | LR 9.5 |
| E-TYP-060 | interface requirement cycle | break the cycle | LR 9.5 |
| E-MIX-001 | derive plus a hand-written method the derivation generates; or two mixins provide one method the class does not declare | drop one; declare the method in the class | LR 9.5, LR 9.6 |
| E-TYP-100 | implementation outside the packages defining the interface or the type; two implementations for one type | implement in the owning package; keep one | LR 9.5 |
| E-TYP-090 | `derive` whose rule is not met (a field does not implement the interface) | implement it for the field type, or write the method by hand | LR 6.10 |
| E-MAT-001 | match over a closed type misses variants (one record, each missing variant named) | add an arm per variant | LR 9.8 |
| E-MAT-002 | catch-all (`_`, a bare binding, `otherwise`) as the last arm over a closed enum | name every variant | LR 9.8 |
| E-MAT-003 | an or-pattern alternative binds a name or is `otherwise`, or the arm has a `when` guard | match the binding or guarded cases in arms of their own; `_` for an unused payload | LR 9.8 |

## Correction patterns

### E-TYP-070: field and method share a name (LR 9.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-070
class Account {
  balance: Int
  export pure func balance(self) Int => self.balance        // reject: E-TYP-070
}

test "balance" {
  expect true
}
```

```fortis
// accept
class Account {
  balance: Int
  export pure func current(self) Int => self.balance
}

test "balance" {
  expect Account(balance: 5).current() == 5
}
```

### E-TYP-080: implementation weakens the interface (LR 9.5)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-080
interface Priced {
  pure func price(self) Int
}

class Pear implements Priced {                  // reject: E-TYP-080
  export pure try func price(self) Int => 4
}

test "price" {
  expect true
}
```

```fortis
// accept
interface Priced {
  pure func price(self) Int
}

class Pear implements Priced {
  export pure func price(self) Int => 4
}

test "price" {
  expect Pear().price() == 4
}
```

### E-MIX-001: two mixins provide one method (LR 9.6)

```fortis
// reject: E-MIX-001
mixin English {
  export pure func hello(self) StringView from static => "hello"
}

mixin French {
  export pure func hello(self) StringView from static => "bonjour"
}

class Greeter with English, French {            // reject: E-MIX-001
  export id: Int
}

test "hello" {
  expect true
}
```

```fortis
// accept
mixin English {
  export pure func hello(self) StringView from static => "hello"
}

mixin French {
  export pure func hello(self) StringView from static => "bonjour"
}

class Greeter with English, French {
  export id: Int
  export pure func hello(self) StringView from static => "hi"
}

test "hello" {
  expect Greeter(id: 1).hello() == "hi"
}
```

### E-MAT-001 and E-MAT-002: closed matches (LR 9.8)

`E-MAT-001` is reported at the `match`; `E-MAT-002` at the catch-all arm.

```fortis
// reject: E-MAT-001
enum Light {
  Red
  Amber
  Green
}

pure func code(l: Light) Int {
  return match l {                       // reject: E-MAT-001
    Red => 1
    Amber => 2
  }
}

test "code" {
  expect code(Light.Red) == 1
}
```

```fortis
// reject: E-MAT-002
enum Light {
  Red
  Amber
  Green
}

pure func code(l: Light) Int {
  return match l {
    Red => 1
    otherwise => 2                       // reject: E-MAT-002
  }
}

test "code" {
  expect code(Light.Red) == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
enum Light {
  Red
  Amber
  Green
}

pure func code(l: Light) Int {
  return match l {
    Red => 1
    Amber => 2
    Green => 3
  }
}

test "code" {
  expect code(Red) == 1
  expect code(Green) == 3
}
```

### Class pattern only with `move` (LR 9.8)

A class pattern destructures, so it is permitted only in `match move` or `let … = move`, every field named (or `_`
for a non-linear one), and never for a class with `cleanup`. Which code reports a class pattern without `move` is
not yet settled (X-152).

```fortis
// accept
class Parcel {
  export label: String
  export grams: Int
}

pure func heavy(p: owned Parcel) Bool {
  return match move p {
    Parcel(label: _, grams: g) => g > 1000
  }
}

test "heavy" {
  expect heavy(Parcel(label: "books", grams: 2500))
  expect !heavy(Parcel(label: "feather", grams: 1))
}
```

### E-TYP-040: calling `cleanup` (LR 9.4)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-040
class Cell {
  export value: Int
  cleanup(editable self) {
  }
}

test "cell" {
  let mut c = Cell(value: 1)
  c.cleanup()                            // reject: E-TYP-040
  expect c.value == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
class Cell {
  export value: Int
  cleanup(editable self) {
  }
}

test "cell" {
  {
    let c = Cell(value: 1)
    expect c.value == 1
  }
}
```

### E-OBL-007: `...move` drops a linear field (LR 9.2)

```fortis
// reject: E-OBL-007
class Pending {
  export label: String
  export result: Outcome[Int]
}

class Label {
  export label: String
}

pure try func compute() Int => 1

pure recovers func relabel() String {
  let p = Pending(label: "p", result: compute())
  let l = Label(...move p)                 // reject: E-OBL-007
  return copy l.label
}

test "relabel" {
  expect relabel() == "p"
}
```

```fortis
// accept
class Pending {
  export label: String
  export result: Outcome[Int]
}

pure try func compute() Int => 1

pure recovers func relabel() String {
  let p = Pending(label: "p", result: compute())
  let Pending(label: label, result: r) = move p
  let value = move r or recover 0
  return "${label}${value}"
}

test "relabel" {
  expect relabel() == "p1"
}
```

source: docs/agent/10-outcomes.md

# Outcomes and failures (LR 10)

<!-- covers: LR 10 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Outcomes and failures](../guide/10-outcomes.md). Source of truth: LR 10.*

> Preview: linear containers (LR 10.7) arrive in v0.1. The rest of this chapter (LR 10) is in v0.0.1.

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-10-01 | An `Outcome[T]` stays wrapped until consumed by an operation of LR 10.2; its success value is never reachable otherwise. | LR 10.1 |
| LANG-10-02 | Linear obligations survive storage in collections, fields and closures; dropping one is rejected. | LR 10.7 |
| LANG-10-03 | A reported failure is unreachable afterwards; `annotate` keeps exactly one obligation. | LR 10.6 |
| LANG-10-04 | `noalloc try` functions use the bounded failure representation on success and failure paths. | LR 10.3 |
| LANG-10-05 | `recover` without a prior `report` adds the `recovers` effect. | LR 10.4 |
| LANG-10-06 | Defects follow the closed taxonomy and are never catchable. | LR 10.8 |

## Facts

- `try func f(…) T` returns `Outcome[T]`; `return v` = success, `fail f` = failure; the call needs no prefix
  (LR 10.1). Patterns `success(x)`, `failure(f)`; by hand: `Outcome.success(v)`, `Outcome.failure(move f)` for a failure binding `f` (LR 10.1).
- Consuming operations, the complete list (LR 10.2):

  | Operation | Effect | Where |
  |---|---|---|
  | `e or fail` | propagate | `try` functions |
  | `e or recover v` | discharge, `v` lazy; adds `recovers` | anywhere |
  | `e catch n { … }` | block ends in `recover v`, `return`, `fail` or a `Never` call | anywhere |
  | `match e { success(x) => …, failure(f) => … }` | the `failure` arm consumes `f` | anywhere |
  | `report f` / `report f as r` | consume; `r: Report` receipt | `io` allowed (not `pure`) |
  | move to `owned Outcome[T]` / `owned Failure`, store in linear container or field | transfer | anywhere |
  | `fail f` (`f: Failure`) | propagate | `try` functions |

- No bare `or value`, no `?`, no call-site `try`, no `unwrap` (LR 10.2). `or` binds loosest: write
  `let v = f() or fail` on its own line (LR 1.1).
- Integer arithmetic the checker cannot prove safe, as the left operand of an outcome operator, is a checked
  region handled like a call: `total = total + r or fail`, `value * 10 + d or recover 0` (LR 6.4).
- In `test` and `property` bodies `or fail` is implied after a fallible call nothing else consumes:
  `expect half(4) == 2` (LR 14).
- `Failure`: stable `code` (`StringView from static`), typed payload, origin, optional cause chain; linear, not
  copyable; created in a `pure` function it reads no clock and allocates no identifier; bounded payload (64 bytes
  inline) satisfies `noalloc` (LR 10.3).
- `error Name { … }` with the lines `code: "…"`, optionally `payload { … }` and `message: "…${field}…"`, one per
  line: constructor `Name(…)` producing a `Failure`,
  pattern `is Name(…)`, display template over payload fields only (not rendered in records yet, and `Failure` is
  not `Displayable`: read `e.code` and payloads, X-154, D-57; constructor calls where a `Failure` value is expected
  are refused today, D-52); library failures have no `is`-nameable kind: test `e.code` (D-58); codes unique per package and stable; payload
  fields trivial or length-bounded `String`/`Bytes` (LR 10.3).
- `catch`: `return`/`fail` leave the function; `recover v` is the expression's value; `give` not allowed; covers
  only its left operand; `recover` after the failure was consumed (`report`, `fail`, `move`, `match`) adds
  nothing, otherwise it consumes and adds `recovers` (LR 10.4).
- Failure match: `match move f { is A(x: v) => …, is B as b => { …consume b… }, otherwise(o) => { …consume o… } }`;
  payloads bound by copy; `is` without `as` discharges (adds `recovers`); `otherwise(name)` is required (open type);
  `match f` without `move` inspects only and `f` must still be consumed (LR 10.5).
- `report` is a statement; with the `log` statements, the `io` needing no capability (diagnostic plane only); a
  `pure` function cannot report (LR 10.6, LR 11.6). A failure is recorded with `report e` alone, never logged as
  well; `log.warn(…)` is for what is not a failure, such as a fallback taken (LR 13).
  `annotate(f: owned Failure, note: StringView) Failure`; `Failures.aggregate(list: owned List[Failure]) Failure`
  (LR 10.6).
- A failing `try main`: one report on standard error, exit status 1 (LR 4.6).
- Linear containers: `push(move x)` in, `pop()` out as a linear `T?`, `consumeEach(owned self, fn mut(owned T) Void)`
  (in order, no early exit), `clear()` and dropping rejected, `count()`/`isEmpty()` borrow;
  `Outcome.collect(move list) Outcome[List[T]]`; a generic function holding `T` linearly declares `T: linear`
  (LR 10.7).
- Defects (contract violation in trusted code, stack exhaustion, out of memory, runtime invariant): native aborts,
  the VM terminates the task; never a `Failure`, never caught, no completion value; observed only as
  `TaskCompletion.Defect` by a supervisor (LR 10.8).

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-OBL-001 | an outcome (or any linear value) dropped at the end of a statement or block, overwritten or discarded (a never-polled future holding nothing linear and no exclusive loan may be discarded, LR 12.3) | consume it: `or fail`, `or recover v`, `catch`, `match`, `report`, move | LR 10.1 |
| E-TYP-040 | an `Outcome[T]` used where `T` is expected | consume it first: `let v = f() or fail` | LR 10.1 |
| E-OBL-002 | a path through a `catch` block ends without `recover`, `return`, `fail` or a `Never` call | end every path | LR 10.4 |
| E-ERR-001 | `fail` outside a `try` function | declare the function `try` | LR 5.4 |
| E-EFF-001 | a discharged, unreported failure in a function without `recovers` (the record carries a `correction` inserting `recovers `) | write `recovers`, or `report` the failure before `recover` | LR 11.1 |
| E-OWN-020 | a failure used after `report`, `fail` or `move` consumed it | consume it once | LR 7.4 |
| E-OBL-005 | a linear value live across a cancellation point, unless its type is `Abandonable` (as `Task` is); the future or task being awaited is not live across its own `await` | consume it before the `await`, pass it into the awaited call, or hold an `Abandonable` handle instead | LR 12.4 |
| E-OBL-006 | a `fn`/`fn mut` closure owning a linear value | `fn once` | LR 8.3 |
| E-OBL-007 | `...move` dropping a linear field | destructure and consume it | LR 9.2 |

## Correction patterns

### E-OBL-001: dropped outcome (LR 10.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-OBL-001
export error Missing {
  code: "store.missing"
}

pure try func lookup(key: Int) Int {
  if key > 3 {
    fail Missing()
  }
  return key
}

pure try func check(key: Int) Bool {
  lookup(key)                                  // reject: E-OBL-001
  return true
}

test "check" {
  expect check(1) or fail
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export error Missing {
  code: "store.missing"
}

pure try func lookup(key: Int) Int {
  if key > 3 {
    fail Missing()
  }
  return key
}

pure try func check(key: Int) Bool {
  let found = lookup(key) or fail
  return found == key
}

test "check" {
  expect check(1)
}
```

### E-TYP-040: an outcome where a value is expected (LR 10.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-040
export error Missing {
  code: "store.missing"
}

pure try func lookup(key: Int) Int {
  if key > 3 {
    fail Missing()
  }
  return key
}

pure func double(n: Int) Int => Int.saturatingMul(n, 2)

pure try func twice(key: Int) Int {
  return double(lookup(key))                   // reject: E-TYP-040
}

test "twice" {
  expect twice(2) == 4
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export error Missing {
  code: "store.missing"
}

pure try func lookup(key: Int) Int {
  if key > 3 {
    fail Missing()
  }
  return key
}

pure func double(n: Int) Int => Int.saturatingMul(n, 2)

pure try func twice(key: Int) Int {
  let v = lookup(key) or fail
  return double(v)
}

test "twice" {
  expect twice(2) == 4
}
```

### E-OBL-002: a `catch` path without an ending (LR 10.4)

The path that falls through also drops `e`: `E-OBL-001` on the same line (LR 10.1).

```fortis
// reject: E-OBL-002, E-OBL-001
export error Missing {
  code: "store.missing"
}

pure try func lookup(key: Int) Int {
  if key > 3 {
    fail Missing()
  }
  return key
}

pure recovers func safe(key: Int) Int {
  let v = lookup(key) catch e {                // reject: E-OBL-002, E-OBL-001
    if key > 100 {
      recover 0
    }
  }
  return v
}

test "safe" {
  expect safe(1) == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export error Missing {
  code: "store.missing"
}

pure try func lookup(key: Int) Int {
  if key > 3 {
    fail Missing()
  }
  return key
}

pure recovers func safe(key: Int) Int {
  let v = lookup(key) catch e {
    if key > 100 {
      recover 0
    }
    recover -1
  }
  return v
}

test "safe" {
  expect safe(1) == 1
  expect safe(7) == -1
}
```

### E-EFF-001: a silent discard without `recovers` (LR 10.4, LR 11.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-EFF-001
export error Missing {
  code: "store.missing"
}

pure try func lookup(key: Int) Int {
  if key > 3 {
    fail Missing()
  }
  return key
}

pure func orZero(key: Int) Int => lookup(key) or recover 0     // reject: E-EFF-001

test "orZero" {
  expect orZero(9) == 0
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export error Missing {
  code: "store.missing"
}

pure try func lookup(key: Int) Int {
  if key > 3 {
    fail Missing()
  }
  return key
}

pure recovers func orZero(key: Int) Int => lookup(key) or recover 0

test "orZero" {
  expect orZero(9) == 0
  expect orZero(2) == 2
}
```

Alternative when the discard must not be silent: a `catch e` block whose first line is `report e` and whose last
is `recover 0`, which adds no `recovers` but needs `io`, so the function cannot be `pure` (LR 10.4, LR 10.6).

### E-OWN-020: reporting and then propagating (LR 10.6, LR 7.4)

```fortis
// reject: E-OWN-020
export error Missing {
  code: "store.missing"
}

pure try func lookup(key: Int) Int {
  if key > 3 {
    fail Missing()
  }
  return key
}

try func strict(key: Int) Int {
  let v = lookup(key) catch e {
    report e
    fail e                                     // reject: E-OWN-020
  }
  return v
}

test "strict" {
  expect strict(1) == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export error Missing {
  code: "store.missing"
}

pure try func lookup(key: Int) Int {
  if key > 3 {
    fail Missing()
  }
  return key
}

try func strict(key: Int) Int {
  let v = lookup(key) catch e {
    fail annotate(move e, "strict lookup")
  }
  return v
}

test "strict" {
  expect strict(1) == 1
}
```

### Matching failures by kind (LR 10.5)

```fortis
// accept
export error NotANumber {
  code: "parse.not_a_number"
  payload { position: Int }
}

export error Empty {
  code: "parse.empty"
}

pure try func firstDigit(text: StringView) Int<0..9> {
  if text.scalarCount() == 0 {
    fail Empty()
  }
  let s = text.scalarAt(0) or fail
  let d = Scalar.digitValue(s)
  if d == null {
    fail NotANumber(position: 0)
  }
  return d
}

pure try recovers func classify(text: StringView) StringView from static {
  return match firstDigit(text) {
    success(d) => "digit"
    failure(f) => match move f {
      is NotANumber(position: p) => "not a number"
      is Empty => "empty"
      otherwise(other) => fail other
    }
  }
}

test "classify" cases {
  "digit": { text: "7x", expected: "digit" }
  "letter": { text: "x7", expected: "not a number" }
  "empty": { text: "", expected: "empty" }
} as row {
  expect classify(row.text) == row.expected
}
```

### Consuming a list of outcomes (LR 10.7)

```fortis
// accept
export error Missing {
  code: "store.missing"
}

pure try func lookup(key: Int) Int {
  if key > 3 {
    fail Missing()
  }
  return key
}

pure try func sumAll(keys: List[Int]) Int {
  let mut outcomes: List[Outcome[Int]] = List.default()
  for k in keys {
    outcomes.push(lookup(k))
  }
  let values = Outcome.collect(move outcomes) or fail
  let mut total = 0
  for v in values {
    total = Int.saturatingAdd(total, v)
  }
  return total
}

test "sumAll" {
  expect sumAll(List.of(1, 2, 3)) == 6
  let bad = sumAll(List.of(1, 9)) catch e {
    expect e.code == "store.missing"
    recover -1
  }
  expect bad == -1
}
```

# Effects and contracts (LR 11)

<!-- covers: LR 11 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Effects and contracts](../guide/11-effects.md). Source of truth: LR 11.*

> Preview: contracts (LR 11.5) arrive in v0.1. Effects, claims, noalloc and capabilities (LR 11.1, 11.2, 11.3, 11.4 and 11.6) arrive in v0.2. The observation plane and aspects (LR 11.7, 11.8) arrive in v0.5, except the diagnostic plane that `report` and the `log` statements write to (LR 11.7, LR 13), which is in v0.0.2. `main`'s capability parameters (LR 4.6, 11.6) and the core aspect `@ignorable` (LR 5.5, 11.8) are in v0.0.2.

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-11-01 | The effect set is exactly `alloc`, `io`, `mutate`, `nondet`, `suspend`, `block`, `fail`, `recovers`; summaries are computed transitively, closed under recursion by a least fixed point. | LR 11.1, 11.3 |
| LANG-11-02 | Writes to fresh storage, and writes through the function's own `editable` parameters (its write footprint), are not `mutate`; writes through captures, guards or atomics are. | LR 11.1, 11.3 |
| LANG-11-03 | `noalloc` is checked against the allocation-pattern whitelist for the actual target and telemetry plan, covering failures, cleanup, closures and every async phase; a conflicting telemetry policy is rejected at the policy. | LR 11.4 |
| LANG-11-04 | A trusted summary is labelled `trusted`, never `proved`; `trusted` is rejected outside the `fortis` package. | LR 11.3 |
| LANG-11-05 | `async`, `try` and `recovers` are written wherever the summary has the effect; across a module boundary only written `pure`/`noalloc` count; weakening an exported function's written modifiers is a reported API change. | LR 11.2, 11.3 |
| LANG-11-06 | A contract contains only modifiers, `forbids <effect>`, `requires capability A` and `excludes capability A`; configuration never adds predicates. | LR 11.5 |
| LANG-11-07 | `io` other than `report` and the `log` statements requires an `Authority` parameter, except in the entry `main`, which receives the capabilities as parameters (or, declaring none, creates them with one direct `Host.capabilities()`), and in an adapter's minting function, which itself requires the capability it derives the authority from, so every authority traces back to `main`; `Host.capabilities()` anywhere else, twice, or in a `main` that takes a capability parameter, is rejected. | LR 11.6 |
| LANG-11-08 | Contracts are applied in the modifier position, before single-word modifiers, without arguments; `@` applies aspects only. | LR 11.5 |
| LANG-11-09 | Aspects have only the parts `needs`, `before`, `after`, `on failure`, `metadata`; they elaborate before checking (`before` in application order, `after` reversed, `on failure` innermost first) and the elaborated function passes every ordinary check. | LR 11.8 |

## Modifier claims

| Modifier | Summary must not contain | Must be written when summary has |
|---|---|---|
| `pure` | `io`, `mutate`, `nondet`, `suspend`, `block` | (optional claim) |
| `noalloc` | `alloc` | (optional claim) |
| `async` | — | `suspend` |
| `try` | — | `fail` |
| `recovers` | — | `recovers` |

Source: LR 11.2. Order in a head: `[export] [Contract …] [pure] [noalloc] [async] [try] [recovers] func` (LR 8.1).

## Summary transfer rules (LR 11.3)

- Call: imports the callee's summary at its actual type arguments and callback types.
- `fail` is imported only when the failure leaves the function: kept by `or fail` and `fail f`; removed by
  `or recover`, `catch … recover`, and a consuming `match`, which add `recovers` unless the failure was reported
  first (LR 10.4).
- Write footprint: per `editable` parameter (and `editable self`). At a call each footprint parameter is
  instantiated with the argument place: fresh in the caller → nothing; reachable from a caller `editable`
  parameter → joins the caller's footprint; otherwise (capture, `Mutex` guard, atomic) → `mutate`.
- Fresh: a `let mut` initialised from a constructor, a literal or an owned call result. A binding holding a loan
  result is a path to the loan's owner.
- `async` call: builds a future, imports only argument evaluation; `await` (or `launch` into the awaiting scope)
  imports the future's summary; `launchParallel`/`launchBlocking` import the work's summary minus `block`.
- Callback parameter: contributes what its function type permits. A lambda literal with no `pure`-excluded effect
  has a `pure` type.
- `cleanup` effects join every function that may drop the type.
- `report` and `log.info`/`log.warn`/`log.error` are `io` but need no capability (LR 11.6, LR 13); a `pure`
  function cannot report or log.
- Instrumentation (`capture`, `record`, completion records) does not change a summary (LR 11.7).

## Contract elements (LR 11.5)

| Element | Effect on the target |
|---|---|
| `pure`, `noalloc`, … | the modifier's claim |
| `forbids recovers` (any of the eight effects) | that effect must be absent from the summary |
| `requires capability A` | the function takes a parameter of `Authority` type `A` |
| `excludes capability A` | the function neither takes `A` nor calls, transitively, a function that requires `A` |

Contracts compose by conjunction; contradictions are rejected; `pure` with `requires capability` is a
contradiction because a `pure` function takes no capability parameter (LR 11.5). The formatter keeps the name
and prints the expansion after it: `export FastCalculation pure noalloc func square` (LR 11.5).

## Authorities (LR 11.6)

- Capabilities (process-wide; created once, only for the entry `main`, which declares the ones it needs as
  parameters, `func main(console: Console, files: FileSystem)`, LR 4.6): `FileSystem`, `Network`, `Clock`,
  `Random`, `Environment`, `Process`, `Supervisor`, `Console`, `SecretAccess`, `RawSql`. Other functions take them
  as ordinary parameters. Older code calls `Host.capabilities()` once in a `main` with no capability parameter;
  that stays accepted, and `fortis fmt` rewrites it.
- Per-activation authorities (`RequestContext`, `Identity`, `Db`, `Tx`, `TaskContext`, `Mail`): minted by a
  kit's adapter from a capability, passed as a parameter.
- `Shared[A]` of an authority `A` satisfies the rule like `A`; share one capability as
  `let c = Shared.create(move out)`, then `c.retain()` per owner (no field stores a loan, LR 7.7).
- Attenuation only narrows: `fs.subtree(path)`.
- Clock reads are `nondet` and need `Clock`; a `pure` function takes time as a plain parameter.

## Aspect parts (LR 11.8)

| Part | Constraint |
|---|---|
| `needs name: Type` | target has exactly one parameter of `Type` (two: error); hooks use it with the target's mode |
| `needs Contract` | target carries the contract |
| `before { … }` | may `fail` on a non-`try` target only if an `on failure` of this or an outer aspect maps every failure |
| `after(result: R) { … }` | read loan of the result; may `fail` only when `R` is not linear |
| `on failure(f: Failure) R { … }` | owns `f`; must `return` an `R` or `fail` |
| `metadata` | arguments readable by libraries through the toolchain |

Arguments are compile-time constants: literals, record and variant-map literals, enum values, capture-free `fn`
literals, declaration names. First parameter may be positional, the rest named. Specialisation:
`aspect a(params, ...rest) = b(fixed: v, ...rest)`. No `around`, no body access. Core aspects (LR 11.8):
`observe(schema)` (LR 13), and `ignorable()`, applied as `@ignorable`, which lets a call statement drop the
function's non-linear result without `discard` (LR 5.5).

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-EFF-001 | summary exceeds the modifiers or contract: an effect `pure` excludes, `alloc` under `noalloc`, `suspend` without `async`, `fail` without `try`, `recovers` without `recovers`, a forbidden effect, a missing required or a present excluded authority | remove the effect; or, when the effect is intended, write the modifier its type needs (`async`, `try`, `recovers`). Dropping a written `pure`, `noalloc` or contract is an API change for whoever owns the claim, never a correction (LR 11.3) | LR 11.1, 11.3, 11.5 |
| E-EFF-010 | `io` reached through a capability without an `Authority` parameter (`report` and `log` need none); `Host.capabilities()` outside `main`, called twice, or in a `main` that takes a capability parameter | take the authority (`console: Console`) as a parameter; declare the capabilities `main` needs as its parameters and pass them down | LR 11.6 |
| E-EFF-020 | `block` inside an `async` function (or anything it calls), such as `lockBlocking` | `await m.lock()`, or move the blocking work into `launchBlocking` | LR 11.1 |
| E-EFF-030 | the application's telemetry policy attaches an allocating record to a `noalloc` function | change the policy at the reported site | LR 11.4 |
| E-EFF-040 (warning) | `--api-baseline OLD`: an exported function lost a written `pure`/`noalloc` or gained `async`/`try`/`recovers` | intended: bump the API; otherwise restore the modifier | LR 11.3 |
| E-TYP-150 | unknown aspect, arguments not matching the declaration, unmet or ambiguous `needs`, `...rest` outside an aspect's parameter list | fix the application or the target's parameters | LR 11.8 |
| E-OBL-008 | an `after` hook that may fail on a linear result type | do not fail in `after`, or apply it to a non-linear result | LR 11.8 |
| E-OBL-001 | elaborated path leaves a linear `owned` parameter unconsumed (a failing `before`) | consume it on that path, or take it by loan | LR 11.8 |

## Correction patterns

### E-EFF-001: `pure` function performing I/O (LR 11.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-EFF-001
import fortis.host { Console }

pure func greet(console: Console) {      // reject: E-EFF-001 (a pure function takes no capability)
  console.print("hello")              // reject: E-EFF-001
}

func main(console: Console) {
  greet(console)
}
```

```fortis
// accept
import fortis.host { Console }

func greet(console: Console) {
  console.print("hello")
}

func main(console: Console) {
  greet(console)
}
```

```output
hello
```

### E-EFF-001: missing `recovers` (LR 11.1, LR 11.2)

`main` inherits the effect from its callee and needs the modifier too.

```fortis
// reject: E-EFF-001
export error Odd {
  code: "demo.odd"
}

try func half(n: Int) Int {
  if n % 2 == 1 {
    fail Odd()
  }
  return n / 2
}

func halfOrZero(n: Int) Int => half(n) or recover 0   // reject: E-EFF-001

test "half" {
  expect halfOrZero(4) == 2
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export error Odd {
  code: "demo.odd"
}

try func half(n: Int) Int {
  if n % 2 == 1 {
    fail Odd()
  }
  return n / 2
}

recovers func halfOrZero(n: Int) Int => half(n) or recover 0

test "half" {
  expect halfOrZero(4) == 2
  expect halfOrZero(3) == 0
}
```

### E-EFF-001: `mutate` through a capture in a `pure` function (LR 11.1, LR 11.3)

```fortis
// reject: E-EFF-001
class Cell {
  export value: Int
  pure func set(editable self, value: Int) {
    self.value = value
  }
}

pure func viaClosure() Int {
  let mut cell = Cell(value: 0)
  let mut poke = fn mut[editable cell]() Void {
    cell.set(2)
  }
  poke()                              // reject: E-EFF-001
  return 0
}

test "closure" {
  expect viaClosure() == 0
}
```

```fortis
// accept
class Cell {
  export value: Int
  pure func set(editable self, value: Int) {
    self.value = value
  }
}

pure func direct() Int {
  let mut cell = Cell(value: 0)
  cell.set(2)
  return cell.value
}

test "direct" {
  expect direct() == 2
}
```

### E-EFF-001: allocation under `noalloc` (LR 11.1, LR 11.4)

```fortis
// reject: E-EFF-001
noalloc func pair(a: Int, b: Int) List[Int] => List.of(a, b)   // reject: E-EFF-001

test "pair" {
  expect pair(1, 2).count() == 2
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure noalloc func larger(a: Int, b: Int) Int {
  if a > b {
    return a
  }
  return b
}

test "larger" {
  expect larger(1, 2) == 2
}
```

### E-EFF-001: contract violation (LR 11.1, LR 11.5)

```fortis
// reject: E-EFF-001
import fortis.host { Network }

contract Offline {
  excludes capability Network
}

func lookup(net: Network, name: StringView) Int => name.scalarCount()

Offline func viaNetwork(net: Network) Int => lookup(net, "example")   // reject: E-EFF-001

test "offline" {
  expect true
}
```

```fortis
// accept
contract Offline {
  excludes capability Network
}

Offline pure func measure(name: StringView) Int => name.scalarCount()

test "offline" {
  expect measure("example") == 7
}
```

### E-EFF-010: `Host.capabilities()` outside `main` (LR 11.6)

Only the entry `main` receives capabilities; it declares them as parameters and lends them down.

```fortis
// reject: E-EFF-010
import fortis.host { Host }

func sneak() {
  let caps = Host.capabilities()      // reject: E-EFF-010
}

func main() {
  sneak()
}
```

```fortis
// accept
import fortis.host { Console }

func work(console: Console) {
  console.print("work")
}

func main(console: Console) {
  work(console)
}
```

```output
work
```

### E-EFF-010: I/O without an `Authority` parameter (LR 11.6)

Reported at the I/O statement.

```fortis
// reject: E-EFF-010
import fortis.host { Capabilities, Host }

func write(caps: Capabilities, text: StringView) {
  caps.console.print(text)            // reject: E-EFF-010
}

func main() {
  let caps = Host.capabilities()
  write(caps, "hello")
}
```

```fortis
// accept
import fortis.host { Console }

func log(console: Console, text: StringView) {
  console.print(text)
}

func main(console: Console) {
  log(console, "hello")
}
```

```output
hello
```

### E-EFF-020: blocking inside `async` (LR 11.1)

The `block` effect is reported in every `async` function that reaches it, here `wait` and its caller `main`.

```fortis
// reject: E-EFF-020
async try func wait(m: Mutex[Int]) Int {
  let g = m.lockBlocking() or fail    // reject: E-EFF-020
  return 0
}

async try func main() {
  let m = Mutex.create(1)
  let v = await wait(m) or fail       // reject: E-EFF-020
}
```

```fortis
// accept
async try func wait(m: Mutex[Int]) Int {
  {
    let g = await m.lock() or fail
  }
  return 0
}

async try func main() {
  let m = Mutex.create(1)
  let v = await wait(m) or fail
}
```

### E-TYP-150: unmet `needs` (LR 11.8)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-150
import fortis.host { Console }

export aspect logged(label: StringView) {
  needs console: Console
  before {
    console.print("before ${label}")
  }
}

@logged("count")                      // reject: E-TYP-150
func count(n: Int) Int => n

func main() {
  discard count(3)
}
```

```fortis
// accept
import fortis.host { Console }

export aspect logged(label: StringView) {
  needs console: Console
  before {
    console.print("before ${label}")
  }
}

@logged("count")
func count(console: Console, n: Int) Int => n

func main(console: Console) {
  discard count(console, 3)
}
```

```output
before count
```

### E-OBL-008: failing `after` on a linear result (LR 11.8)

```fortis
// reject: E-OBL-008
export error Stop {
  code: "demo.stop"
}

export aspect strict[R]() {
  after(result: R) {
    fail Stop()                       // reject: E-OBL-008
  }
}

@strict()
try func produce(n: Int) Outcome[Int] {
  return Outcome.success(n)
}

func main() {
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export error Stop {
  code: "demo.stop"
}

export aspect positive() {
  after(result: Int) {
    if result < 0 {
      fail Stop()
    }
  }
}

@positive()
try func produce(n: Int) Int {
  return n
}

test "produce" {
  expect produce(3) == 3
}
```

## Facts used when writing code

- Elaboration order for `@a @b func f`: `a.before`, `b.before`, body, `b.after`, `a.after`; a failure goes to
  `b`'s `on failure` first, then `a`'s; a handler that returns completes the function with its value, which is a
  success exit for observation (LR 11.8).
- The hooks' effects join the summary; a hook that allocates under `noalloc`, reports under `pure` or calls
  `Host.capabilities()` is rejected by the ordinary rules (LR 11.8).
- `pure` and `noalloc` are independent (LR 11.2). There is no `nostate`; `no-local-mutation` is an opt-in lint
  (LR 11.2).
- `noalloc` on an `async` function covers construction, every poll, completion and destruction; the VM's own
  allocations do not count against the native claim (LR 11.4).
- Target feature sets (`core`, `alloc`, `host`, `async`, `web`, `browser`) are not effects and not capabilities
  (LR 11.6).
