# Cleanup, async and concurrency (LR 12)

<!-- covers: LR 12 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Cleanup, async and concurrency](../guide/12-async.md). Source of truth: LR 12.*

> Preview: async, cancellation, scopes and sharing (LR 12.3, 12.4, 12.5, 12.6 and 12.7) arrive in v0.3. `defer` and destruction order (LR 12.1, 12.2) are in v0.0.1.

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-12-01 | A `defer` body is checked as if written at every exit of its block (after the block's own loans end, before its locals drop); it cannot alter the outcome; the places it names are initialised at every exit. | LR 12.1 |
| LANG-12-02 | Failures produced inside a `defer` are consumed there (`or recover`, `catch … recover`, `report`) and never replace the primary outcome; cleanup reports are labelled as such. | LR 12.1 |
| LANG-12-03 | `Future` and `Task` are linear; a pending future is never destroyed; cancellation is observed only at cancellation points. | LR 12.3, 12.4 |
| LANG-12-04 | A scope joins or cancels every task it launched before its block exits. | LR 12.5 |
| LANG-12-05 | Only `Shareable` environments without loans cross `launchParallel`/`launchBlocking`; loans cross only cooperative `launch` within the owner's block. | LR 12.5, 12.7 |
| LANG-12-06 | A `MutexGuard` is never live across `await`. | LR 12.3, 12.7 |

## Exit and destruction order (LR 12.2, LR 5.1, LR 7.9)

At every block exit, including cancellation and `or fail`:

1. the block's loans end; tasks launched on a `scope` declared in the block are cancelled and joined (their
   carried loans end) (LR 12.4, LR 12.5);
2. deferred blocks run, last registered first (LR 12.1);
3. during an unwind (cancellation or `fail`), `abandon` runs on every live `Abandonable` local, reverse
   initialisation order (LR 12.4);
4. owned locals drop, reverse initialisation order; a class value runs its `cleanup`, then drops its fields in
   declaration order (LR 7.9).

## `defer` constraints (LR 12.1)

- Block form only; no `return`, `fail`, `give`, `break`, `continue`, `await` inside (`E-DEF-001`); `defer await` is
  not in v1.
- Places it names must be initialised at every exit: no `move` of them between the `defer` and an exit
  (`E-DEF-002`).
- It may not use a binding of its own block that holds a loan (`E-OWN-052`); loans of enclosing blocks still apply.
- Its effects join the function's summary; a silent recovery inside it adds `recovers`.

## Async model (LR 12.3, LR 12.4)

- `async func f(…) T` call: evaluates arguments, returns `Future[T]` (`Future[Outcome[T]]` with `try`); the body
  starts at the first `await` or at `launch`.
- `await e`: only directly in an `async` body (not in a non-async lambda, not in `defer`).
- `Future[T]` is linear: `await`, launch, or `discard`. `discard` only for a never-polled future whose environment
  holds no linear value and no exclusive loan; it emits a `not_started` record.
- A future holds its arguments' loans (LR 7.3).
- Cancellation points: `await` (cooperative); `await` and `checkpoint()` (parallel and blocking pools). Cancellation
  is not a failure: not catchable, recoverable or matchable.
- No linear value live across a cancellation point unless it implements `Abandonable`
  (`func abandon(owned self)`: synchronous, non-failing, non-suspending). An `Abandonable` local may also be
  live at `or fail` (the unwind abandons it); a normal exit must still consume it. `Task` implements it.
- The futures and tasks being awaited are not "live across" their own `await`.

## Launch forms (LR 12.5)

| Form | Executor | Environment |
|---|---|---|
| `s.launch(f)` → `Task[T]` | same cooperative executor and thread | may borrow any binding declared in or before the scope |
| `s.launchParallel(f)` → `Task[T]` | CPU worker pool | `Shareable`, no loans; cancellation at `await` and `checkpoint()` |
| `s.launchBlocking(work)` → `Task[T]` | bounded blocking pool | `work: fn once() T`, `Shareable` environment; the only place `block` is allowed in async code; cancellation at `checkpoint()` |
| `s.detach(move task, supervisor)` | — | moves the join obligation to a `Supervisor`; removes the task from the scope |
| `join(a, b)` → `(A, B)` | polled inside the parent | consumes both futures; loans allowed; never returns early; failures stay in the tuple |

A `Task` is awaited inside its scope or detached. A scope exiting by `fail`, `return`, `break` or cancellation
cancels and joins its running tasks before its deferred blocks run; results never awaited are consumed by the
scope (a failure inside one is reported, labelled as abandoned by the scope) (LR 12.5).

`TaskCompletion[T]` = `Completed(value: T)` | `Cancelled(reason: Cancellation)` | `Defect(info: TaskDefect)`;
observed only by the supervisor of a detached task; linear when `T` is; consumed with `match` (LR 12.6).

## Shareable (LR 12.7)

- Shareable: trivial types; `String`, `Bytes`, `BigInt`; `List`, `Array`, `Map`, `OrderedMap`, `Set`,
  `FixedList`, `FixedMap` of shareables; classes, enums, tuples and records whose fields are all shareable;
  `Shared[T]`, `Weak[T]`, `Mutex[T]` with `T: Shareable`; `AtomicInt`, `AtomicBool`; `fn` / `fn once` closures
  capturing only `copy`/`move` of shareables; capability values.
- Not shareable: loans and views, `MutexGuard`, `fn mut` closures, `Future`, `Task`, thread-bound resources.

`List.of("a", "b")` is a `List[StringView]` (views of static text), which is not `Shareable`; annotate
`let words: List[String] = …` to make owned strings (LR 3.5, LR 12.7).

Mutation between tasks: `Mutex[T]`. Async: `await m.lock()`; sync: `m.lockBlocking()` (`block`). Both return
`Outcome[MutexGuard[T]] from mutex`; the guard is an exclusive loan of `T`, not `Shareable`, unlocks when
destroyed, and cannot cross `await`. Atomics: `AtomicInt`, `AtomicBool` (LR 12.7).

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-DEF-001 | `return`, `fail`, `give`, `break`, `continue`, `await` (including `or fail`) inside `defer` | consume failures with `catch … recover`, `or recover` or `report`; move control flow out of the `defer` | LR 12.1 |
| E-DEF-002 | a place the `defer` names is moved out before an exit | keep it owned until every exit (lend it instead of moving it), or do the deferred work before the move and drop the `defer`; registering the `defer` later does not help, since the place is still moved at the exit | LR 12.1 |
| E-OWN-052 | a `defer` uses a loan-holding binding of its own block | use the owner (or a parameter), or copy the value into a non-loan binding | LR 12.1 |
| E-OBL-001 | a future, task or outcome dropped at block exit; an outcome unconsumed inside `defer` | `await` it, launch it, or consume it | LR 6.12, 12.1, 12.3 |
| E-OBL-005 | a linear value live across `await` whose type is not `Abandonable` | consume it before the `await` (`let v = e or fail`), or pass it into the awaited call | LR 12.4 |
| E-ASY-001 | a `Task` leaves its scope block (`return`, `give`, assignment to an outer binding) | `await` it inside the scope, or `detach` it to a `Supervisor` | LR 12.3 |
| E-ASY-002 | a `MutexGuard` live across `await` | end the guard's block before the `await` | LR 12.3 |
| E-ASY-003 | a pool launch whose future arguments or closure captures include a loan or a non-`Shareable` value | pass owned shareable data (`copy`/`move`); use cooperative `launch` for borrowed data | LR 12.7 |
| E-EFF-020 | `block` inside an `async` function or anything it calls | `await m.lock()`, or `launchBlocking` | LR 11.1 |

## Correction patterns

### E-DEF-001: `or fail` inside `defer` (LR 12.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-DEF-001
export error FlushFailed {
  code: "demo.flush"
}

try func flush() {
  fail FlushFailed()
}

try func work(n: Int) Int {
  defer {
    flush() or fail                   // reject: E-DEF-001
  }
  return n
}

test "work" {
  expect work(1) == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export error FlushFailed {
  code: "demo.flush"
}

try func flush() {
  fail FlushFailed()
}

func work(n: Int) Int {
  defer {
    flush() catch e {
      report e
      recover Void
    }
  }
  return n
}

test "work" {
  expect work(1) == 1
}
```

### E-DEF-002: a deferred place moved away (LR 12.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-DEF-002
export class Handle {
  export open: Bool
  export func close(editable self) {
    self.open = false
  }
}

func keep(h: owned Handle) {
}

func run() {
  let mut input = Handle(open: true)
  defer { input.close() }
  keep(move input)                    // reject: E-DEF-002
}

test "run" {
  run()
  expect true
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export class Handle {
  export open: Bool
  export func close(editable self) {
    self.open = false
  }
}

func keep(h: owned Handle) {
}

func run() {
  let mut input = Handle(open: true)
  input.close()
  keep(move input)
}

test "run" {
  run()
  expect true
}
```

### E-OWN-052: a loan binding used in `defer` (LR 12.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-OWN-052
export class Buffer {
  export used: Int
  export func peek(self) alias Buffer from self => alias self
}

func run(items: Buffer) Int {
  let seen = items.peek()
  defer { discard seen.used }         // reject: E-OWN-052
  return seen.used
}

test "run" {
  expect run(Buffer(used: 1)) == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export class Buffer {
  export used: Int
  export func peek(self) alias Buffer from self => alias self
}

func run(items: Buffer) Int {
  defer { discard items.used }
  let seen = items.peek()
  return seen.used
}

test "run" {
  expect run(Buffer(used: 1)) == 1
}
```

### E-OBL-001: a future dropped (LR 6.12, LR 12.3)

```fortis
// reject: E-OBL-001
async func work(n: Int) Int => n

async func run(n: Int) Int {
  let pending = work(n)               // reject: E-OBL-001
  return n
}

async func main() {
  discard await run(1)
}
```

```fortis
// accept
async func work(n: Int) Int => n

async func run(n: Int) Int {
  let pending = work(n)
  return await pending
}

async func main() {
  discard await run(1)
}
```

### E-OBL-005: a linear value across `await` (LR 12.4)

```fortis
// reject: E-OBL-005
export error Negative {
  code: "demo.negative"
}

try func parse(n: Int) Int {
  if n < 0 {
    fail Negative()
  }
  return n
}

async func pause() {
}

async try func run(n: Int) Int {
  let pending = parse(n)
  await pause()                       // reject: E-OBL-005
  return pending or fail
}

async try func main() {
  discard await run(3) or fail
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export error Negative {
  code: "demo.negative"
}

try func parse(n: Int) Int {
  if n < 0 {
    fail Negative()
  }
  return n
}

async func pause() {
}

async try func run(n: Int) Int {
  let value = parse(n) or fail
  await pause()
  return value
}

async try func main() {
  discard await run(3) or fail
}
```

### E-ASY-001: a task escaping its scope (LR 12.3)

```fortis
// reject: E-ASY-001
async func work(n: Int) Int => n

async func run(n: Int) Task[Int] {
  scope tasks {
    let t = tasks.launch(work(n))
    return move t                     // reject: E-ASY-001
  }
}

async func main() {
}
```

```fortis
// accept
async func work(n: Int) Int => n

async func run(n: Int) Int {
  scope tasks {
    let t = tasks.launch(work(n))
    return await t
  }
}

async func main() {
  discard await run(2)
}
```

### E-ASY-002: a guard across `await` (LR 12.3)

```fortis
// reject: E-ASY-002
async func pause() {
}

async try func run(m: Mutex[Int]) Int {
  let g = await m.lock() or fail
  await pause()                       // reject: E-ASY-002
  return 0
}

async try func main() {
  let m = Mutex.create(1)
  discard await run(m) or fail
}
```

```fortis
// accept
async func pause() {
}

async try func run(m: Mutex[Int]) Int {
  {
    let g = await m.lock() or fail
  }
  await pause()
  return 0
}

async try func main() {
  let m = Mutex.create(1)
  discard await run(m) or fail
}
```

### E-ASY-003: a non-`Shareable` capture crossing a pool launch (LR 12.7)

```fortis
// reject: E-ASY-003
async func pools() Int {
  let words = List.of("a", "b", "c")
  scope tasks {
    let blocking = tasks.launchBlocking(fn once[move words]() Int => words.count())   // reject: E-ASY-003
    return await blocking
  }
}

async func main() {
  discard await pools()
}
```

```fortis
// accept
async func pools() Int {
  let words: List[String] = List.of("a", "b", "c")
  scope tasks {
    let blocking = tasks.launchBlocking(fn once[move words]() Int => words.count())
    return await blocking
  }
}

async func main() {
  discard await pools()
}
```

## Facts used when writing code

- `main` may be `async func main` or `async try func main`; it runs as the root task on the core cooperative
  executor (LR 4.6).
- `await first or fail` leaving a scope cancels the other tasks of that scope; a task cancelled before its first
  poll never runs (LR 12.5).
- The v1 executor runs every cooperative task of one scope tree on one thread; `launch` never needs `Shareable`
  (LR 12.5).
- `Shared[T]` gives read access only; mutation goes through `Mutex[T]` or an atomic (LR 7.8, LR 12.7).
- No cross-backend agreement is claimed for interleaving timing; write output after `await`s in a fixed order
  (LR 12.7).

---
source: docs/agent/13-observation.md
---

# Observation schemas and statements (LR 13)

<!-- covers: LR 13 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Observation](../guide/13-observation.md). Source of truth: LR 13.*

> Preview: observation schemas, `capture` and `record` (LR 13) arrive in v0.5. Log statements, `log.info`, `log.warn` and `log.error` (LR 13), are in v0.0.2.

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-13-01 | `capture field = e` snapshots `e` at the statement, copying it into the activation's frame; `e` is pure, infallible, non-suspending and of the field's declared type; it takes a read loan for the statement only. `record Name(field: v, …)` has the same requirement for its arguments. | LR 13 |
| LANG-13-02 | Each `required: all` field is assigned on every path before every exit; `required: success` / `failure` before every exit of that class; at most one `capture` per field per path; no `capture` in a loop body. Exits include `fail`, `return`, `await` (a cancellation edge) and cancellation. | LR 13 |
| LANG-13-03 | Frame contents are bounded by the schema: a `String` field declares a bound; a longer value is truncated or omitted as the schema declares, and the frame records which. | LR 13 |
| LANG-13-04 | `log.info(m)`, `log.warn(m)` and `log.error(m)` write one `log` record (level, message, function) to the diagnostic plane, standard error, never standard output; `m` is a `StringView`; no capability is needed, and the statement has the `io` effect, so a `pure` function cannot log. `log` is not a keyword: where a binding or declaration named `log` is in scope, `log.info(...)` is an ordinary call. Record a failure with `report e`, not a log; log what is not a failure (X-345, X-147). | LR 13 |

## Declarations and statements

| Form | Meaning | LR |
|---|---|---|
| `observation Name { … }` with one item per line: `version: n` (optional), each `field: T required: all\|success\|failure\|none`, and `encoding: bounded(n)` | schema; `version` defaults to 1; every field type `Encodable` (recursively, as derivation) | LR 13, LR 6.10 |
| `@observe(Name)` above a function head | the core aspect attaching the schema; the frame's fields are the schema's | LR 13, LR 11.8 |
| `capture field = e` | assign the frame field once | LR 13 |
| `record Name(field: v, …)` | emit one event per execution; allowed in loops | LR 13 |
| start, end, duration, outcome class | generated by the compiler; never written in source | LR 13 |
| cancelled before start | a frame marked `not_started`, no captured fields | LR 13 |
| `log.info(m)`, `log.warn(m)`, `log.error(m)` | one `log` record (`level`, `message`, `function`) per execution, to standard error: text on a terminal (`warn: could not take 9 nuts`), a JSON line otherwise; never standard output | LR 13, LR 11.7 |

Effects: observation does not change a function's effect summary; records go to the diagnostic plane, which
feeds nothing back (LR 11.7). A `pure` function may be observed. A log statement is the exception: it has the
`io` effect, like `report`, so a `pure` function cannot log; it needs no capability (LR 13, LR 11.6). Output: the default task reporter writes frames
without field values to standard error; field values leave only through the Telemetry kit, or on the record
stream under the development plan `FORTIS_TELEMETRY=permit-all` (LR 15).

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-OBS-001 | a required field unassigned on an applicable exit (`return`, `fail`, an `await`, the end) | `capture` the field before that exit; for an `await`, before the `await` | LR 13 |
| E-OBS-010 | a second `capture` of one field on one path | keep one `capture`; compute the value first | LR 13 |
| E-OBS-011 | `capture` inside a loop body | capture once after the loop, or use `record` for per-iteration events | LR 13 |
| E-OBS-012 | `capture`/`record` whose expression has an effect; a field the schema lacks; `capture` with no schema attached | bind the fallible or suspending value on its own line and capture the binding; fix the field name; attach `@observe(Schema)` | LR 13 |
| E-TYP-090 | a schema field type that is not `Encodable` (`Secret[T]`, an authority, a loan, a closure, …) | capture an `Encodable` projection, never the secret or resource | LR 13, LR 6.10 |

## Correction patterns

### E-OBS-001: required field missing on a failure exit (LR 13)

```fortis
// reject: E-OBS-001
export error Rejected {
  code: "shop.rejected"
}

observation Payment {
  amount: Int        required: all
  reason: Int        required: failure
}

@observe(Payment)
try func pay(amount: Int<0..10000>) Int {
  capture amount = amount
  if amount == 0 {
    fail Rejected()          // reject: E-OBS-001
  }
  return amount
}

test "pay" {
  expect pay(5) == 5
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export error Rejected {
  code: "shop.rejected"
}

observation Payment {
  amount: Int        required: all
  reason: Int        required: failure
}

@observe(Payment)
try func pay(amount: Int<0..10000>) Int {
  capture amount = amount
  if amount == 0 {
    capture reason = 1
    fail Rejected()
  }
  return amount
}

test "pay" {
  expect pay(5) == 5
}
```

### E-OBS-001: required field after an `await` (LR 13, LR 12.4)

```fortis
// reject: E-OBS-001
async func pause() {
}

observation Wait {
  tier: Int        required: all
}

@observe(Wait)
async func slow(tier: Int) Int {
  await pause()              // reject: E-OBS-001
  capture tier = tier
  return tier
}

test "slow" {
  expect true
}
```

```fortis
// accept
import fortis.host { Clock, Console }

observation Wait {
  tier: Int        required: all
}

@observe(Wait)
async func slow(clock: Clock, tier: Int) Int {
  capture tier = tier
  await clock.sleep(5ms)
  return tier
}

async func main(clock: Clock, console: Console) {
  let t = await slow(clock, 2)
  console.print("tier ${t}")
}
```

```output
tier 2
```

### E-OBS-010: captured twice (LR 13)

```fortis
// reject: E-OBS-010
observation Trace {
  tier: Int        required: all
}

@observe(Trace)
pure func process(n: Int<0..100>) Int {
  capture tier = n
  capture tier = n + 1       // reject: E-OBS-010
  return n
}

test "process" {
  expect process(1) == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
observation Trace {
  tier: Int        required: all
}

@observe(Trace)
pure func process(n: Int<0..100>) Int {
  let tier = n + 1
  capture tier = tier
  return n
}

test "process" {
  expect process(1) == 1
}
```

### E-OBS-011: capture in a loop (LR 13)

```fortis
// reject: E-OBS-011
observation Batch {
  last: Int        required: none
}

@observe(Batch)
pure func sum(items: List[Int<0..100>]) Int {
  let mut total = 0
  for item in items {
    capture last = item      // reject: E-OBS-011
    total = Int.saturatingAdd(total, item)
  }
  return total
}

test "sum" {
  expect sum(List.of(1, 2)) == 3
}
```

```fortis
// accept
observation Batch {
  count: Int        required: all
}

observation Item {
  value: Int        required: all
}

@observe(Batch)
pure func sum(items: List[Int<0..100>]) Int {
  capture count = items.count()
  let mut total = 0
  for item in items {
    record Item(value: item)
    total = Int.saturatingAdd(total, item)
  }
  return total
}

test "sum" {
  expect sum(List.of(1, 2)) == 3
}
```

### E-OBS-012: an effectful capture expression (LR 13)

```fortis
// reject: E-OBS-012
export error Odd {
  code: "demo.odd"
}

pure try func half(n: Int<0..100>) Int {
  if n % 2 == 1 {
    fail Odd()
  }
  return n / 2
}

observation Trace {
  half: Int        required: none
}

@observe(Trace)
pure try func process(n: Int<0..100>) Int {
  capture half = half(n) or fail     // reject: E-OBS-012
  return n
}

test "process" {
  expect process(4) == 4
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export error Odd {
  code: "demo.odd"
}

pure try func half(n: Int<0..100>) Int {
  if n % 2 == 1 {
    fail Odd()
  }
  return n / 2
}

observation Trace {
  half: Int        required: none
}

@observe(Trace)
pure try func process(n: Int<0..100>) Int {
  let h = half(n) or fail
  capture half = h
  return n
}

test "process" {
  expect process(4) == 4
}
```

### E-TYP-090: a field that is not `Encodable` (LR 13, LR 6.10)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-090
import fortis.host { Secret }

observation Login {          // reject: E-TYP-090
  password: Secret[String]   required: all
}

test "nothing" {
  expect true
}
```

```fortis
// accept
observation Login {
  user: String<scalars: 0..64>   required: all
}

@observe(Login)
pure func login(user: String) Int {
  capture user = user
  return 1
}

test "login" {
  expect login("ada") == 1
}
```

## Facts used when writing code

- A `String` field must be bounded: `String<scalars: 0..n>` (LR 13).
- `capture` takes a read loan for its statement and copies; later mutation does not change the frame (LR 13).
- `required: success` fields need not be assigned on failure exits, and the reverse (LR 13).
- A mapped failure (an aspect's `on failure` that returns a value) is a success exit of the outer function; the
  frame is shared by hooks and body (LR 11.8).
- Optimisation preserves required records (trace equivalence); non-required instrumentation may be elided
  (LR 11.7).
- Logs (LR 13) are for what is not a failure: progress, a summary, a fallback taken. A failure is recorded with
  `report e` alone, never logged as well. The program's own output stays `console.print`. `m` is a `StringView`: a literal, an interpolated literal or a `String`.
- `log` is not a keyword: where a binding or declaration named `log` is in scope, `log.info(…)` is an ordinary
  call; `log` used any other way with nothing declared is `E-NAM-001` (LR 13).
- Open defects: no backend supplies the duration (D-28); native writes no `not_started` frame (D-27).

---
source: docs/agent/14-tests.md
---

# Test declarations (LR 14)

<!-- covers: LR 14 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Tests](../guide/14-tests.md). Source of truth: LR 14.*

> Preview: property tests and shrinking (LR 14) arrive in v0.2. Example tests and cases tables are in v0.0.1.

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-14-01 | A table test binds its rows explicitly: `test "name" cases { "row": { f: v, … } … } as row { … }`; no implicit names enter scope. | LR 14 |
| LANG-14-02 | `expect e` takes a `Bool`, records a typed actual/expected pair, and fails the test when false. | LR 14 |
| LANG-14-03 | In `test` and `property` bodies `or fail` is implied: a call of a fallible function that is not the left operand of `or` or `catch` or a `match` scrutinee has its success type, and its failure fails the test with the failure's record. `let o = f()` keeps the outcome when the body later consumes `o` with `or`, `catch` or `match`, or annotates it `Outcome[…]`. Integer arithmetic the checker cannot prove safe is a checked region with the same implied `or fail` (LR 6.4): write `expect a * b == c`. A lambda in the body keeps its own rules; outside tests nothing changes (X-345). | LR 14 |

Further statements of LR 14:

- Tests are core declarations; no kit is needed to test a package (LR 14).
- A `test` body is an implicit `try` body: `or fail` is implied after a fallible call and may still be written;
  an escaping failure fails the test (LR 14). Write `expect f() == v`, not `expect (f() or fail) == v`.
- A row's record type is inferred from the body's uses; every row literal is then checked against it at compile
  time, exactly as the same literal in that position (LR 14).
- Expecting a failure consumes its obligation inside the test (LR 14).
- `property "name" forall (x: T, …) { … }` draws inputs from the parameter types, refinements included (LR 14).
- Test declarations are compiled only in test builds and may import test-only modules (LR 14).
- `fuzz` and `bench` are reserved words (LR A); fuzzing is `--fuzz` over every property (X-131).

## Commands

<!-- no-citation: the toolchain's test commands and records, not language rules -->

| Command | Backend | Options |
|---|---|---|
| `fortis test FILE\|DIR` | interpreter | `--format json` |
| `fortisc test FILE\|DIR` | VM | `--test NAME`, `--case NAME`, `--seed S`, `--cases N`, `--fuzz [--budget N] [--corpus DIR]`, `--replay FILE`, `--format json` |
| `fortisc native FILE --tests` | native | builds and runs the test executable |

Records (JSON lines with `--format json` or on a pipe): `test-result` (`test`, `case`, `status`, `evidence`),
`property-failure` (`seed`, `original`, `minimal`, `shrinks`, `replay`), and a final `test-summary`
(`passed`, `failed`) (X-131). Both runners write the results on standard error and the summary on standard output.
Exit status 1 when any test fails.

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-TYP-010 | `expect` of a non-`Bool` | compare: `expect f() == v` | LR 14, LR 5.2 |
| E-SYN-000 | a `cases` table without `as name` | add `as row` and use `row.field` | LR 14, LR 3.2 |
| E-REF-001 | a row literal outside the refinement of the position its field reaches | fix the row, or widen the parameter's type | LR 14, LR 3.5 |
| E-OBL-001 | a fallible call left unconsumed outside a test body, or in a lambda written in one (its body is its own function); in the body itself `or fail` is implied | `or fail`, or, to expect the failure, a `catch e` block that inspects `e` with `expect` and ends `recover v` (one statement per line) | LR 14, LR 10.1 |

## Correction patterns

### E-TYP-010: `expect` of a non-`Bool` (LR 14, LR 5.2)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-010
pure func double(n: Int<0..1000>) Int => n * 2

test "doubling" {
  expect double(2)           // reject: E-TYP-010
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func double(n: Int<0..1000>) Int => n * 2

test "doubling" {
  expect double(2) == 4
}
```

### E-SYN-000: rows not bound with `as` (LR 14, LR 3.2)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-000
pure func double(n: Int<0..1000>) Int => n * 2

test "doubling" cases {
  "one": { n: 1, expected: 2 }
} {                                   // reject: E-SYN-000
  expect double(n) == expected
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func double(n: Int<0..1000>) Int => n * 2

test "doubling" cases {
  "one": { n: 1, expected: 2 }
  "ten": { n: 10, expected: 20 }
} as row {
  expect double(row.n) == row.expected
}
```

### E-REF-001: a row outside the parameter's refinement (LR 14, LR 3.5)

```fortis
// reject: E-REF-001
pure func percent(part: Int<0..100>) Int => part

test "percent" cases {
  "low":      { part: 0, expected: 0 }
  "too high": { part: 150, expected: 150 }     // reject: E-REF-001
} as row {
  expect percent(row.part) == row.expected
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func percent(part: Int<0..100>) Int => part

test "percent" cases {
  "low":  { part: 0, expected: 0 }
  "high": { part: 100, expected: 100 }
} as row {
  expect percent(row.part) == row.expected
}
```

### E-OBL-001: an outcome dropped outside a test (LR 10.1, LR 14)

In a test or property body `or fail` is implied after a call of a fallible function (LANG-14-03, X-345). Outside
tests it is not: an outcome nothing consumes is dropped.

```fortis
// reject: E-OBL-001
export error Empty {
  code: "cart.empty"
}

pure try func average(total: Int<0..100000>, count: Int<0..1000>) Int {
  if count == 0 {
    fail Empty()
  }
  return total / count
}

func touch() {
  average(10, 0)             // reject: E-OBL-001
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export error Empty {
  code: "cart.empty"
}

pure try func average(total: Int<0..100000>, count: Int<0..1000>) Int {
  if count == 0 {
    fail Empty()
  }
  return total / count
}

test "empty" {
  let r = average(10, 0) catch e {
    expect e.code == "cart.empty"
    recover -1
  }
  expect r == -1
  expect average(10, 5) == 2
}
```

## Patterns

Property over a refined domain (LR 14):

```fortis
// accept
pure func clampTo(n: Int<0..1000>, high: Int<0..1000>) Int {
  if n > high {
    return high
  }
  return n
}

property "clamp never exceeds the bound" forall (n: Int<0..1000>, high: Int<0..1000>) {
  expect clampTo(n, high) <= high
}
```

- Replay a failing property: run the `replay` command of its `property-failure` record (`--test`, `--seed`,
  `--case`) with `fortisc test` (X-131).
- Never change an expected value, remove an `expect` or weaken a property to make a test pass.

# Core runtime inventory (LR 15)

<!-- covers: LR 15 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [The core runtime](../guide/15-runtime.md). Source of truth: LR 15.*

> Preview: the core runtime inventory (LR 15) arrives in v0.4.

LR 15 has no rule table of its own; its components are bound by rules elsewhere: LANG-04-06 (LR 4.6),
LANG-11-07 (LR 11.6), LANG-12-04 (LR 12.5), LANG-13-01 (LR 13). A conforming implementation ships these so that a
program importing no kit runs; kits add adapters and policy and never replace them (LR 15).

## Components

| Component | Core provides | Kits add | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Executor | one cooperative executor per process (root task and every `scope`); parallel and blocking pools; cancellation and deadlines | Tokio adapter, I/O readiness, timers, channels (Runtime host kit) | LR 15, LR 12.5 |
| Task reporter | sink for `report`, cleanup reports, `log` records, `not_started` records, completed `capture` frames; default: reports plus each frame's schema, outcome class and duration to stderr, never a captured field value; `FORTIS_TELEMETRY=permit-all` puts every field on the record stream | exporters, archive, projections (Telemetry kit) | LR 15 |
| Authorities | `Authority`; the ten capabilities, supplied to the entry `main`'s parameters by type; `Host.capabilities()` in `fortis.host`; the rule for per-activation authorities | minting adapters, attenuation helpers, sandboxing | LR 15, LR 11.6 |
| Observation schemas | the `observation` head | registry and pipelines (Telemetry kit) | LR 15, LR 13 |
| Entry | `main` in four forms, its parameters supplied by type; one report and exit status 1 on failure | the `application` head and lifecycle (Runtime host kit) | LR 15, LR 4.6 |
| Standard modules | `fortis.prelude`, `fortis.text`, `fortis.collections`, `fortis.numeric`, `fortis.time`, `fortis.money`, `fortis.host` | everything else under `fortis.*` | LR 15 |
| Secrets | `Secret[T]` (no codec, no capture, fingerprint display), `reveal(secret, cap: SecretAccess)` | `declassify`, `Sanitiser`, authentication adapters (Security kit) | LR 15 |

## Capabilities and their core operations

Created once, only for the entry `main`: the runtime passes each capability `main` declares as a parameter, by its
type (`func main(console: Console, fileSystem: FileSystem)`, LR 4.6), and `main` lends them to the functions it
calls (LR 11.6). Older code calls `Host.capabilities()` once in a `main` with no capability parameter; the fields of
the returned `Capabilities` are `fileSystem`, `network`, `clock`, `random`, `environment`, `process`, `supervisor`,
`console`, `secretAccess`, `rawSql` ([`fortis.host`](../../library/fortis/host.ft)).

| Capability | Operations (LR 15) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `FileSystem` | `readText(path) String`, `writeAll(path, text)`, `readAll(path) Bytes`, `open(path) File`, `create(path) File`, `subtree(path) FileSystem` | all but `subtree` are `try`; `File`: `readAll`, `writeAll`, `close` |
| `Network` | `resolve(host) String` | `try` |
| `Clock` | `now() Timestamp` (`nondet`), `frozen(instant) Clock`, `sleep(d)` (`async`), `elapsedSince(t) Duration` (`try`) | a `pure` function takes time as a parameter |
| `Random` | `below(bound: Int<1..>) Int<0..>` (`nondet`), `seeded(seed) Random` | |
| `Environment` | `get(name) Secret[String]?` | |
| `Process` | `run(program, arguments: ListView[String]) Int` | `try`, `block` |
| `Console` | `print(text)` | standard output, one line |
| `RawSql` | `execute(statement) Int` | `try` |
| `Supervisor` | none; authorises `scope.detach(move task, supervisor)` | LR 12.5 |
| `SecretAccess` | none; authorises `reveal(secret, cap)` | |

`Path.parse(text: String) Path` is `try` (LR 15). Per-activation authorities (`RequestContext`, `Identity`, `Db`,
`Tx`, `TaskContext`, `Mail`) are minted by their kit's adapter from a capability (LR 15, LR 11.6).

Development adapters of the reference toolchain (library contracts in `fortis.host`, not language rules): file
system rooted in a fresh empty directory per run or `FORTIS_DEV_ROOT` (relative to the working directory; every
backend); network offline except `localhost`;
`Random` SplitMix64 from seed 0 or `FORTIS_DEV_SEED`; `Process` simulates `true` (0) and `false` (1); `RawSql`
fails `sql.unavailable`.

## Standard module contents named by LR 15

| Module | Contents | LR |
|---|---|---|
| `fortis.money` | `Decimal` amount with run-time `Currency`; `Money.of`, `zero`, `add`, `subtract`, `multiply(money, factor: Int)`, `divide(money, divisor: Int<1..>)`, `greaterThan`; arithmetic fails on currency mismatch | LR 15 |
| `fortis.time` | `Duration.days/hours/minutes/seconds/milliseconds`, fallible `Duration.add/sub/multiply`, `d.nanoseconds()`, comparisons on `Duration`, display in the largest exact unit (`150s`, `1h`, `250ms`, `0s`); `Timestamp.epoch()`, fallible `Timestamp.add(t, d)`, `Timestamp.after`, `Timestamp.before` | LR 15 |
| `fortis.host` | capabilities, `Path`, `Secret[T]`, `reveal` | LR 15 |

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-EFF-010 | `Host.capabilities()` outside `main`, a second call in `main` (reported at `main`), a call in a `main` that takes a capability parameter, or `io` other than `report` and `log` reached without an `Authority` parameter | declare the capability as a parameter of `main`; pass it (or a `Shared` of it) down as a parameter | LR 11.6 |
| E-TYP-090 | a `Secret[T]` (or an authority) in an `Encodable` position, such as an observation field | capture or encode a non-secret projection | LR 15, LR 6.10 |

## Correction patterns

### E-EFF-010: capabilities created outside `main` (LR 11.6)

```fortis
// reject: E-EFF-010
import fortis.host { Host }

func greet() {
  let caps = Host.capabilities()     // reject: E-EFF-010
}

func main() {
  greet()
}
```

```fortis
// accept
import fortis.host { Console }

func greet(console: Console) {
  console.print("hello")
}

func main(console: Console) {
  greet(console)
}
```

```output
hello
```

### E-EFF-010: `Host.capabilities()` in a `main` that takes capabilities (LR 11.6)

A `main` with a capability parameter already has its capabilities; a call of `Host.capabilities()` there is a
second creation.

```fortis
// reject: E-EFF-010
import fortis.host { Console, Host }

func main(console: Console) {
  let caps = Host.capabilities()     // reject: E-EFF-010
  console.print("ready")
}
```

```fortis
// accept
import fortis.host { Console }

func main(console: Console) {
  console.print("ready")
  console.print("once")
}
```

```output
ready
once
```

## Patterns

Failing `try main` (exit status 1, one `runtime-failure` record on stderr naming code, payload and origin;
LR 4.6):

```fortis
// accept (exit status 1)
import fortis.host { Path, FileSystem, Console }

try func main(fileSystem: FileSystem, console: Console) {
  let path = Path.parse("missing.txt") or fail
  let text = fileSystem.readText(path) or fail
  console.print(text)
}
```

Revealing a secret (LR 15):

```fortis
// accept
import fortis.host { reveal, Environment, SecretAccess, Console }

func main(environment: Environment, secretAccess: SecretAccess, console: Console) {
  let home = environment.get("HOME")
  if home != null {
    let value = reveal(home, secretAccess)
    console.print("${value.byteCount() > 0}")
  }
}
```

```output
true
```

Time arithmetic (LR 15):

```fortis
// accept
pure try func deadline(start: Timestamp, slack: Int<0..60>) Timestamp {
  let wait = Duration.add(Duration.minutes(5), Duration.seconds(slack)) or fail
  return Timestamp.add(start, wait) or fail
}

test "deadline is later" {
  let t = deadline(Timestamp.epoch(), 30)
  expect Timestamp.after(t, Timestamp.epoch())
}
```

---
source: docs/agent/16-kits.md

# Reserved declaration heads for kits (LR 16)

<!-- covers: LR 16 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Kits and declaration heads](../guide/16-kits.md). Source of truth: LR 16.*

> Preview: declaration heads and kits (LR 16) arrive in v0.5.

LR 16 has no rule table; the rule that binds it is LANG-03-04 (LR 3.4): every reserved word, head words
included, is rejected in declaration and binding positions and admitted as a member or method name.

## Facts

| Fact | LR |
|---|---|
| A kit is a named, versioned bundle of packages shipped with the distribution; it extends Fortis only through libraries, aspects, declaration heads, embedding bindings and verifiers. Toolchain components (daemon, LSP, SDK generators) are not kits. | LR 16 |
| A kit never changes core semantics and is never a prerequisite of Language 1.0. | LR 16 |
| Kits extend the language with aspects (LR 11.8) and, for non-function-shaped declarations, declaration heads. | LR 16 |
| A head's body is validated by a versioned schema and elaborated into core declarations before type checking. | LR 16 |
| Elaboration contract: a head produces only classes, functions, enums, contracts and observation schemas that obey every LR rule. | LR 16 |
| Elaborated code is checked like any other code; heads have no ownership or effect rules of their own. | LR 16 |
| Packages cannot add heads, tokens or grammar rules. | LR 16 |
| Head words are reserved words, never imported; importing a kit's package makes its heads available; its aspects are imported by name. | LR 16 |
| Raw template region: a statement `[export] [server\|client\|hybrid] view [name [(params)]] {` opens a region; the lexer takes the text to the balancing `}` (counting all braces, including `${…}`) as one unlexed token handed to the Web UI kit. | LR 16 |

## Reserved heads

| Head | Kit | Elaborates to | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | Runtime host | generated `main`, capability acquisition, lifecycle ordering | LR 16 |
| `explore` | Developer tooling | an exploration declaration | LR 16 |
| `context` (body word `provide`), class member `inject` | Dependency injection | constructor parameters, generated scope struct | LR 16 |
| `model` | Data | nominal data class, schema, codecs, query metadata | LR 16 |
| `view` (standalone), `component` (body words `state`, `action`, `view`, `resource`) | Web UI | render function; class with explicit state struct, action functions, render function | LR 16 |
| `observation` | core (LR 13), consumed by Telemetry | frame type and schema | LR 16 |

Reserved also: prefixes `server`, `client`, `hybrid`; body words `inject`, `provide`, `state`, `action`,
`resource` (LR A). Not reserved (contextual): `lazy`, `launch`, `launchParallel`, `launchBlocking`, `detach`,
`retain`, `validate`, `checkpoint`, `join`, `annotate`, `cleanup`, `capability` (LR A).

## Extension slots (exactly four; LR 16)

1. A head block, optionally prefixed `server`, `client` or `hybrid`.
2. `[export] inject [lazy] name: Type` inside a class body; an exported slot is an exported field (X-138).
3. Aspects declared by the kit, applied with `@name(args)` (no slot of their own).
4. The `cases` table syntax of tests (LR 14).

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-SYN-002 | a head word, prefix or head-body word used as a binding, parameter, field, type or free-function name | rename (`page`, `pageView`); a method or associated function may keep the keyword name | LR 3.4, LR 16 |

## Correction patterns

### E-SYN-002: a head word as a field name (LR 3.4, LR 16)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-002
export class Page {
  export view: Int            // reject: E-SYN-002
}

test "page" {
  expect true
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export class Page {
  export views: Int
  export func view(self) Int => self.views
}

test "page" {
  let p = Page(views: 3)
  expect p.view() == 3
}
```

### E-SYN-002: a head word as a binding (LR 3.4, LR 16)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-002
pure func size() Int {
  let model = 1               // reject: E-SYN-002
  return model
}

test "size" {
  expect size() == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func size() Int {
  let dataModel = 1
  return dataModel
}

test "size" {
  expect size() == 1
}
```

### E-SYN-002: a head word as a free function name (LR 3.4, LR 16)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-002
pure func component(n: Int) Int => n      // reject: E-SYN-002

test "component" {
  expect component(1) == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export class Widget {
  export id: Int
  export func component(id: Int) Widget => Widget(id)
}

test "component" {
  expect Widget.component(1).id == 1
}
```

## Pattern: a user aspect (no slot needed; LR 16, LR 11.8)

```fortis
// accept
import fortis.host { Console }

aspect logged(label: StringView) {
  needs console: Console
  before {
    console.print("enter ${label}")
  }
}

@logged("work")
func work(console: Console, n: Int) Int => n

func main(console: Console) {
  console.print("result ${work(console, 3)}")
}
```

```output
enter work
result 3
```

---
source: docs/agent/embedded-languages.md
---

# Embedded languages (LR 16)

<!-- covers: LR 16 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Embedded languages](../guide/embedded-languages.md). Source of truth: LR 16.*

> Preview: declaration heads and kits (LR 16) arrive in v0.5.

| Fact | Source |
|---|---|
| The core's only embedded text is the raw template region: a statement `[export] [server\|client\|hybrid] view [name [(…)]] {` opens it, recognised lexically with no knowledge of the enclosing declaration; the lexer takes the text to the balancing `}` (every brace counted, `${…}` included) and hands it to the Web UI kit unlexed, as one token. | LR 16 |
| Recognition is the lexer's; permission is the kit's: it validates where a region appears, inside a `component` body or as a standalone `view` head. Where the `view` is a declaration, its group must be a parameter list. Template syntax is the kit's; a template adds no core token. | LR 16 |
| Elsewhere, another language's text is a string (`StringView` or `String`). Interpolation never escapes for HTML, SQL or any context: bind or escape values through a library. | LR 3.5, LR 3.6 |
| Fenced embedded-language blocks with typed holes, `embed … from`, embedding bindings and their verifiers are not in Language 1.0 (a later edition, X-145). Do not write them: they are not syntax (LR 3.2). | X-145 |

---
source: docs/agent/appendix-a-keywords.md
---

# Keyword inventory (LR A)

<!-- covers: LR A -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Keywords](../guide/appendix-a-keywords.md). Source of truth: LR A, LR 3.4.*

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-03-04 | Every word below is reserved in every declaration and binding position (variable, parameter, field, type, declaration name), except the name of a method or associated function; after `.` every word is a member name (`memberName`). The lexer never reclassifies a keyword. | LR 3.4, LR A |

## Inventory

| Group | Words | LR |
|---|---|---|
| Declarations | `func` `fn` `let` `mut` `const` `type` `alias` `class` `trivial` `enum` `error` `interface` `mixin` `implement` `implements` `with` `derive` `requires` `forbids` `excludes` `contract` `aspect` `needs` `before` `after` `on` `metadata` `lifetime` `from` `where` `export` `import` `as` | LR A |
| Modifiers | `pure` `noalloc` `async` `try` `recovers` `editable` `owned` `dynamic` `linear` `trusted` `once` | LR A |
| Ownership | `copy` `move` | LR A |
| Control | `if` `else` `while` `for` `in` `loop` `break` `continue` `return` `fail` `give` `recover` `match` `when` `otherwise` `is` `or` `catch` `discard` `defer` `await` `scope` | LR A |
| Values | `true` `false` `null` `present` `success` `failure` `self` `Self` | LR A |
| Observation | `capture` `record` `report` `observation` `required` `version` `encoding` | LR A |
| Testing | `test` `cases` `property` `forall` `fuzz` `bench` `expect` | LR A |
| Kit heads (reserved by the core) | `application` `context` `model` `component` `view` `explore`; prefixes `server` `client` `hybrid`; in head bodies `inject` `provide` `state` `action` `view` `resource` | LR A, LR 16 |
| Contextual, not reserved | `launch` `launchParallel` `launchBlocking` `detach` `retain` `validate` `checkpoint` `join` `annotate` `cleanup` `capability` `lazy`; `log` (the log statements `log.info`/`log.warn`/`log.error`, LR 13) | LR A |

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-SYN-002 | a keyword in a declaration or binding position (`let match`, a field `from`, a parameter `type`) | rename (`pattern`, `start`, `kind`); a method may keep the keyword name | LR 3.4 |

Tool behaviour: the checker stops parsing a module at its first `E-SYN-002`, so fix each one and re-check; the
rule itself is LR 3.4.

## Correction patterns

### E-SYN-002: keyword as a binding (LR 3.4)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-002
pure func span(start: Int, end: Int) Int {
  let match = end            // reject: E-SYN-002
  return match
}

test "span" {
  expect span(1, 4) == 4
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func span(start: Int, end: Int) Int {
  let last = end
  return last
}

test "span" {
  expect span(1, 4) == 4
}
```

### E-SYN-002: keyword as a field; keep it as a method (LR 3.4, LR A)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-002
class Span {
  export from: Int           // reject: E-SYN-002
}

test "span" {
  expect Span(from: 1).from == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
class Span {
  export start: Int
  export pure func from(start: Int) Span => Span(start)
  export pure func where(self, n: Int) Int => n
}

test "span" {
  let s = Span.from(1)
  expect s.start == 1
  expect s.where(4) == 4
}
```

source: docs/agent/appendix-b-decisions.md
---

# Closed decisions (LR B)

<!-- covers: LR B -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Closed decisions](../guide/appendix-b-decisions.md). Source of truth: LR B.*

Decisions Language 1.0 does not reopen. Never write the rejected form; the normative statement is in the section
cited (LR B).

## Syntax and literals

| Topic | Decision | LR |
|---|---|---|
| Declaration vs assignment | `let` / `let mut` declare; `=` assigns only | LR 5.1 |
| Semicolons | `;` is `E-SYN-001` | LR 3.2 |
| File extension, comments | `.ft`; `//` only; documentation = the `//` run directly above a declaration; no `/* */`, no `///` | LR 3.1, LR 3.7 |
| Integer literal | type from context, default `Int`; must fit the target refinement | LR 3.5 |
| Float literal | needs `.` or exponent; `f32` suffix for `Float32` | LR 3.5 |
| Decimal literal | `d` suffix (`19.99d`) | LR 3.5 |
| String literal | `StringView from static`; converts to `String` only where a `String` is expected (allocates) | LR 3.5, LR 6.6 |
| Block value | `give` (not `yield`); single-expression match arms need none; `catch` ends in `recover` | LR 5.4, LR 9.8 |
| Type of `fail` | `Never` | LR 5.4 |
| Catch binding | explicit: `catch e { … }` | LR 10.4 |
| Named arguments | after positionals, any order, each once; names are public API | LR 5.8 |
| Default arguments | pure constant expressions, re-evaluated per call | LR 5.8 |
| Variadics | none in user code; take `ListView[T]`, pass `List.of(…)` | LR 5.8, LR 6.2 |
| Constructor naming | `create`, `of`, `from`; no `new` | LR 1.1, LR 9.2 |
| Transparent type aliases | none; `type` is always nominal | LR 6.9 |
| Operator overloading | none; `Type.add(a, b)` | LR 6.10 |
| Or-patterns | narrow: `A \| B => v`, whole patterns of an arm, no bindings, no guard | LR 9.8 |
| Not in v1 | range patterns, generic lambdas, generic functions over `N`, associated types, explicit type arguments at calls (annotate the binding) | LR 6.2, LR 6.10, LR 8.2, LR 9.5, LR 9.8 |
| Standard package | `fortis`; no `std` | LR 4.3 |
| Negative example marker | `// reject: E-XXX-NNN` | LR 0 |
| Test rows | `cases { … } as row { … }` | LR 14 |

## Ownership

| Topic | Decision | LR |
|---|---|---|
| Call-site markers | `move p`, `copy p`, `editable p` for existing places; fresh values unmarked | LR 7.5 |
| Receiver markers | `move p.m()` for `owned self`; an `editable self` call is `p.m()` on a root that shows it may change (`let mut`, `editable` parameter or capture, exclusive loan, the method's own `editable self`) and `E-OWN-001` on any other root, marked or not; `editable p.m()` stays accepted | LR 7.5, LR 7.6 |
| Kept loans at call sites | `alias p` / `editable p` for an argument the result borrows `from` | LR 7.6 |
| Returning a local | `return local` moves it; `return move local` stays accepted; parameters, fields and captures keep their marker | LR 7.5, LR 7.6 |
| Partial moves | not in v1 (`E-OWN-040`) | LR 7.2 |
| Non-lexical lifetimes | not in v1; loans end at their block | LR 7.3 |
| Stored loans | not in v1 (`E-OWN-053`): loans live in locals, parameters and `from` returns | LR 7.7 |
| Stored and returned loans | both spell `from`; `within` removed | LR 7.6, LR 7.7 |
| Two-phase borrows | reserve at argument evaluation, activate at call entry | LR 5.7 |
| Two-origin loans | rejected | LR 7.6 |

## Functions, failures, effects

| Topic | Decision | LR |
|---|---|---|
| `Void` functions | may fall off the end; non-`Void` need `return`/`fail` on every path; a function or method head leaves out `Void`, a function type keeps it | LR 5.4, LR 8.1 |
| Closure kinds | `fn`, `fn mut`, `fn once`, always written; a `fn mut` held by a `let mut` is called `f()` | LR 8.2 |
| Lambda modifiers | same as named functions; capture brackets only when non-empty | LR 8.2 |
| `recovers` | a modifier, written like `try` | LR 8.1, LR 10.4 |
| `or die` | removed; `try main` (one report, exit status 1) | LR 4.6 |
| `report` | statement; `report e as receipt` binds the receipt | LR 10.6 |
| `nostate` | removed; opt-in lint `no-local-mutation` only | LR 11.2 |
| Effect clauses | the vocabulary is `pure`/`noalloc`/`async`/`try`/`recovers`; no `effects(…)` clause; tools show inferred `alloc`, `block`, `nondet` | LR 11.2, LR B |
| Contracts | by name in modifier position (`export FastCalculation func …`); never `@`; no arguments | LR 11.5 |
| Aspects | `@name(args)`, lowercase, the only use of `@`; parts `needs`, `before`, `after`, `on failure`, `metadata`; `...rest` specialisation; `on failure` may re-fail; user packages may declare them | LR 11.8 |
| Aspect hooks | failure handlers innermost first; no `around`; no body re-execution | LR 11.8 |
| Observation attachment | `@observe(Schema)`, a core aspect | LR 11.8, LR 13 |
| Interfaces | nominal; `requires` for sub-interfaces; bundles satisfied automatically; no method bodies | LR 9.5 |
| Serialisation | `derive Codec` = `Encodable` + `Decodable`; canonical `toBytes`/`toText`; formats as packages with `…Serialised` mixins; hand-written `encode` and `derive` never coexist | LR 6.10 |
| Projection | `...copy p` copies taken fields; `...move p` consumes the whole source; `derive From[S]`; `to()` on every type | LR 6.10, LR 9.2 |
| Constants | include record and variant-map literals, declaration names, `Type.of(…)` intrinsics | LR 5.1 |
| Variant maps | `VariantMap[E, V]` written `{ Variant: value }`; optional callable `(fn(…) R)?` | LR 6.9 |
| Entry point | `main` in the manifest's entry module, `export` implied; its parameters are the capabilities and arguments it needs, supplied by type | LR 4.6 |

## Numbers, collections, concurrency

| Topic | Decision | LR |
|---|---|---|
| Float equality | IEEE `==` allowed; no `Equatable`/`Hashable`/`Comparable` | LR 6.5 |
| Hash iteration | deterministic per build; allowed in `pure` | LR 6.7 |
| Length-refined collections | immutable; mutate an unrefined collection and `validate` | LR 6.3 |
| Executor | cooperative single thread per scope tree; parallel/blocking pools need `Shareable` | LR 12.5 |
| Blocking in async code | forbidden; `launchBlocking` takes a synchronous `fn once` | LR 11.1, LR 12.5 |
| Atomics | `AtomicInt`, `AtomicBool`; `seqcst`, `acquire`/`release` | LR 12.7 |
| `defer` | block form only; `defer await` is `E-DEF-001` | LR 12.1 |

## Correction patterns

### `or die` → `try main` (LR 4.6)

```fortis
// accept
import fortis.host { Console }

export error Empty {
  code: "demo.empty"
}

try func first(items: ListView[Int]) Int {
  if items.count() == 0 {
    fail Empty()
  }
  return items.get(0) ?? 0
}

try func main(console: Console) {
  let n = first(List.of(4, 5)) or fail
  console.print("${n}")
}
```

```output
4
```

### `;` (LR 3.2)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-001
pure func one() Int {
  return 1;                 // reject: E-SYN-001
}

test "one" {
  expect one() == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func one() Int {
  return 1
}

test "one" {
  expect one() == 1
}
```

source: docs/agent/appendix-c-lowering.md

# Lowering reference and the Rust-expressible subset (LR C)

<!-- covers: LR C -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Lowering to Rust](../guide/appendix-c-lowering.md). Source of truth: LR C, LR 7.10.*

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-07-03 | No clone, reference count or hidden shared ownership is ever inserted to repair a rejected program. | LR 7.10, LR C.1 |
| LANG-07-09 | An ownership shape with no lowering is rejected with `E-OWN-090` (or the earlier rule's more specific code), never lowered with `unsafe` or lifetime erasure. | LR 7.10, LR C.2 |
| LANG-11-03 | `noalloc` is decided by the allocation whitelist of LR C.3 against the actual target and telemetry plan. | LR 11.4, LR C.3 |

Generated application crates carry `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`; a `rustc` rejection of frontend-accepted code is a
compiler defect only inside the Rust-checked fragment (LR 7.10, LR C.1).

## Shapes (C.1)

| Construct | Native shape | Rust-checked | Frontend-checked | LR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` newtype | `struct Name(Repr)`, private field | nominal identity | refinement invariant | LR C.1 |
| class | `struct` + `impl` | field privacy | generated-constructor visibility | LR C.1 |
| trivial type | `Copy` struct/enum | `Copy` | the trivial table | LR C.1 |
| `copy p` | `Clone::clone` of a generated `Clone` | | copyable set; allocation | LR C.1 |
| read loan / exclusive loan | `&T` / `&mut T` | loan validity | lexical end (stricter); field-freezing | LR C.1 |
| `move p` | move | use after move | | LR C.1 |
| `from` return | `fn f<'a>(x: &'a T) -> &'a U` | lifetime | single origin | LR C.1 |
| standard view / cursor | `&'a str`, `&'a [T]`, `Cursor<'a, T>` owned by its holder | lifetime | standard types only (X-137) | LR C.1 |
| `Shared[T]` / `Weak[T]` | `Arc<T>` / `Weak<T>` | `Send`/`Sync` | `retain` visibility | LR C.1 |
| `Mutex[T]` | `std::sync::Mutex` wrapper | `Send`/`Sync` | guard across `await` | LR C.1 |
| interface / `dynamic I` | trait + generics / `Box<dyn I>`, `&dyn I`, `Arc<dyn I>` | trait bounds; object safety | substitutability, coherence; dynamic eligibility, allocation | LR C.1 |
| mixin | generated inherent methods | | conflicts, required methods | LR C.1 |
| lambda | closure, concrete environment | `Fn`/`FnMut`/`FnOnce` | declared kind ≥ needed kind; capture list | LR C.1 |
| `try func` / `catch` | `Result<T, Failure>` / `match` | | linearity; recover/return semantics | LR C.1 |
| `T?` / `match` | `Option<T>` / `match` | exhaustiveness (both) | binding ownership | LR C.1 |
| `async func` / `scope` | `async fn` state machine / join set polled by the parent | | linear futures, cancellation at `await`; join on exit | LR C.1 |
| `launchParallel` | pool spawn with `'static + Send` | `Send` | `Shareable` | LR C.1 |
| `defer` | body inlined at every exit (not `Drop`) | each inlined copy's borrows | places initialised at every exit | LR C.1 |
| `cleanup` | `impl Drop` calling the method | drop order | effects contributed | LR C.1 |
| `noalloc`, effects | no representation | | whitelist (C.3); summaries | LR C.1 |
| `capture`/`record` | frame struct writes, record calls | | definite assignment | LR C.1 |
| capability | zero-sized or handle struct, private constructor | | `io` requires capability | LR C.1 |

## Unsupported shapes (C.2)

| Shape | Code | Alternative | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| loan `from` two parameters | `E-SYN-000` | return owned, or split | LR C.2, LR 7.6 |
| class storing a loan (lifetime parameter, loan or loan-carrying field other than a loan `from static`) | `E-OWN-053` | own, copy, `Shared`, or pass per call | LR C.2, LR 7.7 |
| self-referential class | `E-OWN-053` | indices, or `Shared` + `Weak` | LR C.2, LR 7.7 |
| loan stored in `Shared`/`Mutex` | `E-OWN-090` | own the value | LR C.2 |
| `fn mut` escaping into `Shared` | `E-OWN-090` | `Mutex` around the state + `fn` closure | LR C.2 |
| future holding a loan on a parallel pool | `E-ASY-003` | pass owned data | LR C.2, LR 12.7 |
| partial move | `E-OWN-040` | move the whole, or restructure | LR C.2, LR 7.2 |

A shape an earlier rule excludes keeps that rule's code (X-126); `E-OWN-090` is for shapes only the lowering
identifies (LR C.2).

## Allocation whitelist (C.3)

| Allocation-free | Allocating | LR |
|---|---|---|
| arithmetic, comparison; field and array access; trivial and inline values (`Array`, `FixedList`, `FixedMap`, bounded `Failure`); a class or record built from trivial, moved, fresh, call-returned or retained (`retain()`, `downgrade()`) values; read/exclusive loans; calls of non-`alloc` functions; `match`; `defer`; `join(a, b)`; `capture` into a bounded frame | `List`/`String`/`Map` growth; `Shared.create`; `dynamic` creation; `copy` of a heap-owning value; boxed futures of `dynamic` async calls; extended failure payloads; `launchParallel`/`launchBlocking`; every cooperative `launch` in v1 (no inline task storage, X-125) | LR C.3 |

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-OWN-040 | `move p.field` while `p` still owns the rest | move the whole binding; consume it with `let Name(field: x, …) = move p` | LR 7.2, LR C.2 |
| E-OWN-053 | lifetime parameter, or a field of a loan or loan-carrying type (not `from static`) | own the data (`String` for `StringView`), copy it, `Shared`, or pass it per call | LR 7.7, LR C.2 |
| E-OWN-090 | a shape with no lowering (loan or `fn mut` into `Shared`/`Mutex`) | own the value; `Mutex` or atomic state with a `fn` closure | LR 7.10, LR C.2 |
| E-ASY-003 | a pool launch whose future borrows or holds a non-`Shareable` value | pass owned `Shareable` data (`move`, `copy`) | LR 12.7, LR C.2 |
| E-EFF-001 | an allocating pattern in a `noalloc` body | remove the allocation (a caller-provided buffer, an inline `Array`/`FixedList`); removing the claim is an API change, never a correction (LR 11.3) | LR 11.1, LR 11.3, LR C.3 |

## Correction patterns

### E-OWN-040: partial move (LR 7.2, LR C.2)

```fortis
// reject: E-OWN-040
class Order {
  export id: Int
  export lines: List[Int]
}

test "lines" {
  let order = Order(id: 7, lines: List.of(1, 2, 3))
  let lines = move order.lines        // reject: E-OWN-040
  expect lines.count() == 3
}
```

```fortis
// accept
class Order {
  export id: Int
  export lines: List[Int]
}

test "lines" {
  let order = Order(id: 7, lines: List.of(1, 2, 3))
  let Order(id: id, lines: lines) = move order
  expect id == 7
  expect lines.count() == 3
}
```

### E-OWN-053: stored loan (LR 7.7, LR C.2)

```fortis
// reject: E-OWN-053
class Line {                          // reject: E-OWN-053
  export text: StringView
}

test "line" {
  expect 1 == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
class Line {
  export text: String
}

test "line" {
  let line = Line(text: "first")
  expect line.text == "first"
}
```

### E-OWN-090: `fn mut` into `Shared` (LR C.2)

```fortis
// reject: E-OWN-090
test "bump" {
  let mut count = 0
  let bump = fn mut[editable count]() Void {
    count = Int.saturatingAdd(count, 1)
  }
  let shared = Shared.create(move bump)     // reject: E-OWN-090
}
```

```fortis
// accept
test "bump" {
  let counter = Shared.create(AtomicInt.create(0))
  let handle = counter.retain()
  let bump = fn[move handle]() Void {
    discard handle.fetchAdd(1)
  }
  bump()
  bump()
  expect counter.load() == 2
}
```

### E-ASY-003: loan sent to a pool (LR 12.7, LR C.2)

```fortis
// reject: E-ASY-003
import fortis.host { Console }

async func total(items: ListView[Int]) Int {
  let mut sum = 0
  for x in items {
    sum = Int.saturatingAdd(sum, x)
  }
  return sum
}

async func main(console: Console) {
  let numbers = List.of(1, 2, 3)
  scope tasks {
    let t = tasks.launchParallel(total(numbers))   // reject: E-ASY-003
    let sum = await t
    console.print("${sum}")
  }
}
```

```fortis
// accept
import fortis.host { Console }

async func total(items: owned List[Int]) Int {
  let mut sum = 0
  for x in items {
    sum = Int.saturatingAdd(sum, x)
  }
  return sum
}

async func main(console: Console) {
  let numbers = List.of(1, 2, 3)
  scope tasks {
    let t = tasks.launchParallel(total(move numbers))
    let sum = await t
    console.print("${sum}")
  }
}
```

```output
6
```

### E-EFF-001: allocation in `noalloc` (LR 11.1, LR C.3)

The record is reported at the allocating statement.

```fortis
// reject: E-EFF-001
pure noalloc func grow(items: editable List[Int]) {
  items.push(1)                       // reject: E-EFF-001
}

test "grow" {
  expect 1 == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func grow(items: editable List[Int]) {
  items.push(1)
}

pure noalloc func square(n: Int<-1000..1000>) Int => n * n

test "grow" {
  let mut items: List[Int] = List.default()
  grow(editable items)
  expect items.count() == 1
  expect square(12) == 144
}
```

---
source: docs/agent/appendix-d-rules.md
---

# Rule index (LR D)

<!-- covers: LR D -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Rule index](../guide/appendix-d-rules.md). Source of truth: each LR section's rule
table; LR D for old IDs.*

Every `LANG-` rule, its section, a condensed statement and the agent page that carries its codes and correction
patterns. A diagnostic record's `rule` field names one of these IDs, or a `PROG-` or `PLAT-` ID.
The LR rule text is authoritative; the statements here are condensed (LR 0).

## LR 3-6

| Rule | LR | Statement | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| LANG-03-01 | LR 3.2 | `;` outside strings, comments, raw template regions: parse error | [03](03-lexical.md) |
| LANG-03-02 | LR 3.2 | newline termination and continuation follow the 3.2 token lists exactly | [03](03-lexical.md) |
| LANG-03-03 | LR 3.3 | identifier category from its first character | [03](03-lexical.md) |
| LANG-03-04 | LR 3.4 | keywords reserved in declaration/binding positions; allowed as method/associated-function names and after `.` | [A](appendix-a-keywords.md) |
| LANG-03-05 | LR 3.5 | literal typing per 3.5; out-of-range literal rejected at compile time | [03](03-lexical.md) |
| LANG-03-06 | LR 3.6 | interpolations evaluated once, in order; never fallible or suspending | [03](03-lexical.md) |
| LANG-04-01 | LR 4.2 | module identity = file path; modules hold only declarations and constants | [04](04-modules.md) |
| LANG-04-02 | LR 4.2 | importing executes no code | [04](04-modules.md) |
| LANG-04-03 | LR 4.3 | only `exports:` modules importable across packages | [04](04-modules.md) |
| LANG-04-04 | LR 4.1 | distinct nominal types per package version and per module | [04](04-modules.md) |
| LANG-04-05 | LR 4.5 | shadowing a visible binding rejected | [04](04-modules.md) |
| LANG-04-06 | LR 4.6 | entry = the `main` of the manifest's entry module, exported or not, one of the four heads (each optionally `recovers`); each parameter `List[String]` or a capability type, each type once, supplied by its type | [04](04-modules.md) |
| LANG-05-01 | LR 5.1 | `let` declares, and its pattern matches every value; `=` assigns only a visible mutable target | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-02 | LR 5.1 | block exit: end loans, run defers LIFO, drop locals in reverse initialisation order | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-03 | LR 5.2 | `if`/`while` conditions are `Bool` | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-04 | LR 5.3 | ranged `for` refines its index; index immutable | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-05 | LR 5.4 | non-`Void` function ends every path in `return`, `fail` or `Never` | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-06 | LR 5.6 | precedence per 5.6; mixed families without parentheses: parse error | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-07 | LR 5.7 | evaluation order per 5.7, identical on both backends | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-08 | LR 5.5, LR 12.3 | discarding a linear value rejected, except a never-polled future holding nothing linear and no exclusive loan; other non-`Void` values need `discard`, except a call statement of an `@ignorable` function | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-09 | LR 5.8 | named after positional; each parameter once; names are exported signature; a pun `x` is `x: x` | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-06-01 | LR 6.1, LR 6.9 | nominal identity survives calls, storage, serialisation, FFI | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-02 | LR 6.3 | structural refinement subtyping; interval domain exactly as listed | [06](06-types.md), [proofs](06-proofs.md) |
| LANG-06-03 | LR 6.3 | untrusted values pass `validate` before holding a refined or nominal type | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-04 | LR 6.4, LR 6.5 | integer, `Decimal`, listed float operations bit-exact across VM and native; a checked operator fails as its function, at the same operation | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-05 | LR 6.5 | float operators total, strict IEEE; float refinements rejected | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-06 | LR 6.7 | `Map`/`Set` iteration deterministic per build | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-07 | LR 6.11 | trivial and copyable sets exactly as in 6.11 | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-08 | LR 6.8 | optional, `Bool`, `Outcome` never convert into one another | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-09 | LR 6.12 | linear values consumed exactly once | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-10 | LR 6.10, LR 9.5 | coherence: implementation in the package of the interface or the type; no overlap | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-11 | LR 6.10 | type arguments unfixed by arguments and expected type: rejected | [06](06-types.md) |

## LR 7-9

| Rule | LR | Statement | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| LANG-07-01 | LR 7.5 | existing ownership-bearing place assigned/returned/captured carries `copy`/`alias`/`move`, except that returning a local `let` binding moves it; `owned`/`editable` arguments carry their marker; an unmarked `editable self` receiver or `fn mut` call checked as the marked one, rejected where the marker could not be written | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| LANG-07-02 | LR 7.6 | parameters never reassignable | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| LANG-07-03 | LR 7.10 | no inserted clones, reference counts or hidden sharing | [07](07-ownership.md), [C](appendix-c-lowering.md) |
| LANG-07-04 | LR 7.3, LR 7.4 | use after move, conflicting loans, loaned-owner use, escaping loans rejected, incl. closures, `defer`, `await`, `scope` | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| LANG-07-05 | LR 7.3 | loans lexical; aliasing invariant at every point | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| LANG-07-06 | LR 7.6, LR 7.7 | returned loans name one origin; lifetime parameter or loan-carrying field (not `from static`) rejected | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| LANG-07-07 | LR 7.9 | destruction order per 7.9 on both backends | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| LANG-07-08 | LR 7.8 | sharing explicit (`retain`); `copy` of `Shared` rejected | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| LANG-07-09 | LR 7.10 | unsupported shapes rejected, never lowered with `unsafe` or erasure | [C](appendix-c-lowering.md) |
| LANG-08-01 | LR 8.1 | parameter and success types stated (a head may leave out `Void`; a lambda's as 8.2 allows); modifiers in 8.1 order | [08](08-functions.md) |
| LANG-08-02 | LR 8.2, LR 8.3 | lambdas list captures (no brackets when none) and declare kind; stronger-kind body rejected | [08](08-functions.md) |
| LANG-08-03 | LR 8.3 | names outside the capture list inaccessible | [08](08-functions.md) |
| LANG-08-04 | LR 8.4 | callable assignability per 8.4; no boxing without `dynamic fn` | [08](08-functions.md) |
| LANG-09-01 | LR 9.1 | no inheritance, runtime member lookup, reflection-based construction | [09](09-classes.md) |
| LANG-09-02 | LR 9.2 | generated constructor only where every field is visible | [09](09-classes.md) |
| LANG-09-03 | LR 9.5 | implementations never strengthen preconditions or weaken guarantees; coherence | [09](09-classes.md) |
| LANG-09-04 | LR 9.6 | mixins require methods only, add no state; conflicts rejected | [09](09-classes.md) |
| LANG-09-05 | LR 9.8 | closed-type `match` exhaustive without `otherwise`; each missing variant named; or-pattern alternatives count, bind nothing, take no guard | [09](09-classes.md) |
| LANG-09-06 | LR 9.8 | pattern binding ownership per 9.8 | [09](09-classes.md) |

## LR 10-14

| Rule | LR | Statement | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| LANG-10-01 | LR 10.1, LR 10.2 | outcomes wrapped until consumed by a 10.2 operation | [10](10-outcomes.md) |
| LANG-10-02 | LR 10.7 | obligations survive collections, fields, closures; dropping rejected | [10](10-outcomes.md) |
| LANG-10-03 | LR 10.6 | reported failure unreachable afterwards; `annotate` keeps one obligation | [10](10-outcomes.md) |
| LANG-10-04 | LR 10.3 | `noalloc try` uses the bounded failure representation | [10](10-outcomes.md) |
| LANG-10-05 | LR 10.4 | `recover` without a prior `report` adds `recovers` | [10](10-outcomes.md) |
| LANG-10-06 | LR 10.8 | defects follow the 10.8 taxonomy; never catchable | [10](10-outcomes.md) |
| LANG-11-01 | LR 11.1, LR 11.3 | exactly eight effects; transitive fixed-point summaries | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-11-02 | LR 11.1, LR 11.3 | fresh-storage and own-`editable`-parameter writes are not `mutate`; captures, guards, atomics are | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-11-03 | LR 11.4 | `noalloc` against the whitelist for the target and telemetry plan | [11](11-effects.md), [C](appendix-c-lowering.md) |
| LANG-11-04 | LR 11.3 | trusted summaries labelled `trusted`, never `proved` | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-11-05 | LR 11.3 | `async`/`try`/`recovers` written; only written `pure`/`noalloc` cross modules; weakening exported modifiers reported | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-11-06 | LR 11.5 | contracts are conjunctions of 11.5 elements; configuration adds none | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-11-07 | LR 11.6 | `io` (except `report` and the `log` statements) needs an `Authority`; only the entry `main` receives capabilities, as parameters, or creates them once with `Host.capabilities()` when it declares none; every other use of `Host.capabilities` and every reference to the entry `main` rejected | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-11-08 | LR 11.5, LR 11.8 | contracts in modifier position, no arguments; `@` for aspects only | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-11-09 | LR 11.8 | aspects have only the 11.8 parts, elaborate before checking, pass every check | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-12-01 | LR 12.1 | `defer` checked at every exit; cannot alter the outcome; named places initialised at every exit | [12](12-async.md) |
| LANG-12-02 | LR 12.1 | failures in `defer` consumed there; never replace the primary outcome | [12](12-async.md) |
| LANG-12-03 | LR 12.3, LR 12.4 | `Future`/`Task` linear; pending future never destroyed; cancellation only at cancellation points | [12](12-async.md) |
| LANG-12-04 | LR 12.5 | a scope joins or cancels every task before its block exits | [12](12-async.md) |
| LANG-12-05 | LR 12.5, LR 12.7 | only `Shareable` environments cross pools; loans cross only cooperative `launch` | [12](12-async.md) |
| LANG-12-06 | LR 12.3, LR 12.7 | no `MutexGuard` live across `await` | [12](12-async.md) |
| LANG-13-01 | LR 13 | `capture` snapshots a pure, infallible expression | [13](13-observation.md) |
| LANG-13-02 | LR 13 | required fields assigned exactly once per applicable exit; loops and doubles rejected | [13](13-observation.md) |
| LANG-13-03 | LR 13 | frames bounded by the schema; truncation or omission recorded | [13](13-observation.md) |
| LANG-13-04 | LR 13 | each `log.info`/`log.warn`/`log.error` writes exactly one `log` record to the diagnostic plane, never standard output, the same on every backend; needs no `Authority`; has the `io` effect | [13](13-observation.md) |
| LANG-14-01 | LR 14 | table rows bound with `as` | [14](14-tests.md) |
| LANG-14-02 | LR 14 | `expect` takes `Bool`, records typed evidence | [14](14-tests.md) |
| LANG-14-03 | LR 14, LR 6.4 | in `test`/`property` bodies a fallible call nothing else consumes (`or`, `catch`, `match`, a `let` later consumed as an outcome or annotated `Outcome[…]`), and unproved `Int` arithmetic, behave as followed by `or fail`; outside them nothing changes | [14](14-tests.md) |
