# Glossary (agent mode)

<!-- covers: LR E -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Glossary](../guide/glossary.md).*

One meaning per term; where a word has two meanings both rows are listed. A bundle of packages is a kit.
The Language Reference's glossary is LR E; this page adds the in-language terms.

## System

| Term | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| package | unit of distribution, versioning, visibility: `project.yaml`, lockfile, `src/`; two versions are two packages | LR 4.1 |
| module | one `.ft` file under `src/`; name = path below `src/` with `.` separators; declarations and constants only | LR 4.2 |
| kit | named, versioned bundle of packages shipped with the distribution; extends Fortis only by libraries, aspects, heads, embedding bindings, verifiers; never changes core semantics | LR 16 |
| compatibility set | the standard packages at the versions tested together; a standard dependency names the set's version | LR 4.1 |
| toolchain component | daemon, LSP, SDK generators: tools, not kits | LR 16 |
| backend | interpreter (`fortis run`, the reference), development VM (`fortisc vm`), native (`fortis build`); must agree | LR 1 |
| build mode | `dev` (VM), `native-dev`, `release`; optimisation and debug settings belong to a mode | LR 1 |
| lint level | baseline (an unused import warns) or strict (it is an error) | LR 4.3 |
| target feature set | which standard modules exist for a target (`core`, `alloc`, `host`, `async`, `web`, `browser`) | LR 11.6 |

## Declarations

| Term | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| head (declaration head) | reserved keyword introducing a schema-validated declaration elaborated to core declarations before type checking; owner: the core (`observation`, LR 13), developer tooling (`explore`, LR E), or a kit (the rest) | LR 16, LR 13, LR E |
| elaboration | rewriting a head, or a function with aspects, into core declarations before ownership and effect checking | LR 16, LR 11.8 |
| extension slot | head block; `inject` member; aspect application; `cases` table: the only four | LR 16 |
| raw template region | text of `view { … }` in a head body, handed unlexed to the Web UI kit | LR 16 |
| aspect | `@name(args)` behaviour around a function: `needs`, `before`, `after`, `on failure`, `metadata`; adds | LR 11.8 |
| contract | named conjunction of modifiers, forbidden effects, required or excluded authorities; subtracts | LR 11.5 |
| mixin | methods applied with `with`; requires methods, adds no state | LR 9.6 |
| newtype | `type Name = Repr`; nominal, private representation | LR 6.9 |
| refinement | predicate in `<…>` on a built-in type | LR 6.3 |
| binding (name) | name introduced by `let`, `let mut`, a parameter, a pattern or a capture | LR 5.1, LR 7.2 |
| binding (embedded language) | versioned package giving a language fenced blocks via the embedding protocol; meaning compiler-fixed, checking a verifier (SP-23, not yet in the LR) | [Embedded languages](embedded-languages.md) |
| verifier | stricter-only package: reads the checked program, returns records never code; pure, deterministic, bounded, no capability | [Embedded languages](embedded-languages.md) |

## Ownership

| Term | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| place | binding; field path rooted in a binding or `self`; `Array` element with a literal index | LR 7.2 |
| owner | binding holding a value until it is moved out | LR 7.2 |
| loan | `alias` (read) or `editable` (exclusive) reference to a place; lexical | LR 7.3 |
| child loan | a loan taken through a loan-holding binding, recorded against the owner | LR 7.3 |
| marker | `copy`, `alias`, `move`, `editable` before a place; left out where the declaration already shows it (an `editable self` receiver on a `let mut` root, `return local`) | LR 7.5 |
| loan-carrying value | standard views and cursors; store a read loan; owned by their binding | LR 7.7 |
| trivial | duplicated implicitly, never marked | LR 6.11 |
| copyable | supports `copy` | LR 6.11 |
| linear | consumed exactly once on every path | LR 6.12 |
| shareable | may cross `launchParallel` / `launchBlocking` | LR 12.7 |

## Failures, effects, authority

| Term | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| outcome | `Outcome[T]` from a `try` function; linear | LR 10.1 |
| checked region | `Int` arithmetic as the left operand of `or fail`/`or recover`/`catch`; an unproved operator in it is the checked operation | LR 6.4 |
| failure | `Failure`: code, payload, origin, cause chain; linear | LR 10.3 |
| obligation | the duty to consume a linear value | LR 7.1, LR 10.1 |
| defect | broken-assumption condition (stack, memory, trusted contract, runtime invariant); never caught | LR 10.8 |
| effect | one of `alloc`, `io`, `mutate`, `nondet`, `suspend`, `block`, `fail`, `recovers` | LR 11.1 |
| effect summary | a function's effect subset, computed transitively | LR 11.1, LR 11.3 |
| write footprint | `editable` parameters a function writes through | LR 11.3 |
| fresh storage | created in this activation, not yet reachable from a parameter, capture or `self` | LR 11.1 |
| authority | value implementing `Authority`; required for `io` | LR 11.6 |
| capability | process-wide authority (ten types), supplied to the entry `main`'s parameters by type | LR 11.6, LR 4.6 |
| per-activation authority | minted by a kit adapter from a capability for one unit of work | LR 11.6 |
| trusted | bodiless standard intrinsic; claims reported as trusted, never proved | LR 11.3 |

## Concurrency and observation

| Term | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| scope | `scope name { … }`: owns tasks; joins or cancels them before exit | LR 12.5 |
| task | `Task[T]` from a launch; linear | LR 12.5 |
| cancellation point | `await`; on the pools also `checkpoint()` | LR 12.4 |
| observation schema | `observation` declaration of typed frame fields | LR 13 |
| observation frame | one activation's captured fields | LR 13 |
| event | one `record` execution | LR 13 |
| task reporter | diagnostic-plane sink for reports, logs and frames | LR 15 |
| log record | one `log.info`/`log.warn`/`log.error` execution: level, message, function; standard error, never standard output | LR 13 |
| diagnostic plane | output channel nothing can read back | LR 11.7 |
| record (tool output) | schema-valid object; text on a terminal, JSON line otherwise | [records](records.md) |

source: docs/agent/library.md

# The core library

<!-- covers: LR 15 -->
*Both modes. Generated by `conformance/tools/libref.py` from the declarations of `library/fortis`; do not edit.
Source of truth: LR 15 for the inventory, and each declaration's own contract.*

> Preview: the core runtime inventory (LR 15) arrives in v0.4.

Every public declaration of the seven core modules (LR 15): each exported declaration, every member of an
exported interface (whose members share its visibility, LR 4.4) and every variant of an exported enum, with its
signature as the library declares it and the contract its documentation comment states. The check counts these
against the module sources independently of this page. A `trusted` operation is implemented by the toolchain, and
its comment is its review record (LR 11.3). `fortis.prelude` is imported into every module; the other modules
need an `import` (LR 4.3). What is not listed here does not exist in Language 1.0's core library; the gaps
against the Language Reference are recorded as D-58.

## `fortis.prelude`

Imported into every module: the built-in types, the optional and outcome operations, the built-in interfaces (LR 4.3, LR 6.2, LR 6.10).

### `class Void`

### `class Never`

### `class Bool`

### `class Int`

| Declaration | Contract |
|---|---|
| `trusted pure try func add(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | checked 64-bit two's-complement addition; fails `numeric.overflow` outside [-2^63, 2^63-1]; O(1), no allocation |
| `trusted pure try func sub(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | checked subtraction; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1), no allocation |
| `trusted pure try func mul(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | checked multiplication; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1), no allocation |
| `trusted pure try func div(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | truncating division; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` when b = 0 and `numeric.overflow` for -2^63 / -1; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func rem(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | remainder with the sign of a; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` when b = 0; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func shiftLeft(a: Int, bits: Int) Int` | a * 2^bits; fails `numeric.shift_range` unless 0 <= bits < 64 and `numeric.overflow` when the result is out of range; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func wrappingAdd(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | addition modulo 2^64 into [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func wrappingSub(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | subtraction modulo 2^64; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func wrappingMul(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | multiplication modulo 2^64; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func saturatingAdd(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | addition clamped to [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func saturatingSub(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | subtraction clamped to [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func saturatingMul(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | multiplication clamped to [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func validate(value: Int) Int` | the value when it lies in the refinement of the receiver type; fails `refinement.out_of_range` otherwise; O(1) |

### `class Float`

| Declaration | Contract |
|---|---|
| `trusted pure func sqrt(x: Float) Float` | IEEE 754 binary64 correctly rounded square root; NaN for negative input; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func totalOrder(x: Float) Int64` | the IEEE 754 totalOrder key of x as a signed 64-bit integer; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func bitsEqual(a: Float, b: Float) Bool` | true exactly when a and b have the same 64-bit pattern; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func isNaN(x: Float) Bool` | true exactly for NaN; O(1) |

| Declaration | Contract |
|---|---|
| `trusted pure func sqrt(x: Float32) Float32` | IEEE 754 binary32 correctly rounded square root; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func isNaN(x: Float32) Bool` | true exactly for NaN; O(1) |

### `enum RoundingMode`

Variants: `HalfEven`, `HalfAwayFromZero`, `TowardZero`, `AwayFromZero`.

### `class Decimal`

| Declaration | Contract |
|---|---|
| `trusted pure try func add(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | the sum at the larger operand scale, rounded half to even when it needs more than 96 coefficient bits; fails `numeric.overflow` when the integer part does not fit (6.4); O(digits) |
| `trusted pure try func sub(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | the difference at the larger operand scale, rounded half to even when needed; fails `numeric.overflow` (6.4); O(digits) |
| `trusted pure try func mul(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | the product at the sum of the scales, rounded half to even above 28 fractional digits or 96 coefficient bits; fails `numeric.overflow` (6.4); O(digits^2) |
| `trusted pure try func div(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | the quotient at the largest scale that fits, rounded half to even; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` and `numeric.overflow` (6.4); O(digits^2) |
| `trusted pure try func rem(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | the remainder with the sign of the dividend at the larger operand scale; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` (6.4); O(digits^2) |
| `trusted pure func round(value: Decimal, scale: Int<0..28>, mode: RoundingMode) Decimal` | value rounded to scale by mode; total; O(digits) |
| `trusted pure try func fromFloat(x: Float, scale: Int<0..28>, mode: RoundingMode) Decimal` | the binary value of x rounded to scale by mode; fails `numeric.overflow` for a non-finite x or an integer part that does not fit (6.4); O(digits) |
| `trusted pure func scale(self) Int<0..28>` | the number of fractional digits; O(1) |

### `class BigInt`

### `class String`

|---|---|

| `pure func empty() String` | — |
| `trusted pure func scalarCount(self) Int` | the number of Unicode scalar values; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func byteCount(self) Int` | the UTF-8 length in bytes; O(1) |

### `class StringView`

| Declaration | Contract |
|---|---|
| `trusted pure func scalarCount(self) Int` | the number of Unicode scalar values; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func byteCount(self) Int` | the UTF-8 length in bytes; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func slice(self, start: Int, end: Int) StringView` | the scalars [start, end) as a view of the same owner; fails `text.slice_bounds` unless 0 <= start <= end <= scalarCount; O(n) in bytes, no allocation |
| `trusted pure try func scalarAt(self, index: Int) Scalar` | the scalar at index; fails `text.index` past the end; O(n) in bytes |

### `class List[T]`

| Declaration | Contract |
|---|---|
| `trusted pure func default() List[T]` | an empty list with no allocation until the first push; O(1) |

| `trusted func push(editable self, item: owned T)` | appends item; amortised O(1) (capacity doubles), worst case O(n) for the growth step |
| `trusted func pop(editable self) T?` | removes and returns the last element, null when empty; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func get(self, index: Int) (alias T from self)?` | a read loan of the element at index, null outside [0, count); O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func at(self, index: Int) T` | the element at index; fails `collection.index` outside [0, count); O(1) |
| `trusted try func set(editable self, index: Int, value: owned T)` | replaces the element at index, dropping the old value; fails `collection.index`; O(1) |
| `pure func isEmpty(self) Bool` | — |
| `pure func first(self) (alias T from self)?` | — |
| `pure func reversed(self) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | — |
| `pure func concat(self, other: ListView[T]) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | — |
| `pure func countWhere(self, keep: pure fn(T) Bool) Int` | — |
| `pure func map[U](self, f: pure fn(T) U) List[U]` | — |
| `pure func filter(self, keep: pure fn(T) Bool) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | — |
| `trusted pure func iterate(self) ListCursor[T] from self` | a cursor over read loans of the elements in order; O(1) to create, O(1) per step |
| `trusted func consumeEach(owned self, visit: fn mut(owned T) Void)` | consumes the list (10.7): no early exit, so no element is left unvisited; an empty list makes no calls intrinsic: calls visit once per element in order, transferring each element out; O(n) plus the callback per element |

### `class Mutex[T]`

| Declaration | Contract |
|---|---|
| `trusted pure func create(value: owned T) Mutex[T]` | a mutex owning value; O(1) |
| `trusted async try func lock(self) MutexGuard[T] from self` | an exclusive guard over the value, released when the guard is dropped, suspending until the lock is free; fails `concurrency.poisoned` if a holder was terminated by a defect (unreachable on the interpreter, where a defect ends the program) |
| `trusted try func lockBlocking(self) MutexGuard[T] from self` | an exclusive guard over the value, released when the guard is dropped, blocking the thread until free (the `block` effect); fails `concurrency.poisoned` |

### `class MutexGuard[T]`

| Declaration | Contract |
|---|---|
| `trusted pure func get(self) T where T implements Copyable` | a copy of the protected value, read through the exclusive guard (12.7); allocates when the value owns heap storage |
| `trusted func set(self, value: owned T)` | replaces the protected value with value and drops the old one; a write to storage shared between tasks (`mutate`, 11.1) |
| `trusted func replace(self, value: owned T) T` | replaces the protected value with value and returns the old one, which the caller now owns; a write to storage shared between tasks (`mutate`, 11.1) |

### Functions and aspects

|---|---|

| `trusted func checkpoint()` | a cancellation point for parallel and blocking tasks (12.4); no effect in cooperative tasks |
| `trusted func injectDefect(kind: StringView) Never` | the conformance corpus's fault-injection hook (LR 10.8); not part of the language |
| `aspect observe(schema: ObservationSchema)` | — |
| `aspect ignorable()` | the core aspect `@ignorable` (5.5, 11.8; X-345): callers may drop the function's non-linear result without `discard` |

### `class Secret[T]`

### `class SecretAccess implements Authority`

### `class FileSystem implements Authority`

| Declaration | Contract |
|---|---|
| `trusted try func readText(self, path: Path) String` | the UTF-8 contents of path below this root; fails `fs.outside_root` when the path is absolute or escapes the root, `fs.not_found`, `fs.not_a_file` or `fs.invalid_text`. Development adapter: the root is a fresh empty temporary directory per run, or FORTIS_DEV_ROOT when set; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1) |
| `trusted try func writeAll(self, path: Path, text: StringView)` | replaces the contents of path with text, creating the file; fails `fs.outside_root` or `fs.not_found` (missing parent directory); blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1) |
| `trusted try func readAll(self, path: Path) Bytes` | the bytes of path; fails `fs.outside_root`, `fs.not_found` or `fs.not_a_file`; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1) |
| `trusted try func open(self, path: Path) File` | an open file for reading; fails `fs.outside_root` or `fs.not_found`; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1) |
| `trusted try func create(self, path: Path) File` | an open file for writing, created or truncated; fails `fs.outside_root` or `fs.not_found`; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1) |
| `trusted func subtree(self, path: Path) FileSystem` | a FileSystem confined below path; a path that escapes this root yields a confinement that refuses every operation with `fs.outside_root` (attenuation never widens) |

### `class File`

| Declaration | Contract |
|---|---|
| `trusted try func readAll(editable self) Bytes` | the remaining bytes of a file opened for reading; fails `fs.closed` after close and `fs.wrong_mode` on a file opened for writing; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1) |
| `trusted try func writeAll(editable self, data: BytesView)` | appends data to a file opened for writing; fails `fs.closed` after close and `fs.wrong_mode` on a file opened for reading; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1) |
| `trusted func close(editable self)` | closes the file; closing twice has no effect; dropping an open file closes it |

| Declaration | Contract |
|---|---|
| `trusted try func resolve(self, host: StringView) String` | the address of host. Development adapter: offline; `localhost` resolves to 127.0.0.1 and every other host fails `network.unreachable`; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1) |

### `class Clock implements Authority`

| Declaration | Contract |
|---|---|

| `trusted func now(self) Timestamp` | the current instant in UTC (nondet). Development adapter: the system clock; a frozen clock returns its instant |
| `trusted func frozen(self, instant: Timestamp) Clock` | a clock whose now() is always instant (for tests and replay) |
| `trusted try func elapsedSince(self, earlier: Timestamp) Duration` | now() minus earlier; fails `clock.future` when earlier is after now() |

| Declaration | Contract |
|---|---|
| `trusted func capabilities() Capabilities` | the ten process-wide capabilities, created by one direct call in the entry main (11.6): every other use is rejected statically (E-EFF-010), and a second creation stops the run with the runtime-invariant defect (10.8) (E-EFF-010: LR 4.6) |

### Functions and aspects

| Declaration | Contract |
|---|---|
| `trusted func reveal[T](secret: Secret[T], cap: SecretAccess) T` | the secret value (a copy); requires the SecretAccess capability (15); O(size) |

---
source: skills/fortis-code/SKILL.md
---


# Working with Fortis code

Fortis source is read through the language's tools, never through text tools. `fortis view` sees the code as the
compiler does: it knows which `{` opens a body, which word is a keyword used as a name, and where a statement ends.
`grep` and `cat` do not, and they miss what matters in Fortis (parameter modes, effects, failure disposition).

## Read: `fortis view`

Run from the repository root (`bin/fortis`, or `fortis` when installed). It never writes.

| To | Run |
|---|---|
| read a file, a directory or a glob | `fortis view src/orders.ft`, `fortis view src`, `fortis view 'src/**/*.ft'` |
| list declarations (kind, name, modifiers, contracts, aspects, documentation, head) | `fortis view --decls src` |
| read one declaration whole | `fortis view --symbol process src` or `--symbol Order.total` |
| answer a structural question | `fortis view --query async-try src` |
| list the queries | `fortis view --queries` |

The queries answer what text search cannot: `async`, `try`, `async-try`, `pure`, `noalloc`, `trusted`,
`recovers`, `editable-params`, `owned-params`, `or-fail`, `or-recover`, `catch`, `fail`, `return`, `defer`,
`scope`, `capture`, `expect`, `move`, `lambda`, `tests`, `errors`, `classes`, and `aspect:NAME` (`aspect:get` finds
every `@get` route). Each answer is `file:line:column: name`.

Add `--json` for machine-readable output: one JSON object per line, with `kind` one of `line`, `declaration`,
`symbol`, `match` or `query`. JSON is the primary form, and the terminal highlighting is derived from it.

## Check: `fortis check --format json`

`fortis check FILE.ft` or `fortis check DIR` runs every static check: syntax, names, types, ownership,
obligations, effects, contracts and aspects. With `--format json`, each finding is one record per line. A record
has `code` (for example `E-OWN-001`, LR 7.5), `class`, `rule` (the Language Reference rule it enforces), `file`, `line`,
`column`, `message`, `status` (`violated`, `unproved` or `unknown`) and class-specific `fields`; the schema is
`reference/schemas/diagnostic.schema.json`. A record with a `correction` carries the exact edit that fixes it.
Read the record before changing code: `unproved` means the checker could not prove a refinement, not that the
code is wrong. Run `fortis test FILE.ft` or `fortis test DIR` for the tests.

## Format: `fortis fmt`

`fortis fmt --check PATH` lists the files whose layout is not canonical, and `fortis fmt --write PATH` fixes them.
Formatting changes only whitespace: it refuses, and writes nothing, if a result would not be the same program.

## Rules, codes and corrections: the agent mode

The documentation's agent mode, `docs/agent/` (start at `docs/agent/README.md`), states every rule of the Language
Reference by ID, one page per section, with the diagnostic codes of that section and a rejected-then-accepted
pair of programs for each correction. Every example there is checked and run by the real toolchain.

| To | Read |
|---|---|
| fix a record | `docs/agent/codes.md`: the code's class, rule, Language Reference section, trigger and correction, with a link to its correction pair |
| read a record's fields | `docs/agent/records.md`: the diagnostic record and every runtime record (failures, tests, observation, builds) |
| know the rules of a construct | `docs/agent/NN-*.md`: the rules of Language Reference section NN by ID |
| check a rule's exact words | `docs/Fortis_Language_Reference.md`, the source of truth: `LR 7.3` is its section 7.3 |

A correction pattern shows the smallest change that satisfies the rule. Apply the one whose trigger matches the
record's `code` and `fields`; when the record has a `correction`, apply that edit. Never apply a pattern that
weakens a claim (`pure`, `noalloc`, a contract) or discards an outcome to silence a record.

## Prohibitions

- Do not read `.ft` files with `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed -n` or `less`, and do not search them with `grep` or
  `rg`. Use `fortis view`.
- Do not weaken a contract, remove an `expect`, or change an expected output to make a check or test pass.
- Do not hand-format Fortis code; run `fortis fmt --write`.
